docs.title: Bosar
docs.text: Open, install-and-run SAR interferometry for Windows and macOS. Two-pass DInSAR, coherence and coherence-change detection, amplitude change, PS-InSAR and PS/DS time series, SBAS, offset tracking — on Sentinel-1 (native TOPS processing), ALOS-1 PALSAR, ENVISAT ASAR, ERS-1/2 and the first NISAR granules — with automatic data, orbit, DEM and weather-model fetching, a desktop GUI, optional CUDA acceleration and a full UTC-stamped processing log.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Platform Download Notes Windows 10/11 x64 bosar-<version>-win-x64-setup.exe from Releases per-user, no administrator rights; the GUI in the Start menu, bosar on the command line macOS 12+ (Apple silicon) bosar-<version>-mac-arm64.dmg unsigned: right-click → Open once (the README in the image) GPU bosar gpu install after installing CuPy and the CUDA 12 runtime as a plug-in (about 1.5 GB) on an NVIDIA machine

The installers carry everything else: Python, the numerical stack, GDAL/PROJ, the SNAPHU unwrapper (built without the CS2 solver), the licence texts. See Install.

docs.title: Where to go
docs.text:
• Walkthrough (中文) — every step from an empty folder to a validated time series, with the commands.
  • Feature tour — every module, screenshots from the real application.
  • Numerical conventions, held everywhere: positive LOS = toward the sensor; metres, seconds, radians; dates in UTC.
  • Errors, warnings and preflight codes — what a code means and what to do.
  • Sensor download plan — every sensor the readers could handle, where its data come from, what is verified.
  • Licensing — free for non-commercial use (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0); commercial licences from the author; the third-party notices.

(2014) Nezahualcóyotl −223 mm/yr LOS, the airport −192, the volcanic hill −4 ± 3; USABLE in the deforming-area mode ENVISAT ASAR, ERS-1/2 Mexico City the ESA pairs' documented fringe rate real pairs form, unwrap and geocode NISAR L-band track 33 (provisional RSLC, October 2026) the granule's own metadata opens; a pair follows when a repeat exists

Maintainer: Jiashu Hu — oswaldmurphy66@gmail.com.

docs.title: Error, warning and preflight codes
docs.text:
Every failure in Bosar answers five questions on one screen: what (message + code), where (project → run → step → function → tile window → file/dataset → parameter), why (expected vs actual), next (hint + link to this page) and where to look (run-log path + record #seq).

Codes are stable across versions: once a code is published here it is never reused for a different meaning. tests/test_errors_catalogue.py keeps this file, src/bosar/errors.py, the warning and preflight registries and the exit-code table in sync.

docs.title: How a code appears
docs.text: Place Form Exception text window_coherence(): argument 'cpx_sec' has shape (512, 500), expected (512, 512) [E301] Run log (JSONL) step_failed record → error.code; warning records → code; every preflight check → code Human mirror (.log) #000057 … ERROR step_failed step=dummy_001 code=E301 ShapeError … CLI header line, WHERE table, HINT line, → docs/ERRORS.md#e301 project.json steps[].error = {type, code, msg, where, hint, log_seq} Run report (logs/run_<id>.md) section ## Failure — E301 ShapeError (record #57)

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Exit Meaning Error codes 0 success — 1 unexpected error outside a step E000, E001 2 usage error (click) or invalid CLI parameter / unknown step kind E101, E102 3 preflight blocked the run E701 4 step failed; the failure record was written E801, E802 5 project, configuration or input file error before the run started E103, E104, E105, E107, E200, E201, E203, E204, E205 130 cancelled (Ctrl-C); record written, status cancelled E803

docs.title: Families
docs.text:
E0xx internal · E1xx configuration / project file · E2xx inputs · E3xx array / kernel entry · E4xx backend / memory · E5xx external tools · E6xx storage · E7xx preflight · E8xx runner · E9xx numerical · Wxxx warnings (same hundreds) · Pgnn preflight checks (g = group).

Foreign exceptions are classified by errors.classify() in this order: package error → Windows winerror (206 → E604, 3/2 → E201, 5 → E602, 32 → E605, 112 → E603) → errno (ENOSPC → E603, ENAMETOOLONG → E604, EACCES/EPERM → E602) → exception module (pydantic → E101, cupy → E401/E402/E403, numpy.linalg → E901, subprocess → E501/E503) → MemoryError → E404 → KeyboardInterrupt → E803 → builtin FileNotFoundError → E201, PermissionError → E602 → E000. Python folds WinError 206 and 3 into FileNotFoundError and 5 and 32 into PermissionError, and the strerror text is localised, which is why the number is checked first.

docs.title: E000 BosarError
docs.text: Raised by: the base class, and the code given to any foreign exception that no rule matches. Meaning: unclassified failure. Hint: re-run with -v; attach the run log when reporting.

docs.title: E001 InternalError
docs.text: Raised by: library code in place of a bare assert. Meaning: an invariant the package guarantees was violated — a bug.

docs.title: E100 ConfigError
docs.text: Family base for configuration and project-file problems.

docs.title: E101 ParamError
docs.text: Raised by: step parameter validation (pydantic) and CLI option parsing. Meaning: one parameter is wrong; where.param is the dotted field path, param.expected the validator message, extra.errors the full list. Guards against unit mistakes. Also raised by the ALOS-1 / ALOS-2 PALSAR L1.1 reader (data/ceos_alos.py) for several L1.1 products in one folder or zip (two products extracted into one folder, or a zip holding two): the members of different products are never mixed, so the folder or zip itself is refused (where.param = path, the message lists the products); name one of the product's files (its LED- or IMG- file), which opens that product, or extract every product into a folder of its own. Also raised by pipeline stripmap-coregister (without --force) when its step - stripmap_coregister_<tag>, stripmap_coregister_native without --tag - is already done at the current step version with its products on disk but was recorded with other products, another reader, another crop window or (only when --pol is given) another polarisation: the Runner would skip such a step (W101) and the command would import the old stack again, under a new --id too, so it refuses instead. where.param names the first differing parameter with its recorded (expected) and requested (actual) value, extra.changed lists all of them; --tag <name> keeps both results (step stripmap_coregister_<name>), --force re-runs the step with the new parameters. The same parameters pass (the step is skipped and its stack re-imported). The stripmap_coregister step itself raises it when the opened scenes do not share one polarisation (where.param = products, the message names every date with its polarisation: a stack is coregistered in one polarisation - list products of one polarisation, or name one that every product holds with --pol), and when --pol names a polarisation that the scene of a single-polarisation reader does not hold (where.param = pol).

docs.title: E102 UnknownStepError
docs.text: Raised by: pipeline.registry.get_step. Meaning: the step kind is not registered; the message lists the known kinds.

docs.title: E103 ProjectFileError
docs.text: Raised by: project.store and Project.step(). Meaning: project directory or step id problem (e.g. unknown step id, listing the known ids).

docs.title: E104 ProjectCorruptError
docs.text: Raised by: project.store.load_project. Meaning: project.json is not valid JSON; extra.line/column/snippet locate the damage; restore from project.json.bak.

docs.title: E105 ProjectSchemaError
docs.text: Raised by: project.store.load_project. Meaning: the file does not match the schema (every failing field is listed) or its schema_version is newer than the software.

docs.title: E107 DependencyError
docs.text: Raised by: the Runner while resolving requires. Meaning: a required product kind is not available from a done step.

docs.title: E310 ChainUndeclaredError
docs.text: Raised by: the Runner before a time-series step (psds_link, psds_pairs, pair_batch, closure, unw_correct, sbas_invert, ts_correct, psi_classic) in a storage_mode=minimal project that no declared plan names. Meaning: the step belongs to a multi-command chain whose intermediates minimal storage would collect too early. Remedy: bosar project new --storage-mode full, or the chain command (sbas prep, pipeline sbas | psds | psi), which declares its steps.

docs.title: E200 InputError
docs.text: Family base for input problems.

docs.title: E201 MissingInputError
docs.text: Raised by: the Runner, core._check.check_path, readers. Meaning: a file or directory named in WHERE does not exist.

docs.title: E203 UnreadableInputError
docs.text: Raised by: data.raster (rasterio/GDAL failures). Meaning: the file exists but cannot be read; the GDAL message is the cause.

docs.title: E204 ImplausibleMetadataError
docs.text: Raised by: data.model.check_plausible at every reader exit when a parsed value is outside the physical range: wavelength ∉ [0.02, 0.35] m (unit slips: SNAP MHz, GAMMA GHz), incidence ∉ [15°, 65°], slant range ∉ [500, 1500] km, |B⊥| ≥ 5 km, or a scene shape that differs from the stack geometry. WHERE names the file, the field, the expected range and the actual value. Also raised by the ENVISAT / ERS reader (data/asar.py) when a precise orbit file is more than 1 km from the product's own state vectors at mid scene - not this product's orbit (see W223) - and by the ALOS reader for an ALOS-2 observation-mode code it does not know.

docs.title: E205 MetadataError
docs.text: Raised by: readers. Meaning: a required metadata key is absent (where.dataset names the key). Guards against metadata unit and sign traps. Since: v0.1.0 (class), raised from v0.1.0. Also raised by the ALOS PALSAR L1.1 reader (data/ceos_alos.py) for an ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 product it does not serve, named by its product id: a processing level other than 1.1 (where.param = product_level), a spotlight (SBS) or ScanSAR (WBS / WBD / WWS / WWD / VBS / VBD) product, and a product with one image file per scan whatever its product id says (where.param = mode). The message names the mode and its kind; these are not stripmap scenes, and the hint lists the stripmap modes the reader takes (UBS / UBD, HBS / HBD / HBQ, FBS / FBD / FBQ). An observation-mode code the reader does not know at all is E204.

docs.title: E300 ArrayError
docs.text: Family base for kernel-entry checks (core._check).

docs.title: E301 ShapeError
docs.text: Raised by: check_array, check_shapes_match, apply_tiled. Meaning: the named argument has the wrong shape; the message names the partner argument it must match.

docs.title: E302 DTypeError
docs.text: Raised by: check_array, data.raster.RasterWriter. Meaning: wrong dtype (complex64 for phasors, float32 for phase/coherence — np.angle on a float array is silent).

docs.title: E303 NDimError
docs.text: Raised by: check_array. Meaning: wrong number of dimensions.

docs.title: E304 ValueRangeError
docs.text: Raised by: check_array(finite=True, min_value, max_value), check_scalar. Meaning: non-finite values or a value outside the allowed range/choices.

docs.title: E305 EmptyArrayError
docs.text: Raised by: check_array, data.raster.array_stats consumers. Meaning: zero-size array or no valid pixel.

docs.title: E306 WindowSpecError
docs.text: Raised by: core.tiling.Tiler, check_pair. Meaning: invalid (rows, cols) tile/halo/window.

docs.title: E400 BackendError
docs.text: Family base for CPU/GPU backend problems.

docs.title: E401 GpuOutOfMemoryError
docs.text: Raised by: classification of CuPy OutOfMemoryError (and apply_tiled). Meaning: the GPU allocation failed; the hint carries the current tile and free memory.

docs.title: E402 KernelCompileError
docs.text: Raised by: classification of CuPy CompileException. Meaning: NVRTC could not compile a kernel — usually the CUDA headers are missing (pip install "cupy-cuda12x[ctk]").

docs.title: E403 CudaRuntimeError
docs.text: Raised by: classification of CuPy runtime/driver errors. Meaning: driver/runtime mismatch or device error.

docs.title: E404 HostOutOfMemoryError
docs.text: Raised by: classification of MemoryError (host). Meaning: RAM allocation failed; retry with a smaller tile.

docs.title: E500 ExternalToolError
docs.text: Family base for subprocess tools (SNAPHU).

docs.title: E502 ToolNotFoundError
docs.text: Raised by: binary discovery (preflight binaries). Meaning: no usable binary found in the discovery order BOSAR_<NAME>_EXE → bundled → PATH → package → fallback.

docs.title: E510 SnapNotFoundError
docs.text: Raised by: the SNAP bridge (external/snap) and preflight P402 when no gpt is found (BOSAR_SNAP_GPT → PATH → typical installs).

docs.title: E511 SnapRunError
docs.text: Raised by: external/snap/run.py when gpt exits non-zero, is cancelled or times out; extra carries the argv, exit code, duration and the last Java exception; the hint is matched on that exception (heap, orbit, DEM, unknown operator, missing file).

docs.title: E512 SnapOutputError
docs.text: Raised by: the SNAP Steps when gpt exited 0 but the expected BEAM-DIMAP product is absent or empty.

docs.title: E600 StorageError
docs.text: Family base for filesystem problems.

docs.title: E601 WriteError
docs.text: Raised by: writers. Meaning: a file could not be written.

docs.title: E602 PermissionDeniedError
docs.text: Raised by: classification of WinError 5 / EACCES / EPERM, safe_unlink. Meaning: permission denied.

docs.title: E603 DiskFullError
docs.text: Raised by: classification of WinError 112 / ENOSPC, preflight disk check. Meaning: no space left.

docs.title: E604 PathTooLongError
docs.text: Raised by: classification of WinError 206 / ENAMETOOLONG, preflight path check. Meaning: the path exceeds the platform limit.

docs.title: E605 FileLockedError
docs.text: Raised by: utils.fs.replace_with_retry, safe_unlink. Meaning: another process holds the file (WinError 32, or 5 on some volumes); the message counts the attempts.

docs.title: E606 AtomicSaveError
docs.text: Raised by: utils.fs.atomic_write_text. Meaning: the temp-file/replace sequence failed; the previous file is intact.

docs.title: E607 OutputMissingError
docs.text: Raised by: the Runner after Step.run. Meaning: a declared product was not written.

docs.title: E701 PreflightError
docs.text: Raised by: the Runner / CLI when a blocking preflight check fails (extra.checks lists the P-codes).

docs.title: E801 StepFailedError
docs.text: Raised by: Runner.run after persisting the failure record (__cause__ is the original exception).

docs.title: E802 StepInterruptedError
docs.text: Recorded by: the Runner when a step is found running without a run_end in its log (process killed, drive unplugged); the step becomes failed and is re-executed.

docs.title: E803 StepCancelledError
docs.text: Raised by: the Runner on KeyboardInterrupt; status cancelled.

docs.title: Reserved error codes (documented, not yet raised)
E501 ToolExitError (reserved)
docs.text: External tool exited with an error; extra.returncode/argv/stderr_tail. Classification of subprocess.CalledProcessError already yields this code. Planned for the unwrapping step.

docs.title: E503 ToolTimeoutError (reserved)
docs.text: External tool exceeded its time limit. Planned for the unwrapping step.

docs.title: E804 WorkerCrashedError (reserved)
docs.text: A worker process died (BrokenProcessPool). Planned for multi-process execution.

docs.title: E900 NumericalError (reserved)
docs.text: Family base for numerical failures.

docs.title: E901 SingularMatrixError (reserved)
docs.text: numpy.linalg.LinAlgError; the network/design matrix is singular. Planned for the SBAS inversion.

docs.title: E902 NonFiniteResultError (reserved)
docs.text: A kernel produced NaN/Inf where finite values were required. Planned for the DInSAR kernels.

docs.title: E904 NoCandidatesError (reserved)
docs.text: Zero PS candidates after thresholds. Planned for the PS chain.

docs.title: Warning codes (W)
docs.text: Emitted as warning records in the run log; they never stop a run.

docs.title: W000 CapturedPythonWarning
docs.text: A Python warnings message raised inside Step.run. Warnings whose file lies inside this package or a tests/ tree are recorded one by one (category, filename, lineno) and counted in step_end.summary.n_warnings. Third-party warnings (site-packages: CuPy compiler.py EncodingWarnings, NumPy deprecations) are not recorded individually: they are counted per module into one W000 record (detail.third_party = {module: count}) and into step_end.summary.n_warnings_third_party.

docs.title: W101 StepSkipped
docs.text: The step was done with existing outputs and the same version; nothing was re-run (--force overrides). The parameters are compared but do not decide: when the requested parameters differ from the recorded ones, the message names the differing keys and the record carries them in detail.changed_params (null when nothing differs); the recorded result is still kept and the step is still skipped. Re-run with --force, or give the step another id to keep both results. pipeline stripmap-coregister refuses such a skip instead (E101): its old stack would be imported again.

docs.title: W102 ParamDefaulted
docs.text: A parameter fell back to its default because the given value was empty.

docs.title: W103 VersionUnknown
docs.text: The package version is the fallback 0.0.0 (installed without git history); set SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION or install from a checkout.

docs.title: W104 InterruptedStepMarkedFailed
docs.text: A running step from a crashed run was diagnosed (E802) and marked failed before this run continued.

docs.title: W105 LegacyNameDeprecated
docs.text: A name from before the rename to Bosar was read: an environment variable with the old prefix (read only while the BOSAR_* variable of the same suffix is unset), raster tags in the old GDAL metadata namespace, or a product reference / crop.json whose format carries the old name. The old names are listed in src/bosar/_legacy.py; nothing is written under them. Rename the variable or re-run the step that wrote the file; bosar preflight lists old-prefix variables (check system.legacy_env). Support ends in 0.2.0.

docs.title: W106 CcdOnSlcBoxCoherence
docs.text: The ccd step read a coherence product whose estimator tag is slc-box (the author's MintPy recipe: a full-resolution box larger than the looks, then the block mean). Neighbouring looked pixels then share samples, so ccd_z is spatially correlated (null-case Moran's I ≈ 0.37 instead of < 0.1) and detections reach about one looked pixel beyond a real change (precision ≈ 0.72 on the injected patch, recall 1). pipeline ccd therefore defaults to --recipe looks; the warning names the pairs. Re-run the coherence steps with --recipe looks (a --tag) when the statistics must be pixel-independent.

docs.title: W107 SbasNetworkSplit
docs.text: sbas_invert found that the pairs left after the pair-level rules (empty, weak and unreliable pairs) no longer connect all the dates: the network has two or more parts and the offset between them is unknown for every pixel. The time series is still written (zero velocity across the gap, the minimum-norm solution), the velocity is fitted with one common rate and one offset per part, and ts_mask counts a pixel as connected when its network is connected inside every part. To bridge the gap, keep more pairs: design the network with more links across the period (sbas network --k, --max-dt), lower sbas prep --min-coherent-fraction, raise unw_correct --pair-max-error, or name the pairs to exclude yourself with sbas_invert --exclude-pairs.

docs.title: W108 LowUsableFraction
docs.text:
The quality verdict of a time-series chain (core/sbas/quality.py). sbas_invert, ts_correct and the PS/DS chain judge what they measured and write summary.quality = {verdict, findings, indicators}; every finding is logged under its code with the measured value, the threshold and a remedy, the CLI prints the verdict after the chain and the Results page shows it above the map. Verdicts: usable (no finding), marginal (read the result only with the stated limits), not_usable (do not interpret as deformation).

code indicator marginal not usable usual remedy W108 fraction of the image that is connected with temporal coherence above the threshold < 20 % < 2 % PS / DS chain, Goldstein filter before unwrapping, fewer looks, a smaller area W109 share of the designed pairs left out (empty, weak, unreliable), or a date without pairs > 30 % or any lost date - bosar sbas quality per-date table; drop or re-coregister the date; shorter links or a season rule W110 standard deviation of the velocity over the good pixels > 4 mm/yr > 10 mm/yr longer series, tropospheric correction, deramp, an independent chain W111 pair-pixels in triplets that do not close after the correction > 15 % - filter, more looks, mask before unwrapping, shorter baselines W112 median velocity of the good pixels, when larger than 3 mm/yr and than the spread yes - before deramping: --deramp, a reference inside the area (--ref-latlon); after deramping the reference pixel itself is off: another reference — sbas quality --area deforming: W110 judges the spread of the velocity residual about a smooth field (smooth_km, 1 km) and W113 the whole-cycle steps relative to each pixel's fitted line; --area auto picks it when the raw spread exceeds three times a stable area's expectation; the reference moves to the most coherent cell of the stable quintile when the chain chose it — — — W117 a date whose residual to the fitted line exceeds 3 robust standard deviations at more than 20 % of the sampled good pixels; marginal at 35 % and more; the verdict drops when two or more dates are marginal yes - --exclude-dates, --fit huber, --tropo gacos|era5

The thresholds are judgement values for C-band 12-day stacks (quality.THRESHOLDS), not physical limits.

docs.title: W109 PairsExcluded
docs.text: Quality verdict: see the table under W108.

docs.title: W110 VelocityNoise
docs.text: Quality verdict: see the table under W108.

docs.title: W111 UnclosedTriplets
docs.text: Quality verdict: see the table under W108.

docs.title: W112 SceneTrend
docs.text: Quality verdict: see the table under W108.

docs.title: W113 TimeSeriesJumps
docs.text: Quality verdict: after the step common to all pixels is removed (see W114), more than 3 % of the good pixels have a step larger than three quarters of a cycle (0.75 × λ/2 in range, 21 mm at C band) that is still there one date later (a single noisy date steps out and back and is not counted) between two consecutive dates of one network part. Deformation of that size in one revisit is rare; a unwrapping error in time or a date with missing / corrupted data is the usual cause. The message names the dates at which most jumps occur (summary.jumps_by_date). Found on the downtown test area: 20250430 holds a zero-filled strip, and one cycle of error starts at that date in patches of the image.

docs.title: W114 ReferenceUnstable
docs.text: Quality verdict: between consecutive dates the good pixels move together against the reference pixel by more than 5 mm (standard deviation over the dates of their median step, summary.reference_step_std_mm). The reference itself is unstable - on the downtown test area the automatic choice fell on a strong scatterer on a tall building, whose uncompensated height error changes phase with every baseline. Velocities are little affected (a common offset), single dates are. W113 counts jumps after this common step is removed.

docs.title: W117 DateOutlier
docs.text: Quality verdict: the inversion keeps a sample of the good pixels (every n-th, about 200 000 at most) and the residual of their series to the fitted velocity line (one intercept per network part; the median offset for a Huber fit). One robust scale is taken over the whole sample (1.4826 × MAD, summary.date_outliers.scale_mm; the test needs six dates or more, a shorter series has degenerate residuals); a date at which more than 20 % of the sampled pixels lie further than 3 scales from the sample median is an outlier - its atmosphere (or bad data) has moved the whole scene, which deformation does not do in one revisit. summary.date_outliers lists the flagged dates and the fraction of every date; bosar sbas quality prints them. The message says whether the least-squares velocity leans on the date or the Huber fit (--fit huber) has down-weighted it; either way the series at that date stays biased - leave the date out with --exclude-dates or correct the troposphere. The temporal reference is never such a date: with no --ref-date, the reference is the date whose common mode (the scene-wide median) lies closest to the median over the dates (summary.ref_date_rule = common_mode_median, the common modes in summary.common_mode_mm). Found on the three-year Indianapolis product: the first date, 2023-07-10, sat 4 mm below the rest and one 2026-06 date 14 mm above at three landmarks. Two levels since v0.4.0: a date beyond 20 % is noted (the finding is informational, printed with (info), the verdict stands); a date at 35 % or more is marginal and named as such; the verdict drops to MARGINAL only when two or more dates are marginal - one atmospheric date is tolerated because --fit huber or --exclude-dates handles it and the per-date fractions ship with the product (summary.date_outliers) either way.

docs.title: W115 ClosureBudgetUnreached
docs.text: Closure correction (unw_correct): the exact L1 programs run under a wall-clock budget (--correct-budget-s, 900 s by default), the closure patterns covering most pixels first; the patterns not reached stay uncorrected and the warning carries their share of the pixels with errors. A longer budget or more workers reaches them.

docs.title: W116 IntermediatesRematerialized
docs.text: Chains in storage_mode=minimal: a step of the chain is done, but the tier-2 products it made were collected after the chain that declared them had finished (the producer's summary.collected lists the kinds), and a later step of this chain requires them - e.g. pipeline psi after a completed pipeline psds needs the flattened stack again. The chain re-runs that step with the same parameters instead of failing with E107; the record gets summary.rematerialized_for, and the re-made products are collected again when their new dependents are done. Declaring both chains before the first one runs avoids the re-run, as does storage_mode=full.

docs.title: W201 MetadataSuspicious
docs.text: Recorded on a dataset (and in the run log when imported) when a reader detects metadata that is nominal rather than measured — e.g. the SNAP StaMPS export writes near_range_slc/far_range_slc as centre ∓ (N−1)/2 × the nominal 2 m spacing, so the slant-range axis and every incidence angle derived from it are approximate; or every .rslc.par carries the reference scene's date/time header (then acq_utc is the file-name date). Never corrected silently; the warning text says what to verify. bosar data import --annotation <SAFE> resolves the range-axis case from the Sentinel-1 annotation and records I201 instead (see Info records below and docs/data/formats.md).

docs.title: I201 GeometryCorrected (info, not a warning)
docs.text: Appended to a stack's info list (and to the StackRecord) when data import --annotation or data crop --annotation overwrote the nominal GAMMA/StaMPS geometry from the matching Sentinel-1 swath annotation: range spacing, near/mid/far range, azimuth spacing, both radii, incidence angles, the re-projected B⊥ of every pair (first pair before → after in the text) and acq_utc from the SAFE startTime. geometry.provenance becomes safe-annotation:<file>.

docs.title: W202 SidecarMalformed
docs.text: Recorded on a stack when one metadata sidecar cannot be parsed or holds a non-physical value while the rest of the stack is fine — e.g. the author's diff0/20240821_20240809.base carries TCN components of ~1e11 m (the same pair MintPy reported as B⊥ = −1.3e11). The affected pair keeps its interferogram but has no baseline row; the warning names the file and the value. A stack whose reference metadata is broken still fails hard (E204/E205).

docs.title: W203 CalibrationAbsent
docs.text: Recorded on a Sentinel-1 SAFE product whose annotation/calibration/ folder (σ⁰/β⁰/γ⁰ LUTs and noise vectors) is absent — the author's VV-only unzips are like this. Interferometry proceeds; radiometric calibration steps will refuse the product until the full SAFE (or the zip) is supplied.

docs.title: W204 ProductSpacingMismatch
docs.text: Reported by bosar info <product.tif> when a Step product's per-look pixel spacing (tags pixel_spacing_*_m / looks_*) differs by more than 0.1 % from the project stack that has the same geometry_provenance. This is the v0.1.0 regression (Steps re-opened the raw export and wrote the nominal 2 × 14 m grid although the stack had been corrected with --annotation); it is fixed by reapply_from_provenance and the check keeps it from returning. info also prints a W201 line when a product carries the reader's nominal geometry (geometry_provenance = reader).

docs.title: W205 AuxDataMarginal
docs.text: Reported by bosar aux gacos-check when a delivered file is usable but not clean: the GACOS grid leaves less than 0.05 deg between the stack footprint and its edge, more than 1 % of the grid inside the area is NaN or zero, the grid steps differ between dates, grids exist for dates outside the stack, or the acquisition time is unknown so TIME_OF_DAY could not be checked. The same check reports hard problems with the input codes: E201 a date's .ztd or .ztd.rsc is missing, E204 wrong file size, TIME_OF_DAY more than --time-tolerance-h (1 h) from the acquisition, grid not covering the footprint or a median delay outside 1-3 m, E205 unreadable .rsc header; any E makes the folder unusable (exit 5).

docs.title: W206 EmptyInterferogram
docs.text: Reported by bosar data import (GAMMA/StaMPS reader) when a <ref>_<date>.diff or a <date>.rslc holds only zeros in 25 small windows sampled across the raster: the export wrote an empty interferogram for that date (seen for three dates of the author's SNAP export, the same dates whose .base is malformed). The stack still imports; bosar sbas prep drops every pair derived from such an interferogram (empty_pairs) and ifg_flatten can rebuild an empty .diff from the SLCs when those are valid; an empty .rslc cannot be rebuilt from the stack - re-export that date or preprocess it again.

docs.title: W207 PartiallyEmptyDate
docs.text: slc_flatten scans every date of the stack and reports the fraction of zero pixels (summary.missing_fraction_by_date). A date with more than 0.1 % zero pixels inside the stack's common area is partially empty: a strip the export did not fill, a burst that failed. bosar pipeline psds leaves such dates out by default and says so (--keep-partial-dates keeps them: every pixel of the empty area is then lost for all dates). Re-coregister the date from the raw product to get it back.

docs.title: W208 CommonZeroFloor
docs.text: slc_flatten (v3) and bosar data import (every reader) measure the zero pixels of every date against the common floor: the median zero fraction of the non-empty dates, which is the scene edge / burst-gap area the export leaves empty on every date (6.5 % on the full 9-burst IW2 swath). W208 reports that floor once; W207 is then raised only for a date lacking more than two percentage points beyond it. Nothing is left out because of W208 alone.

docs.title: W209 RangeShiftLarge
docs.text: s1_coregister: the amplitude cross-correlation of a date against the reference reads a range shift above 0.1 px. The shift is still applied only under the gate (above range_cc_min_px = 0.02 px and the bursts agreeing within range_cc_max_spread_px = 0.01 px); W209 says that a shift this large is a change of the propagation delay between the date and the reference rather than a coregistration error: on the Indianapolis stack the ionospheric group delay (GIM slant TEC) and the ERA5 tropospheric delay explain the per-date shifts with r 0.87 and a 0.034-px residual, while the IPF version does not (table and regression in docs/data/formats.md). The carrier phase is baseband after deramping, so the correction moves the envelope only.

docs.title: W210 OffsetFieldSparse
docs.text: offset_tracking found that fewer than half of the patches with data carry a valid offset: the rest have an SNR below snr_min, a correlation peak on the edge of the search area, or deviate from the 3 × 3 median of the field by more than mad_k MAD. The products are written as usual (rejected patches are NaN, the classes are in offset_mask) and the summary counts every class, but the field is dominated by decorrelation and its median / std are not representative. It is also raised when no patch of the area has data (every class 255). Use a larger window, a shorter time span, or restrict the run to the coherent area (region, bbox).

docs.title: W211 OffsetSpacingNominal
docs.text: offset_tracking ran on a stack without lat / lon layers (--geocode false): the azimuth offsets are converted to metres with the stack's nominal azimuth pixel spacing (14.0 m for an ISCE-layout stack, whose reference/IW*.xml carries no azimuth spacing) instead of the along-track spacing measured from the layers, and nothing is geocoded. Range offsets use the slant-range spacing of the metadata and are exact.

docs.title: W213 SpeckleEnlNotEstimated
docs.text: The amplitude step was asked for a speckle filter that uses the ENL (--speckle lee, refined_lee, gamma_map or nlmeans; boxcar and frost do not use it and never raise W213) without an ENL (enl), and the automatic estimate on the reference date found no 32 × 32 block (or, on a small image, no block of the image's size) with at least 90 % valid pixels - the image is smaller than 8 × 8 multilooked pixels or mostly no-data (layover, shadow, zero fill). The filter ran with the nominal number of looks (azimuth × range looks) as the ENL, an upper bound (neighbouring looked pixels are correlated): the filter then takes the speckle for weaker than it is and keeps more of it. Pass the ENL with --set amplitude.enl=<looks> (measured with bosar.core.speckle.enl_window on a homogeneous area) to silence it.

docs.title: W215 ThermalNoiseIncomplete
docs.text: s1_coregister with calibrated layers: thermal-noise removal was requested - thermal_noise=on, or auto on an IPF 2.90 or later product - but the SAFE cannot provide it as asked. Either the noise annotation (annotation/calibration/noise-*.xml) is missing or unusable: the calibrated layers of that date are written without noise subtraction; or it holds range vectors only (IPF before 2.90, noiseVectorList; or a new-style file without azimuth vectors): the range noise is subtracted and the azimuth component (the TOPS scalloping) is not. The message names the date and the reason; the date's record (written.<date>.calibrated.thermal_noise) carries the decision, the IPF version and the clamped fraction.

docs.title: W216 ThermalNoiseMixed
docs.text: s1_coregister: the calibrated layers of some dates of the stack have the thermal noise removed and those of others do not - typically thermal_noise=auto on a stack that spans IPF 2.90 (March 2018), or a date without a usable noise annotation (W215). Areas near the noise floor (water, shadow) then step between the two groups of dates. The message lists the dates without removal; re-run with --thermal-noise off (none) or on (range-only noise for the older products) for one rule across the stack.

docs.title: W219 IonoNoSnaphuComponents
docs.text: iono_split (version 2, components=snaphu) found no SNAPHU executable (or the unwrapping backend was set to scikit-image): the full band was unwrapped with scikit-image, which unwraps every 4-connected region of coherent cells on its own (probe: two regions split by a masked band came out 2 cycles apart). Those regions are taken as the components; each one's weighted median is removed before the low-pass, as with SNAPHU's connected components. The estimate is usable; SNAPHU decides better which cells belong together (it grows components by cost, across thin decorrelated gaps). Install or point to the binary (BOSAR_SNAPHU_EXE, packaging/bin/<platform>/) and re-run the step.

docs.title: W220 IonoFragmentedComponents
docs.text: iono_split: the estimate rests on more than one connected component and the largest holds less than half of the used cells. Each component's median was removed (regions unwrapped independently differ by k half-cycles of dispersive phase, core.iono.ambiguity_step_rad), so the ionosphere between components - its long wavelengths across the scene - is not measured; summary.component_list gives each component's constant split into whole ambiguity steps and a remainder. Prefer a pair with more coherent area (winter, short temporal baseline), more looks, or a lower coh_min.

docs.title: W227 IonoModelSkipped
docs.text: The plausibility gate of sbas_invert --iono refused one or more ionospheric models: a model's span (max - min of the model grid that is subtracted) exceeded what a plausible TEC difference makes at the carrier (rad_per_tecu(f) x max(floor, k x |GIM difference|)), its gradient per 100 km of ground (the range slope taken from slant to ground range with the stack's mid-swath incidence) exceeded the ionosphere's (a fixed iono_gate_gradient, 2 TECU per 100 km by default; the GIM enters only the span bound), or the triplet closure vetoed it: a triplet whose three models do not close (the span of m_ab + m_bc - m_ac above the larger of iono_gate_closure_factor - 3 by default - times the median over the triplets and the phase of 1 TECU, rad_per_tecu(f)) names its pair of the largest span as the suspect, and a pair named so by failing triplets in at least half of all the triplets it belongs to (those whose three models are defined) is vetoed. A model that is undefined (its fit could not be made) is skipped as span. Nothing is subtracted for those pairs; the inversion runs on; the summary's iono.gate names them with the reasons and the bounds. --no-iono-gate subtracts every model without judging it and fails the step (E201) on a pair whose model is undefined. A GIM term of the span bounds that was lost before any model was judged is W228.

docs.title: W228 IonexGimUnavailable
docs.text: sbas_invert --iono with the plausibility gate on: the GIM term of the span bounds (W227) was lost for some pairs before any model was judged - the IONEX folder named by --ionex-dir (or found at <project>/aux/ionex) is not a folder, the stack has no footprint centre, or some dates have no usable map (no file for the day, the acquisition time outside the maps, an unreadable file, no VTEC at the centre of a regional map). The message names the folder and a date with its reason; the detail carries gim_pairs (pairs with a finite GIM difference at both dates), ionex_dir, gim_error and up to 20 dates_without_map, and the summary's iono.gate keeps gim_error, gim_dates_without_map and ionex_dir_source. Those pairs' span bounds rest on the floor (iono_gate_tec_floor, 10 TECU by default): the gate is stricter for them, never looser, so a model of a strongly ionised date may be skipped that its map would have let through. Put the daily IONEX file of every date into the folder (or name the right one) and re-run the inversion with --force. Without any IONEX folder, named or found, the floor applies silently.

docs.title: W223 EnvisatMetadataInconsistent
docs.text: data/asar.py: a metadata check of an ENVISAT ASAR IMS or ERS-1/2 IMS product in the Envisat format failed - the SPH disagrees with the annotation data sets (FIRST_LINE_TIME, LINE_LENGTH, PASS against the sign of the orbit's vertical velocity), the annotated line_time_interval does not match the stamped first-to-last-line span, the PRF is not the line rate, the radar frequency or the range sampling rate is off the sensor's nominal value by more than 0.1 %, the processed range bandwidth is off the chirp by more than 5 %, the geolocation grid is off the uniform range axis (0.05 samples) or the line timing (0.5 lines), the data type is not SWORD, the CHIRP PARAMS ADS is missing, or fewer than four product state vectors are usable (the orbit is then extended by two-body + J2 propagation). The message names the field and both values; the annotation data set wins over the SPH and nothing is corrected silently. The strings sit in extra["warnings"] of the StripmapScene; the chain logs them. None of the author's 26 products raises it. The same code checks an external precise orbit (a DORIS DOR_VOR_AX / DOR_POR_AX or ERS PRC file given as orbit_file, or the one open_asar(orbit_dir=...) - the stripmap chain's --orbits <folder> - takes from a folder) against the product's own state vectors at mid scene: more than 100 m apart (ORBIT_FILE_WARN_M) is a W223 naming the file and the distance; more than 1 km (ORBIT_FILE_REFUSE_M) is not this product's orbit - a file named as orbit_file is refused (E204), a folder's file is skipped for the next covering one with a W223 naming it, and E204 follows when every covering file is that far. On real products the matching precise orbit is about 10 m from the product's vectors (ERS PRC) or a few centimetres (ENVISAT DORIS); the other ERS satellite's PRC file of a tandem day is about 11 950 km away. A product without a usable state vector of its own raises a W223 saying that the orbit file is not checked.

docs.title: W224 Ers2GyroDoppler
docs.text: data/asar.py: an ERS-2 scene dated 2001-01-01 or later. ERS-2 lost its gyroscopes in January 2001 and flew in zero-gyro / degraded attitude modes afterwards: the Doppler centroid can be several PRF ambiguities large and the processor's annotation (DOP CENTROID COEFFS ADS, extra["processed_doppler_centroid"]) less reliable; a pair with such a scene needs its Doppler checked before the azimuth spectra are trusted. The message carries the mid-swath value and the confidence. The author's ERS-2 scenes on disk (1996-05 ... 2000-03) all predate that date; note that the 2000-03-17 scene, acquired after the February 2000 switch to one-gyro piloting, already shows a mid-swath Doppler of -349 Hz (0.21 PRF, the other ERS-2 scenes -91 ... -148 Hz) and is not flagged by the date rule.

docs.title: W221 AlosPrfVaries
docs.text: data/ceos_alos.py: the ALOS-1 PALSAR L1.1 reader reads the PRF field of every line header (an integer in mHz) and compares the lines with each other and with the leader's PRF (Pulse Repetition Frequency in mHz, with decimals). A variation across the lines above PRF_TOLERANCE = 1e-6 relative is E205 (one StripmapScene has one PRF; such a file is not one scene). A smaller variation, or a difference between the lines and the leader, is W221: the leader's PRF is used for the azimuth time interval and the line times. On the real products the field is constant and 1e-7 from the leader (the millihertz rounding). The warning is kept in scene.extra["warnings"]. v0.4.0 (ALOS-2): the same code reports the microsecond line stamps' own clock when its rate differs from the leader's PRF by more than the tolerance on a scene spanning at least one second (the Greenland scenes: 8.8e-6 fast, ±44 µs at the ends); the leader's PRF and the centre-weighted fit are used.

docs.title: W222 AlosLeaderPrefixMismatch
docs.text: data/ceos_alos.py: the leader and the image file's line headers describe the same scene twice and the reader checks them against each other. Scene centre time: the least-squares fit of the per-line millisecond stamps puts the scene centre line more than 2 ms from the leader's Scene centre time (E205 above 1 s) - the line times are used. Slant range to the first sample: the leader's range gate delay times c/2 differs by more than 1 m from the integer-metre field of the line headers (E205 above 100 m) - the leader's value is used. On the real products both agree within the quantisation of the header fields (0.5 ms, 0.5 m). v0.4.0 (ALOS-2): the same code reports the leader's Doppler center frequency fields (a + b R) disagreeing with its cross-track polynomial at the first sample by more than 5 Hz, and the millisecond and microsecond stamps disagreeing on the first line by more than 2 ms (the polynomial and the microseconds are used); the ALOS-2 range gate delay is not checked at all - it is not the delay to the first sample. v0.4.0 review (ALOS-2 range bandwidth): the reader takes the range bandwidth from the leader, not from the mode's nominal table - the chirp's |rate| x pulse length and the total processor bandwidth in range field are each plausible when positive, not above the range sampling rate and within ALOS2_BANDWIDTH_TOLERANCE (25 %) of the mode's nominal bandwidth. The same code reports a chirp that is blank or implausible (the total processor bandwidth is used when it is plausible, else the nominal value), and a chirp and a total processor bandwidth that are both plausible but differ by more than BANDWIDTH_CHECK_REL (2 % of the chirp): the smaller of the two is used, since the image's range spectrum is no wider than either. A plausible chirp next to a total that differs from it by more than 2 % but is not plausible itself is reported too, and the chirp is kept. scene.extra records chirp_bandwidth_hz, total_bandwidth_range_leader_hz, nominal_bandwidth_hz and range_bandwidth_source. The Greenland FBS products give 24.9 MHz from both fields (nominal 28 MHz) and raise nothing; ALOS-1 keeps its nominal 28 / 14 MHz without a check.

docs.title: W225 StripmapRefineNotApplied
docs.text: stripmap_coregister: the amplitude cross-correlation refinement of a date (core.offsets.track between the reference and the geometrically coregistered secondary on a coarse patch grid, then core.stripmap.fit_offset_plane) was not applied - fewer than refine_min_patches valid patches survived the SNR / edge / MAD culling (water, snow, a decorrelated pair, an empty scene), the written window holds no patch at all (a crop smaller than refine_window + 2 refine_search), or the fitted constant exceeded the search radius minus one pixel (the correlation peak sits against the search border: the geometric offsets are off by more than refine_search pixels, which points at a timing or orbit problem of that product rather than at a sub-pixel residual). The geometric offsets alone are used for that date; the record keeps the rejected fit (refinement.reason). Inspect refinement.n_valid / rms_px in the stack record; a larger --refine-search, or --no-refine, is the way round a product with a known timing error. Since v0.4.0 a third reason: the residual rms of the kept patches exceeds refine_max_rms_px (2 px by default) in azimuth or range - the patches found no correlation peak (the VV band of a NISAR river-delta scene scattered by 9 px on 250 patches), and the plane fitted through noise would misregister the date; the geometric offsets alone are kept.

docs.title: W226 StripmapMetadataIncomplete
docs.text: stripmap_coregister: a scene's metadata does not fully determine the chain's inputs and an assumption was made. (a) The products mix range samplings - ALOS FBD (14 MHz) with FBS (28 MHz) - and the reader of the FBD scene took no oversample_to_fbs flag, so the pair is coregistered at different range samplings: the geometry is right (the offsets are in each scene's own pixels) but the range spectra overlap by half, which costs coherence; a reader that oversamples silences it. (b) A zero-Doppler product (ASAR / ERS IMS, NISAR RSLC) carries no processed Doppler centroid (extra["processed_doppler_centroid"]), so the secondary is interpolated without demodulation: with the azimuth spectrum off centre by the processor's centroid, the sinc kernel aliases part of it (a few per cent of coherence at ASAR's typical few hundred hertz; more for a yaw-steering-free ERS-1 scene).

docs.title: W301 OrbitFromAnnotation
docs.text: The native TOPS chain (s1_coregister) found no precise orbit file for a date in the project, the data roots or SNAP's cache and used the annotation's state vectors (10 s spacing, metre-level). Run bosar fetch orbits for the products and re-run the step.

docs.title: W302 EsdNoCoherentOverlap
docs.text: Enhanced spectral diversity found no burst-overlap pixel above the coherence threshold (esd_coherence) for a date; the geometric coregistration (orbits + DEM) stands without the azimuth correction. Lower the threshold, widen the looks, or check the date (an empty or decorrelated scene).

docs.title: W401 GpuUnavailable
docs.text: CuPy or a CUDA device was not usable; the run continues on NumPy (reason carries the exception text).

docs.title: W501 SnaphuUnavailable
docs.text: No SNAPHU binary/package; unwrapping falls back to scikit-image.

docs.title: W503 SnaphuNoCs2
docs.text: Retired: mst is the default initialisation of the unwrap step since v0.4.0 (every bundled SNAPHU is a NO_CS2 build, and on a real Sentinel-1 pair the two initialisations differed by one cycle on 4 of 117 888 pixels), so the substitution this warning announced no longer happens by default. An init: mcf asked of a binary without the solver still runs as MST; the step summary records init (applied) and init_requested, without a warning. The code is never reused. The text it carried in v0.4.0: the unwrap step asked SNAPHU for an initialisation the binary cannot run: it was built without the CS2 minimum-cost-flow solver (the solver has its own non-commercial licence), so INITMETHOD MCF is unavailable and the unwrap ran with the MST initialisation; the step summary records init (applied) and init_requested. The installers carry that SNAPHU, and so does a source checkout that uses the bundled binary or builds its own with -NoCs2 / --no-cs2 (bosar preflight reports it as "no CS2 solver (MST init)") - so with the step's default init=mcf this warning comes with every SNAPHU unwrap there: it records the substitution, not a fault. The result is the same optimisation from a different starting flow; on a real Sentinel-1 pair (117 888 unwrapped pixels) the two initialisations differed by one cycle on 4 pixels and nowhere by more. An unwrap step whose parameters ask for init: mst runs without the warning; a SNAPHU of your own that carries the solver, named with BOSAR_SNAPHU_EXE, runs MCF.

docs.title: W502 SnapHeapFromInstall
docs.text: A snap_* Step ran with heap_mb = 0, i.e. with the -Xmx of the install's gpt.vmoptions, and that default is larger than the heap Bosar gives a job when heap_mb is unset (half of the RAM, at least 2 GB and at most 64 GB). SNAP fills whatever heap it is given (41-45 GB peak RSS for a three-scene subset under -Xmx132G), so parallel work on the machine may starve. Pass heap_mb / --snap-heap <MB> or leave the parameter unset.

docs.title: W601 Tier2Kept
docs.text: storage_mode=full kept intermediate products that minimal would have deleted.

docs.title: W602 GcDeleteFailed
docs.text: Garbage collection could not delete a file (locked by another process or permission denied); the file is listed under kept with the reason and the step status is unaffected.

docs.title: W802 PostFailureActionFailed
docs.text: A bookkeeping action after a failure (save, gc, report) failed itself; the original failure is preserved.

docs.title: W803 HookFailed
docs.text: A client-registered hook raised; the step status is unaffected.

docs.title: Preflight check codes (P)
docs.text: P1xx system · P2xx gpu · P3xx dependencies · P4xx binaries · P5xx credentials · P6xx network · P7xx project. Version 0.4.0 added P202 gpu.plugin (the GPU plug-in of an installed build: present, absent with an NVIDIA driver seen, or not needed) and P305 deps.build (the build record of an installed build: id, platform, time, commit, SNAPHU solver); P401 now says whether the SNAPHU binary carries the CS2 solver. The full list with the check ids lives in src/bosar/preflight/model.py (CHECK_CODES) and is printed by bosar preflight; blocking failures raise E701.

Nothing in the present choice prevents a commercial licence, a dual licence, a source-available licence or full open source later: the author holds every right. What would have to change on that day:

  • SNAPHU: keep it free and separate (a downloadable add-on, never part of a paid artefact), or replace it with an unwrapper under the author's control; the CS2 solver stays out.

docs.title: Run log schema (log_schema_version = 1)
docs.text:
Every processing run writes three files under <project>/logs/:

File Content run_<run_id>.jsonl one JSON object per line, the machine-readable record of the run run_<run_id>.log the same records, one human-readable line each (#seq ts LEVEL event …), with a WHERE/HINT/TRACEBACK block for failures run_<run_id>.md the run report: environment, preflight, steps table, failure block, warnings, storage, files — rewritten atomically at every transition

run_id = r_<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>_<4 hex> (logging/records.py::new_run_id), unique for two runs in the same second. Files are UTF-8 with LF line endings on every platform.

docs.title: Record keys
docs.text:
Every record carries: ts (UTC, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ), seq (1-based, strictly increasing per run — the order key, because on Windows 87 % of datetime.now() stamps repeat within 20 000 calls), run_id, level (INFO|WARNING|ERROR), event, step (step id or null), msg, pid (worker records carry the child pid).

event additional keys run_start app_version, argv, env (allow-listed, redacted environment digest), env_sha256, log_schema_version, reproduce preflight report (counts, blocking, checks[] with code, id, group, status, detail, hint, duration_s) step_start kind, version, params (validated, as run), inputs[] (path, bytes, sha256), device, reproduce step_progress done, total, tile (throttled: first, last, every ≥ 1 s or ≥ 5 %) step_end outputs{kind: path}, figures[], summary (per-product stats and step summary), duration_s step_failed error (errors.describe(): type, code, title, msg, where, param, hint, doc, traceback, frames, notes, cause_chain), duration_s, params, inputs[], outputs_partial[], tile, progress gc deleted[], kept[] (with reasons), freed_bytes warning code (Wxxx, see docs/ERRORS.md), detail run_end status (done|failed|cancelled|blocked), n_steps, n_failed, duration_s, report

Deviation from the project rules ("preflight results are the first records of every run"): the first record is run_start — a header carrying the environment digest and log_schema_version — and the preflight records follow immediately.

docs.title: Environment digest and redaction
docs.text: run_start.env records the package version, Python and platform, the versions of the declared dependencies, the git HEAD of the checkout (when present), the backend device_info() and only the environment variables whose names start with BOSAR_, PROJ_, GDAL_, CUDA_ or PYTHON; PATH is stored as a SHA-256 only. Every mapping passes through utils.redact.redact(): keys matching token|secret|passw|pwd|api_key|auth|cookie|netrc|credential become *** and user:password@ in URLs is masked. The same redaction applies to the .log mirror, the report and the CLI output, because logs travel inside release packages and issue reports.

docs.title: Worker processes
docs.text: Workers (Windows spawn) are initialised with logging.queue.worker_init(queue, run_id) and emit records with worker_event(...); the records travel through a QueueHandler → QueueListener in the parent and receive their seq from the same RecordSink as the main process, so seq stays strictly increasing across producers while ts is only guaranteed non-decreasing per producer.

docs.title: Reading logs
docs.text: bosar logs <project> --tail N | --failure | --report | --validate; the reader (logging/reader.py) reports a damaged line as E104 with the file, line and column.

docs.title: Warnings captured inside a step
docs.text:
warning records with code = "W000" come in two forms. A warning raised in this package or in a tests/ tree is one record per warning with detail.category, detail.filename, detail.lineno. Warnings raised in third-party code (any path under site-packages) are summarised: one W000 record per step with detail.third_party = {"<module>": <count>, ...} and a message listing the modules. step_end.summary.n_warnings counts the individually recorded warnings; step_end.summary.n_warnings_third_party counts the summarised ones.

run_start.reproduce lists only the parameters that differ from the step defaults (the full resolved set is in step_start.params). Run ids carry microseconds (r_<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSffffff>Z_<4 hex>) so log file names sort by start time; readers pick the latest run by run_start.ts, not by name.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: What Bosar does today, what comes next, and what is further out — by capability. Dates are not promised; each release's changelog says what actually landed.

docs.title: Available (0.4.1-beta)
docs.text:
• Installers for Windows (.exe, per-user) and macOS (.dmg); the GPU as a plug-in (bosar gpu install); bosar demo as the smoke test of an installed build.
  • Sentinel-1 IW: the native TOPS chain from the raw zips (coregistration, ESD, calibration, sub-swath merge) and the SNAP bridge; SLC search and download from ASF; orbits, DEM, GACOS and ERA5 fetched or found locally.
  • Two-pass DInSAR, coherence change detection with damage-proxy maps, amplitude change with speckle filters and thermal-noise removal, offset tracking.
  • Time series: SBAS with closure-based correction; PS / DS by phase linking with a hybrid stack; classic PS-InSAR; a quality verdict with a stable-area and a deforming-area mode; tropospheric corrections (GACOS, ERA5); ionosphere split-spectrum diagnostics with opt-in models.
  • Stripmap sensors: ALOS-1 PALSAR (a 16-scene series validated), ENVISAT ASAR, ERS-1/2; the first NISAR granule opens.
  • Desktop application: every workflow as one command shown in the window, a result viewer with basemaps (off until enabled), layers, masks, time-series plots and figure export, logs with failure cards, the licence in the About card.
  • Documentation: the feature tour (English and Chinese, 4K bundle), the Chinese walkthrough, the API reference.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• The installers' second iteration from the first field reports: a smaller bundle (the DEM through the direct tile download only), macOS notarisation when a developer certificate is available, the installer's own pages in the tour.
  • The ionosphere per-pair plausibility gate before any model is subtracted (span and gradient against the band's physical bound and the GIM, triplet closure as a veto).
  • ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 (CEOS L1.1 reader, the L-band profile reused) and the first NISAR interferogram when a repeat granule exists.
  • DORIS precise orbits for ENVISAT / ERS and the orbital ramp they remove.
  • An English walkthrough.

docs.title: Later
docs.text:
• SAOCOM, RADARSAT Constellation, Gaofen-3 (stripmap readers); the X-band commercial formats (TerraSAR-X, COSMO-SkyMed, ICEYE, Capella) from sample data; Sentinel-1 EW and SM modes.
  • A Level-0 focusing study.
  • Multi-track fusion and LOS-to-vertical decomposition; corridor and asset reports.

The sensor-by-sensor status, with archives and sample scenes, is kept in the sensor download plan.

docs.title: Bosar walkthrough: from a fresh clone to the downtown displacement map and damage proxy map
docs.text:
Using an installed build? This walkthrough was written on a source checkout. The steps that use the source tree (git clone, pip install -e, scripts/..., pytest) need the source code, which is not published and is available only under a source licence from the author (see Licensing). With the installers, start at Install and at step 50 (the installed version); the bosar commands of the other steps are the commands of the installed build.

This is the English edition of the Chinese walkthrough WALKTHROUGH_zh.md; the screenshots are shared between the two editions.

Applies to: v0.1.0-alpha.1 (end of phase 1). This manual answers "how far does the software go right now": every command was run verbatim while the manual was written, and the full output is in the release notes. There is no graphical interface yet; everything is done in PowerShell.

Goal: on a 7.2 × 10.8 km crop of downtown Indianapolis, starting from a GAMMA/StaMPS stack exported by SNAP, obtain the geocoded line-of-sight displacement map geo_disp, the coherence-change damage proxy map geo_dpm, the amplitude log-ratio and RGB composite, then clip them to 500 m either side of the highways and export them as COG + GeoPackage. The whole process takes about 8 minutes on the CPU, most of it the pip install of step 2; the processing itself is under 2 minutes.

docs.title: Step 0: Edit these three variables for your machine (the only place that needs changing)
docs.text:
$DATA = "<data-root>"                  # read-only data pool (this walkthrough only reads from it, never writes)
$MAIN = "<repo>"       # the main working copy, where SNAPHU is already built
$WORK = "<repo>\data\walkthrough_bosar"   # where the fresh clone goes

Files used under $DATA: the GAMMA stack 01_Preprocessed\01_IW2\, the original zip 00_RawData\S1A_IW_SLC__1SDV_20240821T..._E05B.zip (only the geometry annotation is read, nothing is extracted), the highway lines 04_GIS\indianapolis_highways.geojson, and the GACOS folder 05_Auxiliary\00_GACOS\.

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the code
docs.text:
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $WORK | Out-Null
Set-Location $WORK
git -c safe.directory=* clone --quiet $MAIN bosar_walk
Set-Location bosar_walk
git -c safe.directory=* log --oneline -1

The clone comes from the main working copy of step 0 ($MAIN); the public repository on GitHub carries the documentation and the installers, not the source. Readers who were given the address of the source repository put it in place of $MAIN. On a disk that does not record file ownership, git reports "dubious ownership" (exit code 128) on a fresh clone; the command above allows it for this one call only and does not touch your global configuration. To allow it permanently, run git config --global --add safe.directory <clone directory> yourself.

docs.title: Step 2: Create the Python environment
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install --quiet -e ".[dev,unwrap,viz]"
python --version
  • unwrap installs scikit-image (the unwrapping fallback when SNAPHU is absent), viz installs matplotlib (quick-look figures).
  • With an NVIDIA GPU, also run python -m pip install -e ".[gpu]" and the software uses CuPy automatically; this manual does not install it and runs everything on the CPU (preflight reports W401, which is normal).

docs.title: Step 3: Development environment variables
docs.text:
. .\scripts\dev_env.ps1

Puts the ruff / pytest / CuPy caches inside the repository's .cache\ and reminds you that only one process should use the GPU at a time (do not run the full test suite while a pipeline is running).

docs.title: Step 4: Self-check with preflight
docs.text:
bosar version
bosar preflight

Checks Python, dependencies, GPU, disk, SNAPHU and so on item by item; OK passes, WARN lets you continue, FAIL blocks the run. A fresh clone has no SNAPHU executable yet, so P401 shows WARN (W501: it will fall back to scikit-image).

docs.title: Step 5: Put SNAPHU in place
docs.text:
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force packaging\bin\win-x64 | Out-Null
Copy-Item "$MAIN\packaging\bin\win-x64\snaphu.exe" packaging\bin\win-x64\
bosar preflight | Select-String "P401"

SNAPHU 2.0.6 is compiled by packaging\snaphu\build.ps1 with MinGW-w64; on the same input it gives pixel-identical results to the SNAPHU the author runs in WSL. The binary is not in git (licence and platform reasons), so a fresh clone copies it from the main directory or compiles it. After the copy, P401 is OK.

docs.title: Step 6: Create a project
docs.text:
bosar project new walk --name walk_demo --storage-mode full

A project is just a folder: project.json (steps, parameters, product inventory), products\, logs\, scratch\. full keeps every intermediate product (handy for inspection); the default minimal deletes the regenerable intermediate files when the chain finishes.

docs.title: Step 7: Crop downtown out of the full stack
docs.text:
bosar data crop "$DATA\01_Preprocessed\01_IW2" --window 7904,8672,2590,5662 --dates 20240704,20240821,20240902,20240914,20250723 --annotation "$DATA\00_RawData\S1A_IW_SLC__1SDV_20240821T234025_20240821T234052_055318_06BEBA_E05B.zip" --out data\indy_downtown_crop

Reads a 768 × 3072 pixel window for 5 dates out of the 12239 × 25925 IW2 stack (read-only, windowed reads, the full scene is never loaded) and writes GeoTIFFs + crop.json under this repository's data\. --annotation reads the SAFE annotation straight from the original zip and replaces the nominal geometry of the SNAP export (2 m range spacing, Earth radius 11.5 km too small) with the real values (2.33 m and so on); crop.json records I201.

docs.title: Step 8: Import the crop and the full stack
docs.text:
bosar data import walk data\indy_downtown_crop
bosar data import walk "$DATA\01_Preprocessed\01_IW2" --annotation "$DATA\00_RawData\S1A_IW_SLC__1SDV_20240821T234025_20240821T234052_055318_06BEBA_E05B.zip"
bosar project info walk

Import only registers metadata (dates, geometry, baselines, footprint); the raw data stays where it is. The full stack has 29 scenes; the B⊥ of 20240821_20240704 is corrected from the nominal geometry's 223.8 m to 213.9 m (SNAP itself gives 216.1 m). The project now holds two stacks, and the pipelines below name one with --stack.

docs.title: Step 9: DInSAR pipeline → geo_disp
docs.text:
bosar pipeline dinsar walk --stack crop_indy_downtown_crop --all-pairs --looks 2,10 --backend snaphu --geocode-coh

Each interferogram pair runs in turn: ifg_import (references the differential interferogram in the stack) → multilook (2 × 10 looks, 28 × 23 m) → coherence (since v0.1.0 DInSAR defaults to the slc-box recipe: a 5 × 5 window at full resolution, then averaged inside the 2 × 10 block, consistent with MintPy's coherence; --recipe looks is the standard estimator with 20 samples per multilook block. CCD defaults to looks, see step 11) → goldstein (filtering) → unwrap (SNAPHU, single tile) → geocode_unw → displacement (d = −λφ/4π, metres, positive toward the satellite, 0 at the reference point) → geocode_disp → geocode_coh. One line per step on screen; the last line is the location of the run log. Four pairs make 36 steps, about 25 seconds on the CPU (results agree with the GPU to 1e-6).

docs.title: Step 10: Look at the quick-looks
docs.text:
Get-ChildItem walk\products\figure -Name | Select-Object -First 12
  • *_coherence.png: coherence (black 0 → white 1); river channels and vegetation are dark, buildings and roads bright.
  • *_unwrapped.png: unwrapped phase (radians, symmetric red-blue).
  • *_displacement.png: line-of-sight displacement (millimetres, red = toward the satellite, blue = away from the satellite, colour scale symmetric over the 2–98 % range); on 12–48 day short pairs this is mostly atmosphere (centimetre level), not ground subsidence.
  • The geo_* products (walk\products\geo_disp\ and so on) are EPSG:4326 GeoTIFFs that can be dragged straight into QGIS.

docs.title: Step 11: Coherence change detection → geo_dpm
docs.text:
bosar pipeline ccd walk --pre 20240821_20240902 20240821_20240914 --co 20240821_20240704
bosar pipeline ccd walk --pre 20240821_20240902 20240821_20240914 --co 20240821_20250723

--pre gives the two pre-event pairs (summer, 12/24 days), --co the "event" pair. There is no real destructive event, so: the first command is a null test (another pair of the same season); the second is a seasonal pseudo-event (336 days, across winter). Measured results (with the standard estimator looks, details in the release notes): 2 % exceed the quantile threshold, about 0.36 % remain on the map after despeckling; but in both cases the map concentrates on coherent urban targets rather than vegetation: in C-band 12/24 day summer pairs, fields and woodland are already decorrelated before the event, there is no coherence left to lose, so the land-cover-map failure mode the review expected does not appear on this data. The null test is not pure noise either: the 48 day event pair is itself more decorrelated than the 12/24 day pre-event pairs, and a fixed threshold z ≥ 3 flags about 5 %. Products: ccd_delta (coherence drop), ccd_z (standardised by the spread between the pre-event pairs, positive = drop), dpm (1 = significant drop, 0 = none, 255 = masked where pre-event coherence < 0.3), and the geocoded geo_ccd, geo_dpm. An artificially injected 200 m damage block is detected (test tests/test_ccd.py, precision and recall ≥ 0.9 under looks). The trade-off between the two coherence recipes: the 5-row azimuth window of slc-box is larger than 2 looks, neighbouring multilook pixels share samples, ccd_z is spatially correlated (Moran's I about 0.37 in the null test, < 0.1 under looks), and the edge of the damage block gets an extra ring of flagged pixels (recall still 1, precision about 0.72): small bias but blurred boundaries; looks pixels are independent of each other with crisp boundaries, slightly more bias at low coherence. For damage mapping localisation matters more than bias, so pipeline ccd and the GUI's CCD workflow default to looks (DInSAR still defaults to slc-box). If CCD reads slc-box coherence, the log records a W106 note; to use it anyway, add --recipe slc-box explicitly (a freshly computed coherence step should get a --tag so the two sets of results coexist).

docs.title: Step 12: Amplitude change (log-ratio and RGB)
docs.text:
bosar run walk amplitude --step-id amplitude_crop --stack crop_indy_downtown_crop --looks 2,10
bosar run walk log_ratio --step-id log_ratio_20240821_20250723 --requires amplitude_crop --pre 20240821 --post 20250723
bosar run walk rgb_composite --step-id rgb_20240821_20250723 --requires amplitude_crop --pre 20240821 --post 20250723
bosar run walk geocode --step-id geocode_log_ratio_20240821_20250723 --requires amplitude_crop --requires log_ratio_20240821_20250723 --source log_ratio

The GAMMA stack has no radiometric calibration, so amplitude change is relative: each date is first normalised on "stable scatterers" (the 95 % of pixels with the lowest amplitude dispersion), then 10·log10(I_post/I_pre) is computed (positive = brighter). In the RGB composite red = pre, green and blue = post: red means darkening, cyan brightening, grey unchanged. The calibration look-up tables (σ⁰) can already be read straight from the original zips (all 33 zips readable) and are used in the native SAFE workflow of v0.2.0.

docs.title: Step 13: Export (clipped to 500 m either side of the highways)
docs.text:
bosar export walk all --aoi "$DATA\04_GIS\indianapolis_highways.geojson" --buffer-m 500 --out walk\export
Get-Content walk\export\README.txt -TotalCount 25

Each geocoded product is written as a cloud-optimised GeoTIFF (COG) with nodata beyond 500 m from the highways; the vectors (product extent, reference point, AOI, stack footprint) go into one GeoPackage; README.txt and export.json state each file's units, sign convention, reference point, date pair and run id.

docs.title: Step 14: Where the logs are and how to read them
docs.text:
bosar logs walk --tail 3
Get-ChildItem walk\logs -Name | Select-Object -Last 3

Each run writes one logs\run_*.jsonl (one JSON record per line, UTC time to the microsecond, with parameters, inputs, outputs, duration, peak memory), next to a human-readable .log and a Markdown report .md. bosar logs walk --failure shows the cause and hint of the most recent failure.

docs.title: Step 15: GACOS request card and validation of existing files
docs.text:
bosar aux gacos-request walk --stack gamma_01_IW2
bosar aux gacos-check walk --stack gamma_01_IW2 --dir "$DATA\05_Auxiliary\00_GACOS"

GACOS has no API: the software computes from the project what to type into the gacos.net form, the extent (N/W/E/S), the time (23:40 UTC, from the SAFE startTime, not the halved 11:50 in the SNAP-exported par), the dates (at most 20 per request, so the 29 go in two batches); you submit the form, and once the e-mail arrives you put the .ztd/.rsc files into walk\aux\gacos\ and validate them with gacos-check. All 29 dates already present in <data-root> pass (time difference 0.4 min, edge margin 0.10°, no missing values). The tropospheric correction itself is added in v0.2.0.

docs.title: Step 16: The graphical interface
docs.text:
Start the GUI from the same PowerShell window (the virtual environment and dev_env.ps1 are both in effect):

bosar gui walk

You can also run bosar-gui walk directly (the launcher without a console window). This step is not executed by the automated check above, because the window stays open; closing the window ends it. The interface settings (theme, recent projects, SNAPHU path, and so on) live in the INI file pointed to by $env:BOSAR_CONFIG_DIR (in the development environment that is .cache\config inside the repository); nothing is written to the registry.

The GUI does no computation of its own: every action is one bosar … command, shown in the command bar at the bottom of the window, which can be copied to PowerShell with one click; the results are exactly those of steps 6–15 above. Processing runs in a separate process, and the interface reads the same project.json and logs\run_*.jsonl.

  • Project: create / open a project; the summary card lists the data stacks, step status and the disk usage of each product level.
  • Check: the preflight of step 4, grouped by system / GPU / dependencies / programs / credentials / network / project, in green, yellow and red.
  • Data: dataset table, baseline table (Δt and B⊥ coloured by threshold), baseline network plot, stack footprints on a Natural Earth basemap, and the amplitude image of a date when it is selected; drag a stack folder in to import it (step 8).
  • Run: pick a workflow (DInSAR / CCD / amplitude change) and the pairs; the parameter form is generated automatically from each step's parameter definition (common items on top, the rest under "Advanced"); the command about to run is shown live on the right. Run starts it, Stop first requests cancellation (the current step is recorded as cancelled) and, if nothing has stopped within 5 seconds, ends the whole process tree (including SNAPHU).

  • View: the product tree on the left, two linked image views on the right; colour tables are fixed per product type (coherence grey 0–1, displacement symmetric red-blue in mm, red = toward the satellite); the full-resolution value, unit and lat/lon are shown under the mouse; the damage proxy map can be overlaid, and export is available (the bosar export of step 13).

  • Logs: one row per run; the record table can be filtered by level / event / step / text; a failed run shows a failure card: WHAT (error code and message), WHERE (step, code location, file), HINT (what to do), LOG (log file and line number).

  • Aux: the GACOS request card of step 15, with a copy button on every field; "Copy request k" copies one batch of dates in the order of the website form; the folder holding the files is re-validated automatically whenever it changes. The orbit and DEM cards are enabled in v0.2.0.
  • Settings (gear icon, top right): theme (dark / light / follow system), compute device (auto / CPU / GPU), SNAPHU path, storage mode for new projects, read-only data directory; credentials only show whether they exist, never their content.

docs.title: Step 17: Account credentials
docs.text:
Credentials enter by two routes only: bosar auth set <service> in the terminal (hidden input, or --from-file yourfile.txt, the file is read once and not copied), or in the GUI Settings → Credentials → Set… (which first prompts you to register, explains where to find the key, then lets you type it or "import from file"). The value is stored in the system credential store (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain) and never appears on the command line, in logs or in release packages. To see the status:

bosar auth status
bosar auth services

None of the downloads used in these steps need an account: orbits come from local folders and the SNAP cache, with the ASF public mirror for what is missing; the DEM comes from the AWS public bucket. A cdse (Copernicus Data Space) account is an optional faster source.

docs.title: Step 18: Orbit files: local first, then download
docs.text:
bosar fetch orbits walk --stack crop_indy_downtown_crop --local-dir <data-root>/05_Auxiliary/03_Orbits --no-download

For each date one POEORB covering the acquisition time (±60 s) is chosen (RESORB only when there is none), looked up first in --local-dir (recorded in project.json), BOSAR_ORBIT_DIRS and the SNAP cache ~/.snap/auxdata/Orbits/Sentinel-1; a file found there is referenced in place with its sha256 recorded; drop --no-download and the missing dates are downloaded to walk/aux/orbits/. The project has two stacks (the crop and the full frame), so --stack is required; all 5 dates of this crop are hits locally, 0 downloads.

docs.title: Step 19: DEM: local tile mosaic, ellipsoidal height by default
docs.text:
bosar fetch dem walk --stack crop_indy_downtown_crop --tile-dir <data-root>/05_Auxiliary/02_DEM/tiles --no-download

Finds the 1°×1° GLO-30 tiles for the stack footprint plus 0.1°; when all are present locally they are mosaicked directly (no network) and written to walk/aux/dem/glo30_<W>_<S>_<E>_<N>.tif with a .json of the same name (which tiles were used, sha256, geoid model). The default is ellipsoidal height (GLO-30 is EGM2008 orthometric; the program adds the geoid undulation, here about −33 m); --height orthometric keeps the orthometric height.

docs.title: Step 20: Quick coherence preview and baselines from orbits
docs.text:
bosar data preview walk --pair 20240821_20240914
bosar data baselines walk --stack crop_indy_downtown_crop --from-orbits

The preview gives a coarse coherence map of one pair in a few seconds (walk/preview/coh_<pair>.tif, with Δt and B⊥); in the GUI, select a pair on the Data page and press Preview coherence. --from-orbits uses the orbits of step 18 to compute B⊥/B∥ on a 10×10 grid of targets, compares them pair by pair with the TCN values in .base, and fills in the pairs that have no .base (method orbit). The 4 pairs of the crop all differ by less than 3 m; the same command on the full stack gamma_01_IW2 (29 epochs) gives 21 of 25 pairs within 1 m.

docs.title: Step 21: GACOS atmospheric correction (--tropo gacos)
docs.text:
bosar pipeline dinsar walk --stack crop_indy_downtown_crop --pair 20240821_20240914 --looks 2,10 --backend snaphu --tropo gacos --gacos-dir <data-root>/05_Auxiliary/00_GACOS --tag gacos

One extra step tropo_gacos after unwrap: each pixel is sampled bilinearly on the ZTD grids of the two dates, divided by the cosine of that pixel's incidence angle to give the slant delay, φ_tropo = 4π/λ (S_sec − S_ref) (a larger delay on the secondary = longer range = positive phase), unw_tropo = unw − φ_tropo (the reference point stays 0), and displacement switches to unw_tropo. The step summary gives the displacement RMS on coherent pixels before and after the correction (this pair 6.25 → 5.09 mm; the same pair on the full IW2 30.2 → 22.3 mm).
