bosar gpu install --no-ctk     # CuPy only, when a CUDA 12 toolkit is installed system-wide
bosar preflight --offline      # the GPU row shows the device; the plug-in row says "ok"
bosar gpu status / remove

No pip is needed: Bosar resolves the wheels itself, checks their SHA-256 and unpacks them under your user data folder. BOSAR_FORCE_CPU=1 runs on the CPU even with the plug-in present.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text: What Where Settings an INI file under your user config folder (shown at the bottom of the Settings page) Credentials (Earthdata, Copernicus, OpenTopography, CDS) the operating system's credential store; Bosar never shows, logs or copies them Projects wherever you create them (bosar project new <folder>) — products, logs and project.json inside The GPU plug-in <user data folder>/bosar/plugins/cupy Licence texts _internal/licenses/ inside the installation; the About card of the Settings page

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: Windows: Settings → Apps → Bosar → Uninstall (or the Start-menu entry). macOS: drag Bosar.app to the bin. Projects, settings and the GPU plug-in are left in place; delete them yourself if you no longer need them.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
The reference is rendered from the docstrings (mkdocstrings). The layering is the one of the architecture notes: core is pure NumPy/SciPy on the array module xp (NumPy or CuPy), never touches Qt, the network or the project file; pipeline wraps every operation as a Step run by the Runner; data reads sensors and rasters; cli and gui are thin clients.

  • core — interferograms, coherence, filtering, unwrapping, geocoding, SBAS, PS/DS, ionosphere, troposphere, offsets, speckle, tiling.
  • pipeline — the step registry, the runner, the project products, the planning of a chain, the auxiliary-data fetchers.
  • data and readers — rasters, the project model, Sentinel-1 SAFE, ALOS CEOS, ENVISAT/ERS, NISAR, GAMMA/StaMPS exports, orbits, GACOS, IONEX.

Numerical conventions (hold everywhere): SI units internally — metres, seconds, radians; velocities stored in m/yr; temporal baselines in integer days; an interferogram is reference * conj(secondary); positive LOS displacement means motion toward the sensor; pixel coordinates are integer (row, col) with the pixel centre at the integer index.

docs.title: API — core
docs.text: Pure NumPy/SciPy kernels on the array module xp (bosar.backends.get_array_module()); the same code runs on CuPy when a CUDA device is present and BOSAR_FORCE_CPU is unset.

docs.title: bosar.core.interferogram
docs.text:
Interferogram formation, power and multilooking — pure xp kernels (ARCHITECTURE §5, §6.3).

Conventions (core/conventions.py): cpx_ifg = ref * conj(sec), phase = angle(cpx_ifg); a range increase from reference to secondary (motion away from the sensor) gives positive phase. Multilooking averages the complex product or the power over (azimuth, range) look blocks — never wrapped phases. Units: looks and shapes in pixels; the caller carries the spacing. Every kernel runs unchanged on NumPy or CuPy (xp).

docs.title: form_interferogram
docs.text:
form_interferogram(
    cpx_ref: Any, cpx_sec: Any, xp: ModuleType
) -> Any

cpx_ref * conj(cpx_sec) as complex64 (the binding sign convention).

Units: complex amplitudes in; the phase of the result is radians.

docs.title: power
docs.text:
power(cpx: Any, xp: ModuleType) -> Any

|z|² as float32 (the SLC power an amplitude product or a coherence denominator needs).

Units: the SLC amplitude squared (|z|^2), float32.

docs.title: multilook_shape
docs.text:
multilook_shape(
    shape: tuple[int, int], looks: tuple[int, int]
) -> tuple[int, int]

Output shape of :func:multilook: (rows // la, cols // lr) (ragged edge dropped).

Units: pixels.

docs.title: multilook
docs.text:
multilook(
    block: Any,
    looks: tuple[int, int],
    xp: ModuleType,
    *,
    reduce: str = "mean",
) -> Any

Block-average block over looks = (azimuth, range) pixels.

reduce="mean": complex input is averaged coherently (complex64 out), real input as float32 with NaNs ignored inside a block; reduce="power": |z|² (or the real values) averaged → float32. A ragged edge that does not fill a whole block is dropped (:func:multilook_shape).

Units: looks and shapes in pixels; values keep the input's units (power = |z|^2).

docs.title: fringe_frequency
docs.text:
fringe_frequency(
    cpx_ifg: Any,
    xp: ModuleType,
    *,
    looks: tuple[int, int] = (2, 2),
    pad_to: int = 1024,
) -> tuple[float, float, float]

Dominant fringe frequency (f_azimuth, f_range, peak_share) of an interferogram block.

The block is multilooked by looks (complex sum), reduced to unit phasors, zero-padded to at least pad_to per axis and Fourier transformed; the frequencies of the power peak are returned in cycles per full-resolution pixel (signed: exp(+j 2 pi f x)), with the share of the spectral power in that bin. A mean of pixel-to-pixel phasors is NOT used: on real SLC pairs it is dominated by pixel-scale phase structure.

Units: frequencies in cycles per pixel of the input grid; peak share dimensionless.

docs.title: bosar.core.coherence
docs.text:
Window coherence estimator (ARCHITECTURE §6.4) — pure xp, one implementation for CPU/GPU.

γ = |Σ ref·conj(sec)| / sqrt(Σ|ref|² · Σ|sec|²) over an (azimuth, range) window, computed with uniform_filter on the real part, the imaginary part and the two powers. The numerator is the (flattened) interferogram: on the SNAP export it is the .diff, the denominators the two rslc powers, all on the same grid (full resolution or multilooked). Output float32 in [0, 1].

Two named recipes:

  • looks: the standard estimator over the multilook block — the multilooked interferogram divided by the square root of the product of the two block-mean powers, i.e. coherence(ifg_ml, pow_ml_ref, pow_ml_sec, window=(1, 1)); looks_az × looks_rg samples per value. An extra box on the looked grid (coh_smooth) is the same call with window=(a, b).
  • slc-box (the Step default since v0.1.0): the author's compute_coherence (01_Projects/00_PhD_Prelim_Exam/00_Code/05_utils/gamma_utils.py): a box (5 × 5) uniform_filter on ref·conj(sec) and the two powers at full resolution (mode="reflect"), then the block mean of that coherence over the looks (his snaphu_batch_unwrap.py multilooks the 5 × 5 coherence before writing MintPy's .cor). About 25 samples per value whatever the looks.

docs.title: halo_for_window
docs.text:
halo_for_window(window: tuple[int, int]) -> tuple[int, int]

Rows/cols a tile must be grown by so the window estimate is exact inside the tile.

Units: pixels.

docs.title: coherence
docs.text:
coherence(
    cpx_ifg: Any,
    pow_ref: Any,
    pow_sec: Any,
    window: tuple[int, int],
    xp: ModuleType,
    *,
    ndi: ModuleType | None = None,
) -> Any

Coherence magnitude of cpx_ifg given the two SLC powers, over window pixels.

All three inputs share one grid; mode="reflect" at the array edge, so callers tile with :func:halo_for_window. Pixels whose denominator is 0 (nodata margins) get coherence 0.

Units: dimensionless coherence in [0, 1]; window in pixels; powers = |z|^2.

docs.title: expected_coherence_magnitude
docs.text:
expected_coherence_magnitude(
    gamma: float, looks: int
) -> float

First-order expectation of the estimator for true coherence gamma and looks independent samples: sqrt(γ² + (1 − γ²) / L) (the bias the synthetic tests assert).

Units: dimensionless (coherence), looks = number of samples.

docs.title: bosar.core.filtering
docs.text:
Goldstein–Werner adaptive phase filter (ARCHITECTURE §6.5) — pure xp, batched FFTs.

Goldstein & Werner (1998): every patch × patch block of the complex interferogram is Fourier-transformed, its spectrum is multiplied by the smoothed spectral magnitude raised to alpha (|S|^α, α ∈ [0, 1]) and transformed back; overlapping patches (50 %) are blended with a 2-D Hann window. The coherence-adaptive variant (Baran et al. 2003) uses α = 1 − mean coherence of the patch. Output: complex64 of the input shape; the phase is the filtered phase, the magnitude is scaled by the spectral weight (use the phase or normalise).

docs.title: halo_for_patch
docs.text:
halo_for_patch(patch: int) -> tuple[int, int]

Rows/cols a tile must be grown by so the blended result is exact inside the tile.

Units: pixels.

docs.title: goldstein
docs.text:
goldstein(
    cpx_ifg: Any,
    xp: ModuleType,
    *,
    alpha: float = 0.5,
    patch: int = 64,
    step: int | None = None,
    smooth: int = 3,
    coherence: Any | None = None,
    adaptive: bool = False,
    fft: ModuleType | None = None,
    ndi: ModuleType | None = None,
) -> Any

Filter a complex interferogram block; returns complex64 of the same shape.

patch pixels square, step (default patch // 2 = 50 % overlap), smooth = side of the box that smooths the spectral magnitude (odd, 1 disables), alpha the exponent. With adaptive=True and a coherence array of the same shape, each patch uses α = clip(1 − mean(coherence), 0, 1) instead of alpha. NaN/zero pixels contribute zero power (a nodata margin is not filtered into its neighbours' phase more than a zero).

Units: complex interferogram in/out (phase in radians); patch, step, smooth in pixels.

docs.title: phase_consistency
docs.text:
phase_consistency(
    cpx: Any,
    window: tuple[int, int],
    xp: ModuleType,
    *,
    ndi: ModuleType | None = None,
) -> Any

|mean(z)| / mean(|z|) over window — the spatial phase consistency of a single interferogram in [0, 1] (rises when a filter removes phase noise). float32.

Units: dimensionless [0, 1]; window in pixels.

docs.title: bosar.core.flatten
docs.text:
Simulated flat-earth + topographic phase from orbits and a DEM.

For a coregistered pair on the reference grid, the raw interferogram S_a · conj(S_b) carries the geometric phase 4π (r_b − r_a) / λ (SLC phase −4π r / λ, core/conventions.py), where r_a, r_b are the zero-Doppler slant ranges of the ground point seen from the two orbits. Removing it (· exp(−j φ_sim)) gives the flattened, topography-corrected interferogram - Bosar's own version of the .diff of an export, built from the precise orbits, the v0.2.0 geometry kernels and the ellipsoidal heights in radar coordinates.

The range difference is smooth in the image and nearly linear in the target height, so it is evaluated exactly (rdr2geo on the grid orbit, geo2rdr on the other orbits) on a coarse lattice at two heights and expanded per pixel as

Δr(row, col, h) = Δr₀(row, col) + s(row, col) · (h − h₀)

with bilinear interpolation of Δr₀ and the height sensitivity s (the per-pixel, range-dependent height-to-phase factor - never a scene constant). Everything is float64 until the final phasor: Δr reaches hundreds of metres and the phase needs sub-millimetre precision.

docs.title: RangeModel dataclass
docs.text:
RangeModel(
    rows: ndarray,
    cols: ndarray,
    range0_m: ndarray,
    slope_m_per_m: ndarray,
    h0_m: float,
)

Slant range of one date on the reference grid, on a coarse lattice.

rows / cols are the lattice pixel coordinates (float64, increasing); range0_m the zero-Doppler slant range [m] from the date's orbit to the ground point of each lattice node at the height h0_m; slope_m_per_m its derivative with respect to the target height [m per m]. For the grid (reference) date range0_m is the pixel's own slant range and the slope is zero.

docs.title: range_model
docs.text:
range_model(
    orbit_grid: Orbit,
    orbit_date: Orbit | None,
    az_time_s: Any,
    slant_range_m: Any,
    rows: Any,
    cols: Any,
    *,
    h0_m: float = 0.0,
    dh_m: float = 200.0,
    side: str = "right",
    doppler_grid: Any | None = None,
    doppler_date: Any | None = None,
    wavelength_m: float | None = None,
) -> RangeModel

The :class:RangeModel of one date.

orbit_grid is the orbit the image grid belongs to (the coregistration reference); orbit_date the orbit of the date (None = the grid date itself). az_time_s (nr values, seconds after orbit_grid.epoch) and slant_range_m (nc values, metres) are the azimuth time and slant range of the lattice rows / cols [px] on the grid. h0_m and dh_m [m] set the two ellipsoidal heights of the expansion.

doppler_grid / doppler_date (the stripmap chain): the Doppler centroid polynomials [Hz of slant range] of the grid and of the date for products in native (squinted) geometry - the grid's goes into rdr2geo, the date's into geo2rdr, so the range difference is the one between the two squinted lines of sight, the phase a coregistered squinted pair carries (ISCE2 stripmapApp: geo2rdr with the secondary's Doppler, resamp_slc flattening with its range offsets). Both need wavelength_m [m]; None is zero-Doppler and leaves the model of v0.2.0–v0.3.0 unchanged.

Units: seconds, metres and pixels in; metres and m/m in the model.

docs.title: simulated_phase
docs.text:
simulated_phase(
    model_a: RangeModel,
    model_b: RangeModel,
    height_m: Any,
    wavelength_m: float,
    row0: int,
    col0: int,
    xp: ModuleType = np,
) -> Any

φ_sim = 4π (r_b − r_a) / λ [rad, float64] for the window whose first pixel is (row0, col0) and whose shape is that of height_m (ellipsoidal heights [m]; NaN or non-finite heights are treated as h0).

Units: metres and pixels in; radians out.

docs.title: flatten
docs.text:
flatten(
    cpx_raw: Any, phase_sim_rad: Any, xp: ModuleType = np
) -> Any

cpx_raw · exp(−j φ_sim) as complex64 (the phase is reduced modulo 2π in float64 first, so the float32 phasor keeps its precision).

Units: complex64 interferogram and radians in; complex64 out.

docs.title: bosar.core.unwrap
docs.text:
Phase unwrapping backends (ARCHITECTURE §6.5): SNAPHU binary, snaphu-py, scikit-image.

The discovery of the binary/package is the caller's job (preflight.checks_binaries; the Step passes exe); this module works on in-memory arrays and an explicit backend. SNAPHU raw I/O: float32 in native byte order, INFILEFORMAT FLOAT_DATA (wrapped phase in radians), CORRFILEFORMAT FLOAT_DATA (coherence 0..1), OUTFILEFORMAT FLOAT_DATA (unwrapped radians), connected components UCHAR. The config/raw-file adapter follows the idea of snaphu-py (isce-framework, BSD-3 / Apache-2.0); nothing was copied. scikit-image's unwrap_phase (Herráez et al. 2002, BSD-3) is the licence-free fallback.

docs.title: COMPONENT_MODES module-attribute
docs.text:
COMPONENT_MODES = ('tile', 'regrow', 'reoptimize')

How a tiled SNAPHU run labels connected components:

  • tile — SNAPHU's tile-mode assembly: components are grown per tile and renumbered by size; a region is never merged across a tile border (a coherent ramp over 2 x 2 tiles = 4 labels).
  • regrow — a second SNAPHU invocation on the tiled result with UNWRAPPED_IN TRUE and REGROWCONNCOMPS TRUE: the components are grown once over the whole image from the unwrapped phase and the same costs (no optimisation), so labels are full-image.
  • reoptimize — SNAPHU's SINGLETILEREOPTIMIZE TRUE: the tiled solution initialises a second, single-tile optimisation of the whole image, whose components are full-image. With one tile all three are the same run.

Run the SNAPHU executable on raw files written under workdir; returns the result.

NaN phase pixels are written as 0 with coherence 0 (SNAPHU has no nodata); they are set back to NaN in the output. A non-zero exit raises E500 with the tail of SNAPHU's output. The child's peak resident set is sampled while it runs (UnwrapResult.peak_rss_mb). conncomp=False does not ask SNAPHU for connected components (the caller derives them). Until v0.1.0 the dispatcher did so for tiled runs on Windows: SNAPHU 2.0.6 died with "Out of memory" while assembling tile components when the first two tiles had none - on every platform, not only Windows (probe p18); SNAPHU 2.0.7 (built since v0.2.0) fixes it. component_mode (:data:COMPONENT_MODES) chooses how a tiled run labels its components; regrow costs a second SNAPHU pass (REGROWCONNCOMPS) whose wall time is reported separately and whose peak RSS is folded into peak_rss_mb.

docs.title: bosar.core.geometry
docs.text:
Range–Doppler geometry: rdr2geo and geo2rdr on the WGS84 ellipsoid.

Zero-Doppler convention (Sentinel-1 TOPS/IW products are deskewed to zero Doppler): a target X imaged at azimuth time t and slant range R satisfies

  • (X − S(t)) · V(t) = 0 (zero Doppler: the line of sight is normal to the velocity)
  • |X − S(t)| = R (range sphere)
  • X on the ellipsoid inflated by the target height h: x²/(a+h)² + y²/(a+h)² + z²/(b+h)² = 1 (the usual approximation for h ≪ a; sub-millimetre for the round trip, and the DEM height is then the ellipsoidal height of the target).

rdr2geo solves the three equations with Newton's method in ECEF (vectorised 3 × 3 solves), starting from a spherical-Earth guess on the requested side; geo2rdr solves the Doppler equation for t with Newton and reads R off the distance. Both are xp-agnostic and tiled by the caller (arrays of any shape). Units: seconds, metres, radians inside; degrees only in the lat/lon outputs, as the product layers store them.

Doppler centroid (the stripmap chain): a product focused in its native (squinted) geometry - ALOS-1 PALSAR L1.1 - places a target at the azimuth time where the line of sight carries the Doppler centroid f_dc(R) [Hz], not where it is normal to the velocity. Both kernels take doppler (f_dc as a function of slant range: a callable or a polynomial object with r0_m / coeffs, as bosar.data.stripmap.DopplerPolynomial) and wavelength_m; the azimuth equation becomes

2 (V · (X − S)) / (λ |X − S|) = f_dc(R)        (zero-Doppler: f_dc = 0)

Sign. X − S points from the sensor to the target, so f_dc > 0 means the target lies ahead of the zero-Doppler plane (the beam squints forward, the sensor closes in: a positive Doppler shift). This is ISCE2 zerodop/geo2rdr (fn = dot(dr, satv) − 0.5 wvl f_dc(r) r, dr = xyz − satx) with the sign of its Doppler polynomial (dopplerVsPixel from the sensor readers, Hz), and zerodop/topozero (dopfact = 0.5 wvl f_dc r / |v| as the along-track component of the line of sight). doppler=None or an all-zero polynomial is the zero-Doppler code path of v0.2.0–v0.3.0, bit for bit.

References: Curlander & McDonough (1991) §8; ISCE2 geometryLib (Apache-2.0; re-implemented).

docs.title: rdr2geo
docs.text:
rdr2geo(
    orbit: Orbit,
    az_time_s: Any,
    slant_range_m: Any,
    h_m: Any,
    xp: ModuleType = np,
    *,
    side: str = "right",
    iterations: int = 12,
    tol_m: float = 0.0001,
    doppler: Any | None = None,
    wavelength_m: float | None = None,
) -> tuple[Any, Any, Any]

Radar coordinates → (lat_deg, lon_deg, h_m) of the target.

Units: seconds, metres, metres in; degrees, degrees, metres out.

az_time_s are seconds after orbit.epoch; slant_range_m and h_m (ellipsoidal height of the target) broadcast against it. side is the look side ("right" for Sentinel-1). Newton iterations stop when every update is below tol_m.

doppler: the Doppler centroid f_dc(r) [Hz] of the image as a function of slant range (see the module docstring for the sign); it needs wavelength_m [m]. None, or a polynomial whose coefficients are all zero, is the zero-Doppler solve (bit-identical to the kernel without the argument).

docs.title: geo2rdr
docs.text:
geo2rdr(
    orbit: Orbit,
    lat_deg: Any,
    lon_deg: Any,
    h_m: Any,
    xp: ModuleType = np,
    *,
    t_guess_s: Any | None = None,
    iterations: int = 20,
    tol_s: float = 1e-09,
    doppler: Any | None = None,
    wavelength_m: float | None = None,
) -> tuple[Any, Any]

Geodetic target → (az_time_s, slant_range_m) of its position in the image.

Units: degrees, degrees, metres in; seconds and metres out.

Newton on f(t) = (X − S(t)) · V(t) with f' = −|V|² + (X − S) · A (A from the interpolant's velocity slope). t_guess_s (default: the middle of the orbit's span) must lie within the state vectors; the iteration stays inside them.

doppler: the Doppler centroid f_dc(r) [Hz] as a function of slant range (needs wavelength_m [m]): f(t) = (X − S) · V − g(r) r with g = λ f_dc / 2 and r = |X − S|, whose derivative gains (g / r + g') (X − S) · V (ISCE2 geo2rdr: fnprime = c1 + c2 dopfact). None or an all-zero polynomial: the zero-Doppler solve, bit-identical to the kernel without the argument.

docs.title: bosar.core.geocode
docs.text:
Radar → map geocoding through the importer geometry (ARCHITECTURE §6.3), CPU only.

Given the lat / lon layers of a radar-coded product (the GAMMA export's geo/ layers or the SAFE geolocation grid, multilooked like the product), the inverse mapping (lat, lon) → (row, col) is a 2-D polynomial fitted by least squares on a sub-sample of the grid; the output map grid (EPSG:4326, north-up, one posting) is sampled with scipy.ndimage.map_coordinates (bilinear for continuous rasters, nearest for masks / integer data). Pixels whose predicted radar coordinate falls outside the product are nodata. GDAL "area" geotransform semantics apply here and only here: the transform's origin is the outer corner of the first output pixel; radar pixel centres are the integer indices.

docs.title: bosar.core.baselines
docs.text:
Baselines from orbits: the TCN components and B⊥ / B∥ of a pair at a target.

For a ground point X (lat, lon, h) seen by the reference at zero-Doppler time t_ref: S_ref = orbit_ref(t_ref); the secondary's zero-Doppler time t_sec comes from :func:bosar.core.geometry.geo2rdr on the secondary orbit; the baseline is B = S_sec(t_sec) − S_ref(t_ref). Its TCN frame is GAMMA's, verified against the author's .base values: T along the reference velocity, N the geocentric up direction (from the Earth's centre through the satellite), C = T × N (the right-hand side seen from above: north × up = east on an ascending pass). With the look angle θ between nadir and the line of sight, B⊥ = B_C cos θ − B_N sin θ and B∥ = B_C sin θ + B_N cos θ — the projection bosar.data.model applies to the .base values, so both routes are comparable.

Units: seconds, degrees, metres in; metres and radians out.

docs.title: bosar.core.sbas.network
docs.text:
Small-baseline network design (ARCHITECTURE §6.7).

Pure Python + NumPy. Dates are YYYYMMDD strings; per-date B-perp values are relative to the stack reference (bperp[ref] = 0), so the baseline of a pair (i, j) is b_j - b_i [m] and its temporal baseline t_j - t_i [days]. A pair is selected when it satisfies the Δt / |B⊥| limits or is one of the k_nearest sequential connections of a date (each date is linked to its k nearest neighbours in time, which keeps the network connected across a gap); everything else is rejected with the reason. The design reports the graph components (every date must be reachable for one inversion) and the redundancy (pairs per date).

Algorithm references: Berardino et al. (2002); MintPy select_network (GPL - re-implemented, not copied).

docs.title: bosar.core.sbas.invert
docs.text:
SBAS network inversion.

Small-baseline inversion after Berardino, Fornaro, Lanari & Sansosti (2002, IEEE TGRS 40(11)): the unknowns are the mean phase velocities of the N - 1 intervals between consecutive acquisitions; the unwrapped phase of the pair (i, j) (dates i < j) is the sum of v_k Δt_k over the intervals it spans. With per-pixel pair masks and weights the normal equations (Aᵀ W A) v = Aᵀ W d are solved for every pixel at once through a batched eigen-decomposition; eigenvalues at the noise floor are dropped, which is the minimum-norm (SVD) solution when the pixel's network splits into subsets (the velocity of an unobserved interval is then zero, Berardino's behaviour).

Conventions (core/conventions.py): every interferogram is earlier * conj(later); its unwrapped phase is positive for a range increase, so the LOS displacement toward the sensor is -λ φ / (4π). Everything here stays in radians and years; :func:phase_to_los_m converts at the end. Temporal baselines are integer days, converted with 365.25 d/yr.

Weights: the phase variance of a multilooked interferogram implied by its coherence γ and the number of looks L (Cramér-Rao bound, Rodriguez & Martin 1992): σ² = (1 - γ²) / (2 L γ²).

Temporal coherence (Pepe & Lanari 2006): |Σ_p exp(j (d_p - (A v)_p))| / P over the pairs used at the pixel - 1 for a network that closes, low where unwrapping errors remain.

DEM error (Fattahi & Amelung 2013, IEEE TGRS 51(7)): estimated in the time-series domain from the correlation of the displacement history with the perpendicular-baseline history, jointly with a polynomial deformation model.

All kernels take the array module xp (NumPy or CuPy).

docs.text:
fit_velocity(
    ts: Any, dates_days: Any, xp: ModuleType = np
) -> tuple[Any, Any]

Least-squares linear rate of a time series and its standard error.

ts N x n (any unit u), dates_days the N dates as day numbers. Returns (rate, std) in u/yr: the slope of ts = c + rate * t and its standard error sqrt(Σ r² / (N - 2) / Σ (t - t̄)²) from the fit residuals r (NaN for N < 3). NaN samples are not supported here (SBAS time series are complete per pixel).

docs.title: fit_velocity_segments
docs.text:
fit_velocity_segments(
    ts: Any,
    dates_days: Any,
    segment: Any,
    xp: ModuleType = np,
) -> tuple[Any, Any]

Linear rate of a time series whose dates fall into independent segments.

When the network of a stack splits (no pair bridges a period), the offset between the two parts of the series is unknown - the minimum-norm solution carries zero velocity across the gap. The rate is still observable inside every segment: this fits one common rate and one intercept per segment, ts = c_s + rate * t. segment holds the segment index of each of the N dates; segments with a single date contribute nothing.

Returns (rate, std) in u/yr as :func:fit_velocity (std NaN when fewer than three dates remain beyond the intercepts). Units: ts any unit u, days in.

docs.text:
estimate_dem_error(
    ts_m: Any,
    dates_days: Any,
    bperp_m: Any,
    range_m: Any,
    inc_rad: Any,
    xp: ModuleType = np,
    *,
    poly_order: int = 2,
) -> tuple[Any, Any]

DEM error from the displacement time series (Fattahi & Amelung 2013).

Model per pixel: ts(t_i) = Σ_q c_q t_i^q + g_i Δz with g_i = -B⊥_i / (r sin θ), the LOS displacement [m] a height error of 1 m produces at date i (the topographic phase 4π B⊥ Δz / (λ r sin θ) converted with -λ / (4π)). B⊥_i is the perpendicular baseline of date i relative to the reference geometry [m] (the same sign convention as the stack's baseline table); range_m and inc_rad are scalars or n arrays.

Returns (dz_m, ts_corrected_m): dz_m n float32 [m] and the time series with g_i Δz removed (N x n float32, re-referenced to its first date).

Units: metres, days and radians in; metres out.

docs.title: fit_velocity_huber
docs.text:
fit_velocity_huber(
    ts: Any,
    dates_days: Any,
    xp: ModuleType = np,
    *,
    segment: Any = None,
    c: float = 1.345,
    iterations: int = 10,
    scale_floor: float = 1e-06,
) -> tuple[Any, Any]

Robust linear rate of a time series (Huber M-estimate by IRLS) and its standard error.

Same contract as :func:fit_velocity / :func:fit_velocity_segments: ts N x n in a unit u, dates_days the N day numbers, optional segment index per date (one intercept per network part); returns (rate, std) in u/yr, float32. The residuals are weighted by Huber's function with the tuning constant c (1.345: 95 % efficiency at the Gaussian) on their MAD scale per pixel, re-estimated at every iteration, so that one atmospheric outlier date no longer pulls the rate. std is the weighted least-squares standard error with the weights of the last iteration. Falls back to the least-squares fit (NaN std) when fewer than three dates remain beyond the intercepts.

Units: ts any unit u (scale_floor in that unit) and days in; u/yr out.

A date whose atmosphere offsets the whole scene stands out at most pixels (W117). NumPy only: a summary over a sample.

docs.title: bosar.core.sbas.closure
docs.text:
Triplet phase closure.

For every closed triangle (i, j, k) of the network with pairs (i, j), (j, k), (i, k) (dates i < j < k, every interferogram earlier · conj(later)):

  • wrapped closure arg(c_ij · c_jk · conj(c_ik)) [rad] - zero for a consistent stack; a systematic non-zero value is the phase bias of multilooked interferograms (soil moisture, vegetation; Zwieback et al. 2016, De Zan et al. 2015);
  • integer closure round((u_ij + u_jk − u_ik − w) / 2π) of the unwrapped phases with the wrapped closure w removed - non-zero where at least one of the three unwrapped interferograms carries a 2π unwrapping error (Biggs et al. 2007; MintPy unwrap_error_phase_closure, GPL - re-implemented).

All kernels take the array module xp; phases are float32 radians, interferograms complex64.

docs.title: wrapped_closure
docs.text:
wrapped_closure(
    cpx_ij: Any, cpx_jk: Any, cpx_ik: Any, xp: ModuleType
) -> Any

arg(c_ij c_jk conj(c_ik)) in (−π, π]; NaN-free (0 where any input is 0).

Units: complex64 interferograms in; float32 radians out.

docs.text:
integer_closure(
    unw_ij: Any,
    unw_jk: Any,
    unw_ik: Any,
    xp: ModuleType,
    *,
    wrapped: Any | None = None,
) -> Any

Integer number of 2π cycles by which the three unwrapped phases fail to close, once the wrapped closure (the phase bias / noise part, wrapped) is removed: round((u_ij + u_jk − u_ik − w) / 2π) (Biggs et al. 2007; MintPy's integer ambiguity of the closure phase). Without wrapped the raw sum is rounded, which also counts a bias beyond ±π as an error. NaN where any input is NaN (masked / unreferenced pixels).

Units: unwrapped phases and wrapped in radians; the output is a dimensionless integer count (float32).

Statistics of one triplet: mean and RMS of the wrapped closure, fraction of pixels with a non-zero integer closure (over the finite ones).

Units: radians for the wrapped statistics, dimensionless fractions and counts otherwise.

docs.title: bosar.core.sbas.unwrap_correct
docs.text:
Unwrapping-error correction by phase closure.

Re-implemented from the paper: Yunjun, Fattahi & Amelung (2019), "Small baseline InSAR time series analysis: Unwrapping error correction and noise reduction", Computers & Geosciences 133, section 3.2 ("phase closure" method). MintPy's unwrap_error_phase_closure is GPL and was not copied.

For one pixel let u be the unwrapped phases of the P pairs, C the n_tri x P triplet matrix (+1 for the pairs (i, j) and (j, k), -1 for (i, k)) and w the wrapped closure phases. The integer closure T = round((C u - w) / 2π) is zero for a consistent stack; an unwrapping error of U_p cycles in pair p shows up in every triplet of that pair. The correction is the integer vector U that minimises the L1 norm of the misfit |C U + T|_1 (with the fewest corrections among equal misfits); the corrected phase is u + 2π U.

Millions of pixels share few distinct closure vectors T (most are all zero), so the problem is solved once per unique closure pattern:

  1. the minimum-norm start: U0 = round(-C⁺ T) with the pseudo-inverse of the (masked) closure matrix - the solution orthogonal to the null space of C, i.e. with the per-date gauge fixed and U = 0 by construction on every pair that sits in no triplet; it is accepted only when it closes every triplet exactly and is sparse (at most 3 corrected pairs, or 10 % of the pairs), the sparse answer being the assumption of the method;
  2. everything else goes to the exact L1 linear program (HiGHS), run in a process pool under a time budget in the order of the pixels a pattern covers; a pattern the budget does not reach is left uncorrected and counted;
  3. a correction that does not close its triplets exactly is never applied.

The closure constrains U only up to integer combinations of per-date cycles (adding n_j - n_i to every pair changes no triplet), and a pair in no triplet is not constrained at all: the minimum-norm choice assumes that few interferograms are wrong, which is the assumption of the method.

docs.title: closure_matrix
docs.text:
closure_matrix(
    pairs: list[tuple[str, str]],
    triplets: list[tuple[str, str, str]],
) -> np.ndarray

The n_tri x n_pair matrix C with C u = u_ij + u_jk - u_ik (int8, no units).

pairs are (date1, date2) with date1 < date2; every triplet (i, j, k) must have its three pairs in pairs (ValueError otherwise).

docs.title: solve_patterns
docs.text:
solve_patterns(
    c: ndarray,
    t_patterns: ndarray,
    valid: ndarray | None = None,
    *,
    counts: ndarray | None = None,
    budget_s: float = 900.0,
    workers: int = 0,
    max_masks: int = 256,
    sparse_max: int = 3,
    sparse_fraction: float = 0.1,
    eps: float = 0.001,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, dict[str, Any]]

Integer corrections for unique closure patterns.

docs.title: Parameters (no units; integers are 2π cycles)
docs.text:
c : n_tri x P closure matrix (:func:closure_matrix). t_patterns : n_tri x n_pat integer closures, one column per unique pattern. valid : n_tri x n_pat bool, False where a triplet is unavailable for the pattern (a pair is masked at those pixels); such triplets constrain nothing. None = all valid. counts: pixels per pattern (orders the LP budget; None = equal). budget_s: wall-clock budget of the linear programs [s]; patterns not reached stay uncorrected (n_unreached, pixels_unreached). 0 = no LP at all. workers: processes of the LP pool (0 = the CPU count minus one; 1 = in this process). max_masks: at most this many distinct masks of valid triplets get their own minimum-norm operator (the most frequent first); patterns with rarer masks go to the LP only. sparse_max, sparse_fraction: the minimum-norm start is accepted only when it corrects at most max(sparse_max, sparse_fraction * P) pairs (and closes every triplet).

Returns (U, stats): U P x n_pat int16 and the counts n_patterns, n_zero (nothing to correct), n_start_exact (minimum-norm start, exact and sparse), n_lp (sent to the program), n_lp_exact, n_unresolved (the program's answer did not close: left uncorrected), n_unreached (beyond the time budget), pixels_unreached, lp_seconds. No pattern is ever corrected by a vector that does not close its triplets.

docs.title: correct_unwrap_errors
docs.text:
correct_unwrap_errors(
    integer_closure: ndarray,
    c: ndarray,
    *,
    budget_s: float = 900.0,
    workers: int = 0,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, dict[str, Any]]

Integer cycles to add to every pair at every pixel.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
integer_closure : n_tri x n_pix float array of integer closures (2π cycles; NaN where a triplet is unavailable at the pixel, e.g. one of its pairs is masked). c : n_tri x P closure matrix.

Returns (U, stats): U is P x n_pix int16 (cycles; add 2π U to the unwrapped phase); stats adds the pixel counts n_pixels, n_pixels_nonzero (pixels with a non-zero closure before), n_pixels_corrected (closed exactly afterwards) and n_pixels_residual to the pattern counts of :func:solve_patterns.

Units: integer 2π cycles in and out (dimensionless).

docs.title: bosar.core.sbas.quality
docs.text:
Quality verdict of a time-series result.

A displacement map that is mostly noise must not look like a result. :func:assess turns the indicators a chain has measured (usable fraction, pairs kept, network connectivity, velocity spread, unclosed triplets, long-wavelength trend) into findings with a warning code, the measured value, the threshold it was held against and a concrete remedy, and into one verdict:

  • usable - no finding;
  • marginal - the result can be read only with the stated limits;
  • not_usable - the result must not be interpreted as deformation.

Pure Python: no arrays, no I/O. The thresholds are module constants so that a report can quote them; they are judgement values for C-band 12-day stacks, not physical limits.

docs.title: C_BAND_WAVELENGTH_M module-attribute
docs.text:
C_BAND_WAVELENGTH_M = (
    SPEED_OF_LIGHT_M_S / S1_CENTER_FREQUENCY_HZ
)

Sentinel-1, 5.405 GHz: 0.05547 m - the wavelength the C-band thresholds were set at.

docs.title: L_BAND_WAVELENGTH_M module-attribute

L_BAND_WAVELENGTH_M = 0.2360571

    "reference_step_marginal_mm",
    "trend_min_mm_yr",

assess(

Verdict and findings from the indicators of a time-series chain.

docs.title: bosar.core.tropo
docs.text:
Tropospheric phase from zenith delays.

Per date a zenith total delay grid ZTD(lon, lat) [m] (GACOS) is sampled bilinearly at every pixel's lat/lon and turned into the slant delay S = ZTD / cos θ with the pixel's incidence angle θ. For a pair the differential delay is a range change of the secondary relative to the reference, so with the package's sign convention (reference · conj(secondary); a range increase of the secondary is a positive phase, core/conventions.py)

φ_tropo = (4π / λ) · (S_sec − S_ref)          [rad]

and the corrected unwrapped phase is unw − φ_tropo, re-referenced at the pair's reference pixel. Kernels are xp-agnostic. Units: metres, radians; wavelength in metres; grid coordinates in degrees. Assertions at entry.

docs.title: bilinear_sample

    y_first: float,

    y: Any,
    xp: ModuleType = np,
) -> Any

Bilinear interpolation of grid[row, col] at (x, y) where column c sits at x_first + c · x_step and row r at y_first + r · y_step (ROI_PAC / GACOS .rsc convention, y_step negative for north-up). Points outside the grid get NaN.

Units: whatever the grid holds (metres for a ZTD); coordinates in degrees.

S = ZTD / cos θ — the zenith delay mapped to the line of sight. Units: metres, radians.

φ_tropo = 4π/λ · (S_sec − S_ref): a larger slant delay on the secondary is a range increase and a positive phase (core/conventions.py). Units: metres in, radians out.

docs.title: bosar.core.tropo_era5
docs.text:
Zenith tropospheric delay from pressure-level weather-model fields.

Re-implemented from the literature (no PyAPS code; PyAPS is GPL): Jolivet, Grandin, Lasserre, Doin & Peltzer (2011, GRL 38, L17311) and Doin, Lasserre, Peltzer, Cavalié & Doubre (2009, J. Appl. Geophys. 69). The refractivity of moist air (Smith & Weintraub 1953 constants)

N = k1 (P − e) / T + k2 e / T + k3 e / T²          [N-units, 1e-6]

with k1 = 0.776 K/Pa, k2 = 0.716 K/Pa, k3 = 3.75e3 K²/Pa, pressures in Pa, temperature in K and the partial pressure of water vapour e = q P / (0.622 + 0.378 q) from the specific humidity q. The one-way zenith total delay at the height h is

ZTD(h) = 1e-6 ∫_h^top N dz + 1e-6 k1 R_d / g · P_top

(the second term is the hydrostatic delay of the air above the highest level). Levels are placed at their geopotential height Φ / g0.

Everything is SI: Pa, K, kg/kg, m² s⁻² in; metres out.

docs.title: bosar.core.iono
docs.text:
Ionospheric phase by the range split-spectrum method.

The ionosphere advances the phase by an amount proportional to 1 / f (dispersive); geometry, deformation and troposphere delay it in proportion to f (non-dispersive). An interferogram made from the lower and one from the upper part of the range spectrum (centre frequencies f_L, f_H) separate the two (Gomba et al. 2016, "Toward operational compensation of ionospheric effects in SAR interferograms: the split-spectrum method", IEEE TGRS 54(3), eqs. 5-6; Brcic et al. 2010):

phi_iono(f0)    = f_L f_H / (f0 (f_H^2 - f_L^2)) * (phi_L f_H - phi_H f_L)
phi_nondisp(f0) = f0 / (f_H^2 - f_L^2) * (phi_H f_H - phi_L f_L)

with phi_L, phi_H the unwrapped sub-band phases. The sub-bands differ from the full-band phase by about phi * (f_c / f0) (a few hundredths of a radian per cycle), so only the full band is unwrapped: with d = arg(I_H conj(I_L)) the sub-band phases are phi_unw -+ d / 2 (the full band sits midway) - no second unwrapping, no 2 pi ambiguity between the sub-bands, and the estimate stays unbiased in noisy cells (tested at coherence 0.4). What the method cannot see is a phase that is flat in frequency: a constant, or the 2 pi k between regions unwrapped independently, reads as half its value.

The input must be flattened. Coregistration moves the secondary's envelope by the modelled range difference but leaves the full-band carrier phase 4 pi dR / lambda0 in both sub-bands (a sub-band radar would have seen 4 pi dR / lambda_sub). Removing the modelled geometric phase from all three interferograms (slc_flatten, same orbits and DEM as the coregistration) takes that term out identically; what remains - troposphere, deformation, orbit residuals, ionosphere - is a true, uncompensated delay or advance and carries the proper frequency dependence. Without flattening half the geometric phase would be read as ionosphere.

The estimate amplifies phase noise by about f0 / (f_H - f_L) (some 170 for Sentinel-1 IW): it is made on heavily multilooked interferograms and low-pass filtered with coherence weights (:func:lowpass_weighted); the ionosphere is smooth at the scales that survive.

Connected components. Regions unwrapped independently (SNAPHU connected components, or the separate regions scikit-image unwraps on a masked grid) differ by an unknown 2 pi k of full-band phase. Both sub-band phases inherit it, so the dispersive phase of such a region is off by k times :func:ambiguity_step_rad = 2 pi f_L f_H / (f0 (f_L + f_H)) (pi (1 - f_c^2 / f0^2), i.e. pi to 7 ppm for Sentinel-1). :func:component_constants removes each component's weighted median before the low-pass; :func:closure_residual and :func:plane_fit_components are the validation tools that are blind to those constants; :func:predicted_raw_std and :func:lowpass_noise_std predict the estimator's noise from the coherence and the looks.

Units: Hz, radians. Pure array code on xp; no I/O. Re-implemented from the papers.

docs.title: split_range_spectrum
docs.text:
split_range_spectrum(
    cpx_slc: Any,
    range_sampling_rate_hz: float,
    range_bandwidth_hz: float,
    xp: ModuleType = np,
    *,
    fraction: float = 1.0 / 3.0,
) -> tuple[Any, Any, float]

Lower and upper range sub-band images of cpx_slc (lines, samples; range along the last axis), each demodulated to baseband, and the sub-band centre offset f_c [Hz]: the sub-bands are centred at -f_c and +f_c from the carrier and fraction of the bandwidth wide (a third each by default: the outer thirds, centres at +- B / 3).

The band-pass is a raised-cosine window over the sub-band (a Hann window in frequency: low sidelobes in range, at the cost of 1.5 x the sub-band's resolution cell). The spectrum is rolled by a whole number of bins, so f_c is the value actually used. Lines are independent: the caller may pass any block of lines. complex64 out. Units: Hz.

Unwrapped sub-band phases (low, high) from the unwrapped full-band phase and the (multilooked) complex sub-band interferograms: unw_full -+ arg(I_high conj(I_low)) / 2 (the full band sits midway between the sub-bands). float64. Units: radians.

docs.text:
split_spectrum_phases(

    phi_high_rad: Any,
    f0_hz: float,
    f_low_hz: float,
    f_high_hz: float,

(dispersive, non-dispersive) phase at the carrier f0 from the unwrapped sub-band phases at f_low and f_high (absolute frequencies, Hz). Their sum is the model's phase at f0 (the full-band phase up to noise). f0 is the frequency the phases are expressed at: between the sub-bands of one band, or one of the two carriers when the "sub-bands" are two whole bands (NISAR A / B) - any positive value is a valid evaluation point of the two-term model. float64. Units: radians.

docs.title: noise_gain
docs.text:
noise_gain(
    f0_hz: float, f_low_hz: float, f_high_hz: float
) -> float

Standard deviation of the dispersive phase per unit standard deviation of the (equal, independent) sub-band phases: f_L f_H sqrt(f_L^2 + f_H^2) / (f0 (f_H^2 - f_L^2)).

docs.title: lowpass_weighted
docs.text:
lowpass_weighted(
    values: Any,
    weights: Any,
    sigma_px: tuple[float, float],
    xp: ModuleType = np,
) -> Any

Gaussian low-pass of values with weights (normalised convolution: G * (w v) / G * w); pixels with a non-finite value or a non-positive weight do not contribute and are filled from their neighbours. sigma_px: (lines, samples). The image is mirrored at its edges. NaN where no weight reaches. float32. Units: pixels.

docs.title: ambiguity_step_rad
docs.text:
ambiguity_step_rad(
    f0_hz: float, f_low_hz: float, f_high_hz: float
) -> float

Dispersive phase [rad] that a full-band offset of one cycle (2 pi) becomes.

Both sub-band phases are phi_unw -+ d / 2 (:func:subband_phases), so a 2 pi k in the unwrapped full band shifts each of them by 2 pi k; :func:split_spectrum_phases maps that to f_L f_H / (f0 (f_H^2 - f_L^2)) * 2 pi k (f_H - f_L), i.e. k times

step = 2 pi f_L f_H / (f0 (f_L + f_H))   (= pi (1 - f_c^2 / f0^2) for f_L,H = f0 -+ f_c)
  • half a cycle: two regions unwrapped independently differ by about k pi of ionosphere. Units: Hz in, radians out.

docs.title: component_constants
docs.text:
component_constants(
    raw_rad: Any,
    labels: Any,
    weights: Any,
    xp: ModuleType = np,
    *,
    min_cells: int = 1,
) -> tuple[Any, dict[int, float]]

Remove each connected component's weighted median from the raw dispersive phase.

labels: connected components of the full-band unwrapping (SNAPHU: 0 = in no component, i.e. not reliably unwrapped; 1 = the largest, ...). For every label > 0 the constant is the weighted median of raw_rad over the component's cells with a finite value and a positive weight; it is subtracted from every finite cell of the component. A component with fewer than min_cells such cells is dropped (NaN). The constants absorb the k ambiguity steps of :func:ambiguity_step_rad between components and any true ionospheric difference of their levels - only the sum is observable; the shape inside each component is kept.

Returns (corrected, {label: constant_rad}): corrected float64, NaN on label 0, dropped components and non-finite input. Units: radians; weights dimensionless (relative).

docs.title: robust_stats
docs.text:
robust_stats(
    values_rad: Any, xp: ModuleType = np
) -> dict[str, float]

n, mean, median, std, mad_std (1.4826 x the median absolute deviation from the median: the standard deviation of a Gaussian, blind to outliers) and rms (about zero) of the finite values. NaN statistics when none is finite. Units: those of the input (radians here).

docs.title: closure_residual
docs.text:
closure_residual(
    phi_ab_rad: Any,
    phi_bc_rad: Any,
    phi_ac_rad: Any,
    labels_ab: Any,
    labels_bc: Any,
    labels_ac: Any,
    xp: ModuleType = np,
    *,
    weights: Any | None = None,
    min_cells: int = 1,
) -> tuple[Any, dict[str, Any]]

Closure of the ionospheric phase of three pairs of dates a, b, c.

Each phase is that of ref * conj(sec): phi_xy = K (TEC_x - TEC_y), so a true ionospheric phase gives phi_ab + phi_bc - phi_ac = 0. Evaluated on the cells that are finite with a label > 0 in all three; one combination of the three labels (an intersection component) carries one unknown constant - each pair's component constant is uniform over the component - which is removed as the (weights-weighted) median. Intersection components with fewer than min_cells cells are dropped.

Returns (residual, stats): residual float64 with NaN elsewhere; stats holds :func:robust_stats of the residual plus n_components, largest_fraction (share of the cells in the largest intersection component) and constants_rad (largest component first, at most 50). Units: radians.

docs.title: phase_std_cramer_rao
docs.text:
phase_std_cramer_rao(
    coherence: Any, n_looks: float, xp: ModuleType = np
) -> Any

Cramer-Rao bound of the interferometric phase [rad] from n_looks independent looks at coherence g: sqrt((1 - g^2) / (2 N g^2)) (Rodriguez & Martin 1992; Bamler & Hartl 1998) - the standard deviation of the multilooked phase for large N. inf where g <= 0. float64. Units: radians; coherence dimensionless; looks = count.

docs.title: subband_independent_looks
docs.text:
subband_independent_looks(
    looks: tuple[int, int],
    range_sampling_rate_hz: float,
    range_bandwidth_hz: float,
    subband_offset_hz: float,
    *,
    fraction: float = 1.0 / 3.0,
    range_window_alpha: float = 1.0,
    azimuth_fraction: float = 1.0,
) -> float

Independent samples behind one multilooked cell of a sub-band interferogram.

Range: looks[1] * B_eq / fs with the equivalent bandwidth B_eq = (int P)^2 / int P^2 of the sub-band's power spectrum P(f) = W_full(f)^2 W_sub(f)^2 - the processed full-band window W_full = alpha + (1 - alpha) cos(2 pi f / B) on |f| <= B / 2 (Hamming; Sentinel-1 IPF: alpha 0.75, 1 = flat) times the Hann window of :func:split_range_spectrum (width fraction * B centred at subband_offset_hz). For a flat band the Hann sub-band keeps B_eq = 18/35 * fraction * B; the Hamming-0.75 taper changes that by < 0.1 % for the outer thirds (the Hann window dominates). The averaged interferogram's variance falls with L B_eq / fs for L samples spaced 1 / fs (Bamler & Hartl 1998). Azimuth: looks[0] * azimuth_fraction (the same ratio for the azimuth spectrum; Sentinel-1 IW: a 313 Hz Hamming-0.75 Doppler band sampled at 486.5 Hz gives 0.54). Units: looks = pixels, frequencies in Hz; the result is a count.

docs.title: predicted_raw_std
docs.text:
predicted_raw_std(
    coherence: Any,
    n_looks_subband: float,
    f0_hz: float,
    f_low_hz: float,
    f_high_hz: float,
    xp: ModuleType = np,
) -> Any

Predicted standard deviation [rad] of the raw (unfiltered) dispersive phase per cell: :func:noise_gain x :func:phase_std_cramer_rao (coherence, n_looks_subband).

The estimate is c [phi_unw (f_H - f_L) - d (f_H + f_L) / 2] with d = arg(I_H conj(I_L)) (:func:subband_phases); the sub-bands share no spectrum, so the noise of d is that of two independent sub-band phases and the gain is :func:noise_gain. The full-band term adds f_L f_H / (f0 (f_L + f_H)) ~ 0.5 times the full-band phase noise - below 0.1 % of the variance, neglected. The coherence of the sub-bands is taken equal to the full band's (thermal noise and decorrelation are white across the band). Units: radians; coherence dimensionless; looks = count; Hz.

docs.title: lowpass_noise_std
docs.text:
lowpass_noise_std(
    std_rad: Any,
    weights: Any,
    sigma_px: tuple[float, float],
    xp: ModuleType = np,
) -> Any

Predicted standard deviation [rad] after :func:lowpass_weighted of independent cells with standard deviations std_rad and the same weights and sigma_px.

The normalised convolution is sum k_i w_i v_i / sum k_i w_i; for independent noise its variance is sum k_i^2 w_i^2 s_i^2 / (sum k_i w_i)^2 (both sums are separable Gaussian convolutions, evaluated like the filter). With equal weights and noise this is s^2 / N_eff, N_eff = (sum k)^2 / sum k^2 ~ 4 pi sigma_az sigma_rg independent cells in the kernel; with the filter's weights g^2 / (1 - g^2) (inverse variances) it is the weighted mean's variance. Within 3 sigma of an edge the mirrored cells are counted as independent (the noise there is underestimated by up to sqrt(2)). NaN where no weight reaches. Units: radians; weights dimensionless; sigma in pixels.

docs.title: plane_fit_components
docs.text:
plane_fit_components(
    values_rad: Any,
    labels: Any,
    spacing_m: tuple[float, float],
    xp: ModuleType = np,
    *,
    weights: Any | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]

Least-squares plane with one free offset per component: v = g_az y + g_rg x + c_k.

The slopes come from the variation inside the components (each component's weighted means of y, x and v are removed first), so they are blind to the per-component constants of :func:component_constants. y, x: row and column times spacing_m (azimuth, range) [m]. Cells with a non-finite value, label <= 0 or non-positive weight are left out. Returns az_rad_per_100km, rg_rad_per_100km, span_rad (what the plane spans over the whole grid: |g_az| L_az + |g_rg| L_rg), std_rad (residual standard deviation), n and n_components; NaN slopes when the cells cannot fix a plane. Units: radians, metres.

docs.title: poly_fit_components
docs.text:
poly_fit_components(
    values_rad: Any,
    labels: Any,
    spacing_m: tuple[float, float],
    xp: ModuleType = np,
    *,
    order: int = 1,
    weights: Any | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]

Weighted least-squares polynomial of the ionospheric estimate with one free offset per component: order 1 = the plane g_az y + g_rg x, order 2 adds y^2, x y, x^2. y / x are the row / column distances from the grid centre in kilometres (spacing_m: azimuth, range), so the coefficients are in rad/km and rad/km^2 (coefficients, in the order y, x[, y^2, x y, x^2]). Like :func:plane_fit_components, each component's weighted means are removed first, so the fit is blind to the per-component constants. Returns coefficients (NaN when the cells cannot fix them), az_rad_per_100km / rg_rad_per_100km (the linear terms), span_rad (max - min of the surface over the grid), std_rad (residual standard deviation), n, n_components, order. Units: radians, metres in; rad/km, rad/km^2, radians out.

docs.title: bosar.core.ccd
docs.text:
Coherence change detection (SPEC §3.2 C): coherence loss between pre-event and co-event pairs, its z-score against the pre-event pair-to-pair variability, and the damage proxy map.

Definitions (all on one multilooked grid; xp = NumPy or CuPy):

  • gamma_pre = per-pixel median of the N pre-event coherences, gamma_co = median of the co-event coherences (one or more pairs);
  • delta = gamma_pre - gamma_co (positive = coherence loss);
  • sigma: with N >= 2 pre-event pairs, the per-pixel sample variance across the pre pairs (ddof 1) pooled over a z_window box (a few dozen degrees of freedom instead of N - 1), square-rooted and floored at sigma_floor; with N = 1 there is no pair-to-pair variability and the scene-wide robust spread of delta (1.4826 MAD over the valid pixels) is used — the summary says which (sigma_source);
  • z = delta / sigma;
  • dpm (uint8): 1 where z >= threshold and gamma_pre >= min_coh_pre, 0 elsewhere on valid pixels, 255 where masked (pre-event coherence too low to lose, or NaN); threshold is given or the quantile of z over the valid pixels; connected groups (8-neighbour) smaller than min_area_px are removed (specks).

The same statistic as Tay et al. (2020, typhoon Hagibis damage maps: z-score of the co-event coherence against the pre-event coherence statistics) and the coherence-difference damage proxy of Yun et al. (2015, ARIA); re-implemented from the definitions, no code copied.

docs.title: bosar.core.amplitude
docs.text:
Relative amplitude change on coregistered stacks (SPEC §3.2 F) — pure xp.

On the GAMMA/StaMPS export the SLCs are not radiometrically calibrated: amplitudes are compared relative to each other after a per-date normalisation that removes gain differences between acquisitions. The normalisation is estimated on stable scatterers: the pixels whose amplitude dispersion D_A = sigma_A / mu_A over the dates is below the stable_quantile (0.95: the complement of the 5 % most variable pixels; Ferretti et al. 2001 use D_A for the same purpose). Two methods:

  • stack-median: every date is scaled so that its median intensity over the stable mask equals the median of those medians over all dates;
  • reference-offset: every date is shifted in dB by the median of 10 log10(I_date / I_reference) over the stable mask (the reference keeps 0 dB).

Then amp_db = 10 log10(I); the log-ratio of a pair is 10 log10(I_post / I_pre) [dB] (positive = brighter after); the RGB composite of SPEC §3.2 F is (R, G, B) = (pre, post, post): red where the scene darkened, cyan where it brightened, grey where unchanged.

Units: intensities are powers (|z|^2, any consistent scale); D_A is dimensionless.

docs.title: bosar.core.offsets
docs.text:
Offset tracking: normalised cross-correlation (NCC) of oversampled amplitude patches.

What is measured. For every patch of a regular grid, the 2-D shift between a reference and a secondary image (amplitude only; the interferometric phase is not used), with the NCC peak, a signal-to-noise ratio and an outlier mask. Pure xp (NumPy or CuPy): the patches of a chunk go through one batched FFT, so the GPU path is the same code.

Sign convention (binding; docs/design/offsets.md §3). The offset is the position of a feature in the secondary minus its position in the reference, in (azimuth line, range sample) pixels: sec(r + d_az, c + d_rg) ≈ ref(r, c). Positive range = towards increasing slant range (a range increase, i.e. motion away from the sensor, so the LOS displacement of ARCHITECTURE §5, positive toward the sensor, is −offset_range_m); positive azimuth = towards increasing line number. :func:fourier_shift with a positive shift moves the content towards increasing indices, so a secondary built with it reads that shift back.

Algorithm (ampcor, ISCE2 components/mroipac/ampcor and contrib/PyCuAmpcor, Apache-2.0; read for the method, re-implemented in xp, no code copied):

  1. Complex patches are demodulated (:func:deramp), oversampled oversample times by FFT zero padding (:func:oversample) and only then detected (|.|). The amplitude of a complex signal has twice its bandwidth: detected at the original sampling it is aliased and the correlation peak locks to whole pixels (as 0.31 px from complex-domain oversampling). The demodulation matters for Sentinel-1 TOPS: the azimuth spectrum of a patch sweeps about 3.5 Hz per line (≈ 230 Hz over 64 lines) on top of the 327 Hz bandwidth, more than the 486 Hz PRF; local removes the per-row instantaneous frequency (lag-one correlation along azimuth, smoothed over a few rows, integrated), which also follows the Doppler jump at a burst seam. Real (amplitude) input is oversampled as it is.
  2. The mean-removed reference amplitude is correlated with the secondary search window at every lag of the oversampled grid by FFT; the NCC denominator comes from summed-area tables of the secondary (float64).
  3. Integer peak; edge when it lies less than 1 px from the border of the search area. SNR = peak² / mean(ρ²) over the search surface outside a (2e + 1)² exclusion box around the peak (ampcor: peak² over the mean ρ² around the peak; the box keeps the main lobe out).
  4. Sub-pixel: the NCC surface around the peak is interpolated with a Hann-tapered sinc on a grid corr_oversample times finer over ±1 sample, the maximum refined by a parabola. Near the search border the kernel narrows symmetrically instead of being cut on one side.
  5. :func:outlier_mask: SNR below snr_min, the peak on the search edge, or a deviation from the 3 × 3 median of the offset field above mad_k times the field's MAD.

Units: pixels for every offset, size and position; metres only through :func:offsets_m.

docs.title: bosar.core.speckle
docs.text:
Speckle filters on SAR intensity - pure xp.

Every filter works on intensity (power: |z|^2 or a calibrated backscatter coefficient, linear, float32) under the multiplicative model I = R * n with E[n] = 1 and var(n) = 1 / L; L is the equivalent number of looks (ENL) of the intensity and Cu = 1/sqrt(L) the coefficient of variation of pure speckle. The filters:

  • boxcar: the mean over a w x w window;
  • lee (Lee 1980): R = m + b (I - m), b = var_R / (m^2 Cu^2 + var_R), var_R = (var_I - m^2 Cu^2) / (1 + Cu^2), local mean m and variance var_I;
  • refined_lee (Lee 1981; Lee, Grunes & De Grandi 1999): the edge direction from the 3 x 3 sub-means of the window (four gradient masks), then the Lee estimate over the one of eight directional, non-square half windows (with the edge line) on the side of the centre;
  • frost (Frost et al. 1982): R = sum(m_k I_k) / sum(m_k), m_k = exp(-K Ci^2 d_k) with the damping factor K, the local Ci^2 = var_I / m^2 at the centre and d_k the distance [px];
  • gamma_map (Lopes, Nezry, Touzi & Laur 1990): the MAP estimate under a Gamma-distributed scene; Ci <= Cu: the mean, Ci >= Cmax (default sqrt(2) Cu): the pixel itself;
  • nlmeans (Buades, Coll & Morel 2005; the patch similarity of Deledalle, Denis & Tupin 2009): weighted mean over a search window; the weight of a candidate decreases with the generalised likelihood ratio of two Gamma-distributed patches, d = L log((a + b)^2 / (4 a b)) per pixel pair, averaged over the patch, minus its expectation under "same reflectivity".

No-data: NaN and non-positive pixels keep their value and never enter a neighbour's statistics (every local sum runs over the valid pixels only). The output at a pixel depends on the input within :func:speckle_halo pixels; every kernel pads its block symmetrically (scipy's reflect) so a core.tiling.Tiler with that halo (clipped at the image edge) reproduces the whole-image result. The ENL is a scalar input: estimate it once on the whole image (:func:estimate_enl) and pass it to every tile. Local sums are direct (correlate1d), not running sums, and accumulate in float64: a bright point target on a line does not leave rounding residue in a dark neighbour's variance.

docs.text:

docs.title: lee
docs.text:
lee(
    intensity: Any,
    xp: ModuleType,
    *,
    enl: float,
    window_px: int = DEFAULT_WINDOW_PX,
) -> Any

Lee (1980) local-statistics filter for multiplicative speckle; float32.

R = m + b (I - m), b = var_R / (m^2 / L + var_R) (Lee 1980, the gain of the linearised model I ~ R + m (n - 1)), var_R = max(var_I - m^2 / L, 0) / (1 + 1/L); m, var_I over the valid pixels of the window. b is 0 on homogeneous areas and tends to 1 on edges and point targets (the exact MMSE gain var_R / var_I of Kuan and of the refined Lee stops at 1 / (1 + 1/L), half the pixel at one look). Units: intensity (power, linear) in and out; enl dimensionless (looks); window in pixels.

docs.title: refined_lee
docs.text:
refined_lee(
    intensity: Any,
    xp: ModuleType,
    *,
    enl: float,
    window_px: int = DEFAULT_WINDOW_PX,
) -> Any

Refined Lee filter (Lee 1981; Lee, Grunes & De Grandi 1999); float32.

In the w x w window (7 in the paper) the 3 x 3 sub-means (3 x 3 pixels each, stride 2 at w = 7) give four gradients (horizontal, vertical, two diagonals); the strongest picks the edge direction, and the centre's side is the one whose outer sub-mean is closer to the centre sub-mean. The estimate m + b (I - m) of Lee et al. (1999), b = var_R / var_I, then uses the mean and variance of that directional window (one of eight half windows with the edge line, 28 pixels at w = 7). Units: intensity (power, linear) in and out; enl dimensionless; window in pixels (>= 5).

docs.title: frost
docs.text:
frost(
    intensity: Any,
    xp: ModuleType,
    *,
    window_px: int = DEFAULT_WINDOW_PX,
    damping: float = DEFAULT_DAMPING,
) -> Any

Frost et al. (1982) adaptive exponential kernel; float32.

R = sum_k m_k I_k / sum_k m_k over the valid pixels of the window, m_k = exp(-K Ci^2 d_k) with K = damping, Ci^2 = var_I / m^2 the local squared coefficient of variation at the centre and d_k the Euclidean distance to the centre. Homogeneous areas (small Ci) get a wide kernel, edges and point targets (large Ci) a narrow one. Units: intensity (power, linear) in and out; damping dimensionless; window and d_k in pixels.

docs.title: gamma_map
docs.text:
gamma_map(
    intensity: Any,
    xp: ModuleType,
    *,
    enl: float,
    window_px: int = DEFAULT_WINDOW_PX,
    cmax: float | None = None,
) -> Any

Gamma-MAP filter (Lopes, Nezry, Touzi & Laur 1990); float32.

With Cu = 1/sqrt(L), Ci = sqrt(var_I) / m and alpha = (1 + Cu^2) / (Ci^2 - Cu^2): Ci <= Cu: R = m (homogeneous); Ci >= Cmax: R = I (point target); otherwise R = ((alpha - L - 1) m + sqrt(m^2 (alpha - L - 1)^2 + 4 alpha L I m)) / (2 alpha). cmax default sqrt(2) Cu (Lopes, Touzi & Nezry 1990). Units: intensity (power, linear) in and out; enl, cmax dimensionless; window in pixels.

docs.title: glr_h0_mean
docs.text:
glr_h0_mean(enl: float) -> float

Expected per-pixel GLR dissimilarity L log((a + b)^2 / (4 a b)) of two independent L-look intensities of the same reflectivity: L (2 psi(2L) - 2 psi(L) - 2 log 2) (0.614 at L = 1, -> 0.5 for large L).

Units: dimensionless; enl in looks.

docs.title: nlmeans
docs.text:
nlmeans(
    intensity: Any,
    xp: ModuleType,
    *,
    enl: float,
    window_px: int = DEFAULT_WINDOW_PX,
    patch_px: int = DEFAULT_PATCH_PX,
    h: float = DEFAULT_H,
) -> Any

Non-local means for Gamma-distributed intensity; float32.

Every pixel q of the window_px x window_px search window around p gets the weight exp(-max(D(p, q) - mu0, 0) / h): D is the mean over the patch_px x patch_px patches of the generalised likelihood ratio of two L-look intensities (Deledalle, Denis & Tupin 2009), d(a, b) = L log((a + b)^2 / (4 a b)) (scale-invariant, >= 0, 0 for a = b), and mu0 its expectation for equal reflectivities (:func:glr_h0_mean), so h is the tolerated excess dissimilarity. The centre pixel has D = 0 and weight 1, the largest possible: with mu0 subtracted, neighbours of the same reflectivity weigh close to 1 too (Buades et al. 2005 replace the centre weight by the largest neighbour weight, which flattens point targets further). An isolated point target is one pixel of the patch_px^2 in its patch, so it is kept only when L log(ratio) / patch_px^2 exceeds h clearly: at 4 looks a 26 dB target keeps about half of its intensity (-3 dB), at one look a 30 dB target loses about 11 dB (3 x 3 patch, h = 0.5; tests/test_speckle.py measures it). R = sum w_q I_q / sum w_q; averaging intensity (not log-intensity) keeps the mean. Units: intensity (power, linear) in and out; enl, h dimensionless; windows in pixels.

docs.title: enl_window
docs.text:
enl_window(
    intensity: Any,
    xp: ModuleType,
    *,
    window: tuple[int, int, int, int] | None = None,
) -> float

mean^2 / var (unbiased variance) of the valid pixels in window = (row0, row1, col0, col1) or the whole array: the ENL of a homogeneous area. NaN when fewer than two valid pixels or a zero variance.

docs.title: estimate_enl
docs.text:
estimate_enl(
    intensity: Any,
    xp: ModuleType,
    *,
    block_px: int = 32,
    fraction: float = 0.1,
    min_blocks: int = 4,
    min_valid: float = 0.9,
) -> EnlEstimate

Automatic ENL from the most homogeneous blocks of the image.

The image is cut into block_px square blocks (at least min_valid of their pixels valid). Each block's pixels are split like a chessboard: the squared coefficient of variation CV^2 of the even half ranks the blocks, the fraction with the lowest (at least min_blocks) are kept, and ENL = 1 / mean(CV^2) of the odd half of those blocks. Ranking and estimating on disjoint pixels removes the selection bias of "the block of lowest CV" (on uncorrelated speckle the estimate is unbiased; textured blocks rank last). window is the block of lowest CV. Units: intensity (power) in; ENL in looks; block size in pixels; fractions dimensionless.

Units: intensity (power) in; ENL in looks.

edge_preservation_index(

    reference: Any,
    xp: ModuleType,

Edge-preservation index (Sattar et al. 1997): sum |F(p) - F(q)| / sum |R(p) - R(q)| over the pairs of adjacent pixels (axis 0: vertical pairs, 1: horizontal, None: both) whose two pixels are valid (finite, > 0) in both images and inside mask. reference is the noise-free image in a simulation, or the unfiltered image on real data (then values < 1 mix edge blur with removed speckle). 1 = edges as sharp as the reference.

Units: dimensionless; images in any common unit (intensity or dB).

docs.title: bosar.core.tiling
docs.text:
Tiled processing of rasters that never assumes an image fits in memory.

Tiler partitions an image into write windows (each pixel written exactly once) and gives each tile a read window enlarged by a halo that is clipped at the true image edge. Kernels that use mode="reflect" therefore see the real edge on boundary tiles and real neighbours elsewhere, so a tiled uniform_filter equals the untiled result as long as halo >= size // 2.

Design follows dolphin's io/_blocks.py (isce-framework, Apache-2.0/BSD-3): block indices, padding and trimming; re-implemented, no code copied (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md: reference only). All coordinates are integer pixels, half-open [start, stop); the pixel centre is the index.

docs.title: bosar.core.conventions
docs.text:
Binding numerical conventions (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §5, the project rules) as constants and helpers.

Every kernel imports these instead of re-deriving 4π/λ locally. Units are SI: metres, seconds, radians; temporal baselines are integer days and become years only here (DAYS_PER_YEAR).

Sign convention: cpx_ifg = ref * conj(sec); with the ISCE/SNAP SLC phase convention (φ_slc = −4πr/λ) a range increase between reference and secondary (motion away from the sensor) gives positive interferometric phase, and the LOS displacement d_los = −λ φ / (4π) is positive toward the sensor (MintPy-consistent).

docs.title: API — data and readers
docs.text: Rasters are GeoTIFF (float32 / complex64 / uint8) with bosar: tags; the project file is project.json. Every sensor reader returns the same contract — a scene with its metadata in SI units — so a new sensor is a reader and a fixture test, not a chain.

docs.title: bosar.data.raster
docs.text:
Tiled GeoTIFF create / window-write / read with package-namespaced tags.

Scope for v0.1.0: create, window writes, full reads, tags and array stats — enough for the dummy step to write a tagged, tiled product without loading it into RAM. Complex rasters (two bands + mask) and COG/geocoding arrive with the DInSAR release.

Tags: GDAL splits metadata keys on the first colon, so bosar:units cannot be a key (the development log, probe P2). Tags therefore live in a GDAL metadata namespace (domain) named after the package and are written/read with update_tags(ns=...); TAG_PREFIX is only the display form. Products written before the rename carry their tags in the legacy namespace (bosar._legacy.LEGACY_TAG_NAMESPACES); readers merge it under the current one until 0.2.0.

docs.title: bosar.data.model
docs.text:
Common stack model shared by every reader: geometry, scenes, interferograms, baselines.

v0.1.0. Every reader returns these objects so that the pipeline, the CLI and later the GUI never see a format-specific structure. Rules:

  • Units in names, SI only: metres, seconds, radians, Hz, integer days. Degrees appear only in *_deg fields that mirror what a file says (heading, centre lat/lon).
  • Nothing here loads a full-resolution array. Array access is windowed through :class:ArraySource objects (src[rows, cols]), exactly like data.raster.RasterSource.
  • dt_days is always recomputed from the two dates, never read from a file.
  • Plausibility is asserted at reader exit (:func:check_plausible): a reader that returns an implausible wavelength, incidence, range or baseline raises E204 naming file, field, expected and actual.

docs.title: bosar.data.sentinel1_safe
docs.text:
Sentinel-1 IW SLC SAFE reader: manifest, annotation XML, per-burst windowed measurement access.

v0.1.0 (B2). Own implementation from the ESA product specification; the parsing ideas of xarray-sentinel (B-Open, Apache-2.0) and ISCE2 Sentinel1.py were read as references, no code was copied. Rules: nothing full-resolution is loaded (rasterio windows on the CInt16 TIFF, the geolocation grid is interpolated per window); every failure names the SAFE, the swath, the file and the field (E201 / E203 / E205); missing annotation/calibration/ is a W203 warning on the product, not an error.

Layout of a SAFE folder (unzipped, possibly VV-only)::

<name>.SAFE/manifest.safe
<name>.SAFE/annotation/s1a-iw2-slc-vv-<start>-<stop>-<orbit>-<take>-<n>.xml
<name>.SAFE/annotation/calibration/{calibration,noise}-...xml   (may be absent)
<name>.SAFE/measurement/s1a-iw2-slc-vv-...tiff                    CInt16, one strip per line

The grid is regular (lines × pixels, e.g. 10 × 21 in IW SLC products); bilinear interpolation with scipy.interpolate.RegularGridInterpolator. Values outside the grid are extrapolated linearly (the grid covers the image, so this only touches edge pixels).

Times are seconds after :func:epoch_of (midnight UTC of the acquisition date), the epoch of the date's :class:~bosar.core.orbit.Orbit.

docs.title: bosar.data.annotation
docs.text:
Correct a stack's scalar geometry from the Sentinel-1 SAFE annotation.

The SNAP StaMPS export (GAMMA .par) carries a nominal slant-range axis (2 m spacing, near/far = centre ∓ (N−1)/2 × 2 m, W201) and an earth_radius_below_sensor ≈ 11.5 km too small; the SAFE annotation of the same date holds the measured values. :func:apply_annotation

  • finds the swath annotation whose first-pixel slant range (c · slantRangeTime / 2) and sample count match the stack's reference scene,
  • overwrites pixel_spacing_range_m (c / (2 · rangeSamplingRate)), the near/mid/far ranges, pixel_spacing_azimuth_m, the two radii (orbit state vectors → sensor distance and ellipsoid radius under the sensor) and the incidence angles (geolocation grid),
  • re-projects every TCN baseline with the new look angle,
  • sets acq_utc of every date that has a SAFE to that SAFE's startTime (answer 2),
  • moves the W201 range-axis warning into an I201 info record carrying both B⊥ values and stamps geometry.provenance = "safe-annotation:<file>".

Nothing changes without the call. path may be one .SAFE folder, a SAFE .zip (the annotation XML is read with :mod:zipfile, nothing is extracted) or a folder holding any number of either. Per-pixel geometry from orbits + DEM is v0.2.0.

docs.title: bosar.data.calibration
docs.text:
Sentinel-1 radiometric calibration LUTs: annotation/calibration/calibration-*.xml read straight from the product zip (zipfile; nothing is extracted), or from an unzipped SAFE, and interpolated to a pixel grid.

Each file holds calibrationVector records at a set of image line numbers, each with the sampled pixel columns and the sigmaNought / betaNought / gamma / dn values there (ESA Sentinel-1 Product Specification, S1-RS-MDA-52-7441, §6.4.9). The calibrated backscatter of a complex sample DN is |DN|^2 / A^2 with A the LUT value at that pixel (bilinear in line and pixel, as ESA's SNAP Calibration operator does). The LUT is applied only in the native SAFE path, never to the coregistered GAMMA export, whose amplitude changes stay relative (core.amplitude).

docs.title: bosar.data.noise
docs.text:
Sentinel-1 thermal-noise LUTs: annotation/calibration/noise-*.xml read straight from the product zip (zipfile, nothing extracted) or from an unzipped SAFE, and evaluated on the image grid in DN^2 (the unit of |DN|^2).

Two layouts exist (ESA MPC-0392, "Thermal Denoising of Products Generated by the S-1 IPF"; S1-RS-MDA-52-7441 §6.4.10):

  • IPF 2.90 and later (2018 on): noiseRangeVectorList - per vector an azimuthTime, an image line, the sampled pixel columns and noiseRangeLut - and noiseAzimuthVectorList - blocks (swath, firstAzimuthLine, firstRangeSample, lastAzimuthLine, lastRangeSample) with a line list and noiseAzimuthLut. The noise power is the product range(line, sample) * azimuth(line, sample); in TOPS products the azimuth factor carries the scalloping of the antenna sweep.
  • before 2.90: noiseVectorList with noiseLut - range only.

Evaluation (:func:noise_on_grid): a range vector is interpolated linearly in sample (held constant beyond its first / last pixel); along lines either between the two vectors that bracket the line - exactly :func:bosar.data.calibration.lut_on_grid's convention, so a burst line maps onto the same absolute image line as the calibration LUT - or, for TOPS SLC, the one vector of the burst chosen by azimuth time (range_vector; :meth:NoiseLUT.range_vector_index). The second form is what SNAP's ThermalNoiseRemoval does for IW / EW SLC (one range vector per burst, held over the burst), and the only safe one: in the IPF 3.31 product of the xarray-sentinel test data each vector's azimuthTime is the azimuthTime of burst k while its line is the first line of burst k-1 (the line field is one burst early). The azimuth LUT is interpolated linearly in line inside its block (held beyond the block's first / last listed line); a pixel inside no block takes the nearest block (in lines plus samples).

The IPF version comes from manifest.safe (<safe:software name="Sentinel-1 IPF" version="003.31"/>, as ISCE2's Sentinel1.populateIPFVersion reads it, Apache-2.0; nothing copied). :func:decide_thermal_noise turns the thermal_noise request (auto | on | off) and what the SAFE holds into one decision per date; auto means on for IPF 2.90 and later.

docs.title: bosar.data.stripmap
docs.text:
Stripmap SLC scenes: the one interface the sensor readers fill and the stripmap chain consumes.

A :class:StripmapScene is one single-look complex image of a stripmap sensor (ALOS-1 PALSAR L1.1, ENVISAT ASAR IMS, ERS-1/2 SAR IMS in the Envisat format, NISAR RSLC, ...) with the metadata the coregistration and the flattening need, in SI units, plus a lazy window reader for the samples. Readers live next to it (data/ceos_alos.py, data/asar.py, data/nisar.py) and register an opener with :func:register_stripmap_reader; :func:open_stripmap sniffs the file and dispatches.

Conventions (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5 apply): pixel (row, col) is the integer index, the pixel centre is the index; line row was sensed at sensing_start_s + row * azimuth_time_interval_s seconds after epoch (sensor time of the line, not necessarily zero-Doppler time - see doppler); sample col is at slant range starting_range_m + col * range_pixel_spacing_m. doppler is the Doppler centroid of the image [Hz] as a polynomial in slant range [m]: a product in zero-Doppler geometry has a zero polynomial; the geometry kernels take it into account where it is not zero (the squinted ALOS-1 L1.1 products). The SLC phase convention is that of core/conventions.py (-4 pi R / lambda); a reader that gets a product with the opposite sign conjugates the samples and says so in extra["phase_sign"].
