docs.title: bosar.data.ceos_alos
docs.text:
ALOS-1 PALSAR L1.1 (CEOS SAR-CCT) reader: a product as ASF distributes it - the zip ALPSRP<orbit 5><frame 4>-H1.1__A.zip (or -L1.1.zip) or its extracted folder with VOL-, LED-, IMG-HH-, IMG-HV- (FBD) and TRL- files - opened as a :class:~bosar.data.stripmap.StripmapScene.

The record layouts (byte offsets and widths) are those of ISCE2's alos_slc record definitions, checked against a real product (docs/data/formats.md, "ALOS-1 PALSAR L1.1"):

  • every CEOS record starts with a 12-byte header: record number (uint32), first subtype (uint8), record type code (uint8), second and third subtype (uint8 each), record length (uint32); all binary fields are big-endian; text fields are ASCII, numbers in text fields are Fortran-style (D exponents accepted);
  • the leader file is walked record by record (type code 10 = data set summary, 30 = platform position, 40 = attitude, 50 = radiometric, 60 = data quality, 200 = facility) so that a product with a different facility-record count still parses;
  • the image file: a 720-byte file descriptor, then one record per line of prefix (412) bytes of line header followed by the samples. The descriptor's bits per sample (32), samples per data group (2), bytes per data group (8) and format type code (C*8) decide the sample format: two IEEE float32 per complex sample (COMPLEX*8); a product declaring 16-bit samples would be read as two int16 (never seen; the L1.0 raw is 8-bit and is not a product of this reader).

Conventions (docs/data/formats.md has the record table and the quirks):

  • epoch is the UTC midnight of the first line's date (year / day-of-year of its prefix); sensing_start_s is the least-squares intercept of the per-line milliseconds of day stamps against line / PRF (the stamps are integer milliseconds, half a line of quantisation; the fit recovers the start to a few microseconds); the leader's scene-centre time must agree (W222 above 2 ms, E205 above 1 s);
  • prf_hz is the leader's (mHz with decimals); the per-line PRF field (integer mHz) must not vary by more than PRF_TOLERANCE relatively (E205), any smaller variation or a difference to the leader is W221;
  • starting_range_m is the leader's range gate delay times c / 2 (the prefix's slant range to first sample is an integer metre count; W222 above 1 m, E205 above 100 m);
  • doppler: the leader's cross-track Doppler centroid polynomial is in Hz per range pixel (f = c0 + c1 p + c2 p^2, p the 0-based sample index; ISCE2 ALOS_SLC.py uses it as dopplerVsPixel; checked on a real product by the correlation Doppler estimator at near, mid and far range); it is converted to slant range with p = (r - r0) / dr so that the oversampled FBD grid keeps the same polynomial;
  • the orbit: the platform position record's state vectors (ECR = Earth-fixed, metres, m/s, 60 s apart) on the scene epoch, densified to ORBIT_SPACING_S with the 8th-order Lagrange interpolation so that the chain's cubic Hermite stays below a millimetre (at 60 s it would be 0.3 m);
  • look_side from the leader's sensor clock angle (+90 deg = right, as ISCE2 reads it), checked against the geolocation of the first line's centre pixel (prefix latitude / longitude) relative to the orbit's cross-track direction (E204 when they disagree); pass_direction from the orbit's vertical velocity at mid scene;
  • calibration_db: sigma nought = 10 log10 |DN|^2 + CF - A with the leader's calibration factor CF (-83.0 dB since 2009-04-09, Shimada et al. 2009, IEEE TGRS 47(12)) and the L1.1 conversion A = 32.0 dB, i.e. -115.0 dB; both parts are in extra;
  • mode FBS (32 MHz sampling, 28 MHz chirp, HH) or FBD (16 MHz, 14 MHz, HH + HV); the mode comes from the sampling rate, the chirp bandwidth (|rate| x pulse length) is recorded in extra. oversample_to_fbs=True serves an FBD scene on the FBS grid (:func:bosar.core.range_oversample.oversample_range): n_samples, the range spacing and the sampling rate reflect the oversampled grid, the bandwidth stays 14 MHz.

read_slc(window) reads only the requested lines (one seek per line, prefix skipped) and samples; a zip is read in place when ASF's stored members allow it (one file handle, absolute offsets), a deflated member through zipfile's seekable stream (slow: unzip it first).

ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 L1.1 is the same CEOS product with JAXA's record layout (PALSAR-2_xx_Format_CEOS_E.pdf, checked on the free Greenland FBS pair): the scene id is ALOS2<orbit 5><frame 4>-<YYMMDD> followed by the product id <mode><L|R><level><option> <projection><A|D> (FBSR1.1__A); the leader's data set summary, platform position and radiometric records have the ALOS-1 offsets (the mission id says ALOS2); the signal data record's prefix is 544 bytes with the ALOS-1 fields to byte 216 plus the microseconds of day at bytes 84-92, which give the line times exactly (the millisecond fit stays a check); the leader's range gate delay is not the delay to the first sample (132.5 us where the prefix's slant range says 5056 us: the gate is counted inside a pulse interval), so the prefix's integer metres are the starting range; the cross-track Doppler polynomial is in Hz per pixel as on ALOS-1 and agrees with the leader's a + b R[km] centre-frequency fields (checked: W222 when they differ by more than :data:DOPPLER_CHECK_HZ). The mode comes from the product id (:data:ALOS2_MODES: nominal chirp bandwidth and range sampling rate per mode); the spotlight (SBS) and ScanSAR (WBS / WBD / WWS / WWD / VBS / VBD) products are recognised and refused (E205, the mode named): they are not stripmap scenes (a ScanSAR product's per-scan image files IMG-<pol>-<tail>-F<n> belong to its LED-<tail> product, and one image file per scan is refused as ScanSAR whatever the product id says). The range bandwidth is the leader's chirp |rate| x pulse length when it is plausible against the mode's nominal value (:data:ALOS2_BANDWIDTH_TOLERANCE; 24.9 MHz on the Greenland FBS scenes where the nominal is 28 MHz), else the leader's total processor bandwidth in range, else the nominal value (W222); a plausible total more than :data:BANDWIDTH_CHECK_REL below a plausible chirp is used instead of it (W222: the processed spectrum is no wider than either); the nominal value, the leader's total and the source are in extra. oversample_to_fbs has no effect on an ALOS-2 scene (its FBD shares the FBS sampling). The scene carries mission="ALOS-2", sensor="PALSAR-2", the L band wavelength 0.2425 m (the L-band quality profile follows).

Both missions: without pol the scene is the product's HH image, else its VV image (PALSAR-2 VV and VV + VH products), else its first polarisation (:func:default_polarisation). A folder holding several products (two zips extracted into one folder) is never merged: a member file opens its own product, the folder itself is refused (E101). Only a LED- file with at least one IMG- file of the same name tail makes a product: a GDAL .aux.xml sidecar next to an image file is not one.

ALOS or ALOS-2 from the scene id.

LinePrefixes(records: ndarray)

The per-line headers of an image file as arrays (one entry per line). Units: the stamp in integer milliseconds of day, the PRF in mHz, the slant range in integer metres, the geolocation in micro-degrees; records is the raw structured array.

The microsecond stamps of the ALOS-2 line header; None for the ALOS-1 prefix.

docs.title: parse_volume_descriptor
docs.text:
parse_volume_descriptor(data: bytes) -> dict[str, Any]

The volume directory file: the descriptor record, its file pointer records (one per product file, file_pointers) and the text record (text), keyed as the field tables name them. The records are told apart by the first subtype byte of their header: 192 the descriptor, 219 a file pointer, 18 the text record - on the real products every record of the file carries type code 192 (the text record is not type 63 as older CEOS writers have it). docs.text:
parse_leader(fh: BinaryIO) -> dict[str, Any]

The leader file walked record by record: fdr, dss (data set summary), ppr (platform position: state vectors), att (attitude points), rad (radiometric) and the lengths of the records seen (records). Missing optional records are None. Units: as the field names (deg, m, m/s, s, us, MHz, mHz, dB).

docs.text:
parse_image_descriptor(data: bytes) -> dict[str, Any]

The image file descriptor (first 720 bytes of an IMG- file) with the sample format decided from its fields: sample_dtype (>f4 for COMPLEX*8, >i2 for 16-bit integer pairs) and bytes_per_sample. Units: bytes, counts.

docs.title: list_product
docs.text:
list_product(path: Path | str) -> AlosProduct

The product files behind path (zip, folder, or one of the VOL- / LED- / IMG- / TRL- files of a folder). The members are grouped by their product tail (scene id + product id, ALPSRP082730370-H1.1__A; a ScanSAR per-scan image IMG-<pol>-<tail>-F<n> joins the LED-<tail> product, see :data:SCAN_TAIL_RE), and only a group with a LED- and an IMG- file is a product (a GDAL .aux.xml sidecar is not): a member file selects its own product; a zip or a folder holding several products is E101 (two products unzipped into one folder are never mixed). path of the result is the folder, or the member file passed when its folder holds several products (so that the path re-opens the same product). Units: none.

True for an L1.1 zip / folder / product file of either mission (a name carrying ALPSRP or ALOS2 - JAXA's sample zips are <order>_<item>_ALOS2....zip -, members LED- + IMG-); looks at names only, plus the zip's directory.

    prf_hz: float,
    *,
    stamp_unit_s: float = 0.001,
) -> tuple[float, float, float]

(t0_s, residual_std_s, residual_max_s): the time of line 0 (seconds of the first stamp's day) from a least-squares fit of the integer stamps (milliseconds of day by default, stamp_unit_s=1e-6 for the ALOS-2 microseconds) with the slope fixed at 1 / prf_hz; a day wrap in the stamps is unwrapped. docs.text:
doppler_from_leader(
    coeffs_hz_per_pixel: tuple[float, float, float],
    starting_range_m: float,
    spacing_m: float,
) -> DopplerPolynomial

The leader's cross-track Doppler centroid c0 + c1 p + c2 p^2 (p the 0-based range sample, Hz) as a polynomial in slant range r = starting_range_m + p spacing_m: c0 + (c1 / dr) (r - r0) + (c2 / dr^2) (r - r0)^2. Units: Hz, Hz/px, Hz/px^2 and metres in; a polynomial in metres out.

The platform position record as an :class:Orbit on epoch (seconds of its day plus the day difference); densified to spacing_s with the 8th-order Lagrange interpolation when the record's interval is coarser (None keeps the record's vectors). Units: seconds, metres, m/s.

docs.title: default_polarisation
docs.text:
default_polarisation(product: AlosProduct) -> str

The polarisation opened when none is asked for: HH when the product has it, else VV (PALSAR-2's VV and VV + VH stripmap products), else the first one listed. Units: none.

docs.title: open_alos
docs.text:
open_alos(
    path: Path | str | AlosProduct,
    *,
    pol: str | None = None,
    oversample_to_fbs: bool = False,
    orbit_spacing_s: float | None = ORBIT_SPACING_S,
) -> StripmapScene

Open one polarisation of an ALOS-1 PALSAR or ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 L1.1 product as a :class:StripmapScene.

pol (HH / HV / VH / VV) defaults to :func:default_polarisation (HH, else VV, else the first listed; extra["polarisation_source"] says requested or default). oversample_to_fbs serves an ALOS-1 FBD scene (16 MHz) on the FBS 32 MHz grid (no effect on an FBS or an ALOS-2 scene); orbit_spacing_s is the state-vector spacing the leader's orbit is densified to (:data:ORBIT_SPACING_S; None keeps the leader's 60 s vectors as they are). Units: SI in the scene; the leader's text fields are converted here (MHz, mHz, us, km, kHz).

docs.title: extract_product
docs.text:
extract_product(
    product: Path | str, dest: Path | str
) -> Path

Extract the product files of a zip (VOL- / LED- / IMG- / TRL- members, the quick-look and reports left out) into <dest>/<zip stem>/ and return that folder; a folder (or a file in it) is returned as it is. Members already extracted with the right size are kept. ASF's FBS products (ALPSRP...-L1.1.zip) and JAXA's ALOS-2 zips are deflated, so every window read through the zip inflates the image from its start (1.5 s per window on the real product against 2 ms in place): the chain extracts them once into the project's cache, as it does for SAFE zips. Units: none.

docs.title: bosar.data.asar
docs.text:
ENVISAT ASAR IMS and ERS-1/2 SAR IMS products in the Envisat product format.

One parser serves ASA_IMS_1P...N1 (ENVISAT ASAR, image mode single-look complex) and SAR_IMS_1P...E1 / .E2 (ERS-1 / ERS-2 AMI image mode, as ESA now distributes them from the same processor, SOFTWARE_VER="ASAR/7.00"). Every binary field is big-endian; offsets below are bytes from the start of the record. The layouts were taken from ISCE2's EnviSAT_SLC.py (MPH / SPH / DSD scheme; the first offsets of the processing-parameter, Doppler and geolocation records) and completed on the author's 26 products (docs/data/formats.md); the ESA product specification (PO-RS-MDA-GS-2009 vol. 8) was not on disk.

File layout::

MPH   1247 bytes, ASCII ``KEY=value`` lines (quoted strings, numbers with ``<unit>``)
SPH   SPH_SIZE bytes: ASCII keywords, then NUM_DSD data-set descriptors of 280 bytes each
      (DS_NAME, DS_TYPE, FILENAME, DS_OFFSET, DS_SIZE, NUM_DSR, DSR_SIZE)
ADS   annotation data sets at their DS_OFFSET (file offsets)
MDS1  NUM_DSR line records of DSR_SIZE = 17 + 4 * samples bytes

Records read (offset: field, type, unit):

  • MAIN PROCESSING PARAMS ADS (one DSR of 10069 bytes on these products; 2009 on products of processors before 6.02 - same leading layout, not verified here): 0 first_zero_doppler_time MJD; 13 last_zero_doppler_time MJD; 41 swath (3 chars); 44 range_spacing f32 m; 48 azimuth_spacing f32 m; 52 line_time_interval f32 s; 56 num_output_lines u32; 60 num_samples_per_line u32; 64 data_type (5 chars, SWORD); 73 time_diff_zero_doppler f32 s; 120 fourteen processing flags u8; 703 prf_value[0] f32 Hz; 743 tx_pulse_bw_value[0] f32 Hz; 975 first_proc_range_samp u32; 979 range_ref f32 m (range-spreading-loss reference); 983 range_samp_rate f32 Hz; 987 radar_freq f32 Hz; 991 num_looks_range u16; 993 filter_range (7 chars); 1000 filter_coef_range f32; 1004 look_bw_range[5] f32 Hz; 1024 tot_bw_range[5] f32 Hz; 1264 num_lines_proc u32; 1268 num_look_az u16; 1270 look_bw_az f32 Hz; 1274 to_bw_az f32 Hz; 1278 filter_az (7 chars); 1285 filter_coef_az f32; 1289 az_fm_rate[3] f32 (Hz/s, Hz/s^2, Hz/s^3 in two-way time); 1301 ax_fm_origin f32 ns; 1305 dop_amb_conf f32; 1377 proc_scaling_fact f32; 1381 ext_cal_fact f32 (the external calibration constant K); 1509 output_statistics[2] (4 f32 each); 1541 avg_scene_height_ellpsoid f32 m - the ellipsoidal height the geolocation grid was computed at (2527 m on the ASAR Mexico City products, 0 on the ERS ones; ISCE2 reads 1537, four bytes early, as it reads the state vectors at 1761); 1765 + 36 k (k = 0..4) orbit state vectors: MJD, then x, y, z as i32 in 1e-2 m and vx, vy, vz as i32 in 1e-5 m/s, Earth-fixed frame (a slot that is blank - spaces, 0xFF or zeros, as the spare areas of the record are space-filled - is skipped; all 26 products fill all five).
  • DOP CENTROID COEFFS ADS (55 bytes): 0 zero_doppler_time MJD; 13 slant_range_time f32 ns (two-way origin); 17 dop_coef[5] f32 in Hz, Hz/s, ... Hz/s^4 of tau - tau0 in seconds; 37 dop_conf f32; 41 dop_conf_below_thresh u8; 42 delta_dop[5] i16.
  • GEOLOCATION GRID ADS (NUM_DSR records of 521 bytes): 0 zero_doppler_time MJD of the record's first line; 13 line_num u32 (1-based); 17 num_lines u32; 21 sub_sat_track f32 deg; 25 samp_numbers[11] u32 (1-based); 69 slant_range_times[11] f32 ns (two-way); 113 angles[11] f32 deg (incidence); 157 lats[11] i32 1e-6 deg; 201 longs[11] i32 1e-6 deg; 267 last_zero_doppler_time MJD (line line_num + num_lines - 1); 279 .. 499 the same five arrays for that last line.
  • CHIRP PARAMS ADS (1483 bytes): 13 swath, 16 polarisation (3 chars each); 19 chirp_width f32 samples; 23 chirp_sidelobe, 27 chirp_islr f32 dB; 31 chirp_peak_loc f32; 35 re_chirp_power, 39 elev_chirp_power f32 dB; 43 chirp_quality_flag u8; 44 ref_chirp_power f32 dB; 48 normalisation_source (7 chars). Informational only.
  • MDS1 line record: 0 zero_doppler_time MJD; 12 quality_flag u8; 13 line_num u32 (1-based); 17 samples as big-endian int16 pairs (I, Q), DATA_TYPE="SWORD".

MJD fields are 12 bytes: days since 2000-01-01 00:00:00 UTC as signed i32 (negative for the 1990s ERS scenes), seconds u32, microseconds u32.

Geometry convention: the products are focused to zero Doppler (ALGORITHM="RAN/DOP", lines stamped with zero-Doppler times): the scene's :class:~bosar.data.stripmap.DopplerPolynomial is zero and the processed Doppler centroid of the DOP ADS goes to extra["processed_doppler_centroid"] for the resampler. The acceptance test of this claim and of the parser is rdr2geo of every geolocation-grid tie point from the product state vectors against the tie point's own lat / lon, both at the product's avg_scene_height_ellpsoid (tests/test_integration_asar_real.py; the measured agreement is in docs/data/formats.md: about 1 m on all 26 products).

Orbit: the five MPP state vectors span exactly the frame (first to last line, ~4.6 s apart); they are extended by orbit_margin_s on both sides with :func:bosar.core.orbit.extend_orbit (two-body + J2 in the Earth-fixed frame) so that the geometry kernels have a margin, and replaced by a DORIS / PRC file when orbit_file is given (:mod:bosar.data.doris). Such a file must agree with the product's own vectors at mid scene: W223 beyond 100 m, refused (E204) beyond 1 km - the ERS-1 and ERS-2 PRC files of a tandem day cover the same times 11 950 km apart.

Calibration: calibration_db = -10 log10(K) with K = ext_cal_fact; the full ESA convention for single-look complex products (Rosich & Meadows 2004, ENVI-CLVL-EOPG-TN-03-0010) is sigma0 = |z|^2 / K * (R / range_ref)^3 * sin(incidence) with the per-pixel terms left to the caller (extra["calibration"] carries K and range_ref). Not verified on a target.

open_asar(
    path: Path | str,
    *,
    orbit_file: Path | str | None = None,
    orbit_dir: Path | str | None = None,
    orbit_margin_s: float = 10.0,

Open an ENVISAT ASAR IMS or an ERS-1/2 SAR IMS product (Envisat format) as a :class:~bosar.data.stripmap.StripmapScene.

orbit_file: a DORIS (DOR_VOR_AX / DOR_POR_AX) or ERS PRC precise-orbit file; its state vectors replace the product's (orbit_source names it). orbit_dir: a folder of such files - the one covering the scene is taken (VOR before POR before PRC; files naming another satellite than the product's are left out; E201 when none covers it); the stripmap chain's --orbits <folder>. An external orbit is compared with the product's own state vectors at mid scene: more than :data:ORBIT_FILE_WARN_M apart is a W223, more than :data:ORBIT_FILE_REFUSE_M refuses an orbit_file (E204) and skips a folder's file for the next candidate (W223; E204 when every candidate is that far). orbit_margin_s: how far the product's five state vectors are extended beyond the frame (seconds; 0 = not at all). docs.title: bosar.data.nisar
docs.text:
NISAR L1 RSLC reader: one HDF5 product -> one :class:StripmapScene.

Status: opened on real granules; a real pair through the stripmap chain. The provisional products of ASF (dataset NISAR_L1_RSLC_PROVISIONAL_V1, 0.4-30 GB per granule, searchable without a login) open: a frequency-B-only granule and the 12-day pair of track 58 / frame 53 (2026-06-18 / 06-30, left-looking, descending, 41040 x 6381 per frequency), which went through the stripmap chain to an interferogram (docs/data/formats.md). The layout below is reconstructed from the open ISCE3 sources that write and read the product (the L1 RSLC product specification, JPL D-102274, is not on disk):

  • writer: isce3/python/packages/nisar/products/writers/SLC.py (dataset names, dtypes, the units strings, complex32 images) - https://github.com/isce-framework/isce3/blob/develop/python/packages/nisar/products/writers/SLC.py
  • swath / metadata loader: isce3/cxx/isce3/product/Serialization.h - https://github.com/isce-framework/isce3/blob/develop/cxx/isce3/product/Serialization.h
  • orbit loader and the reference-epoch attribute: isce3/cxx/isce3/core/Serialization.h and isce3/cxx/isce3/io/Serialization.h (getRefEpoch / setRefEpoch: the units attribute is seconds since YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS or ...:SS.fffffffff) - https://github.com/isce-framework/isce3/blob/develop/cxx/isce3/io/Serialization.h
  • identification datasets: isce3/python/packages/nisar/products/readers/Base/Identification.py
  • complex32 (two float16): isce3/python/packages/isce3/core/types.py - https://github.com/isce-framework/isce3/blob/develop/python/packages/isce3/core/types.py

Everything here is re-implemented from those sources (Apache-2.0); no code copied.

Paths read. R = /science/LSAR (L band) or /science/SSAR (S band); I = R/identification; S = R/RSLC/swaths; M = R/RSLC/metadata; F = frequencyA or frequencyB; P = HH / HV / VH / VV ... Units are the units attributes the ISCE3 writer attaches (meters, hertz, seconds since <UTC>):

path dtype, shape unit used as I/zeroDopplerStartTime bytes, ISO-8601 UTC - date; epoch = that midnight I/zeroDopplerEndTime bytes - extra (optional) I/lookDirection bytes Right / Left - look_side (case-insensitive) I/orbitPassDirection bytes Ascending / Descending - pass_direction I/listOfFrequencies bytes (n,) - frequency check (optional) I/trackNumber, frameNumber, absoluteOrbitNumber uint scalars - extra I/boundingPolygon, productVersion, missionId bytes - centre, extra S/zeroDopplerTime float64 (n_lines,) seconds since ref sensing_start_s (rebased) S/zeroDopplerTimeSpacing float64 scalar seconds azimuth_time_interval_s S/F/slantRange float64 (n_samples,) meters starting_range_m, n_samples S/F/slantRangeSpacing float64 scalar meters spacing; sampling rate c / 2 dr S/F/processedCenterFrequency float64 scalar hertz wavelength_m = c / f S/F/processedRangeBandwidth float64 scalar hertz range_bandwidth_hz S/F/processedAzimuthBandwidth float64 scalar hertz azimuth_bandwidth_hz (optional) S/F/nominalAcquisitionPRF float64 scalar hertz prf_hz S/F/listOfPolarizations bytes (n_pol,) - polarisation choice S/F/P complex32 (r/i float16) or complex64 (n_lines, n_samples) 1 read_slc M/orbit/time float64 (n,) seconds since ref orbit (rebased to epoch) M/orbit/position, velocity float64 (n, 3) meters, meters / second orbit (ECEF) M/orbit/orbitType bytes (FOE, NOE, MOE, POE, Custom) - orbit_source (optional) M/processingInformation/parameters/F/dopplerCentroid float64 (nt, nr) hertz extra M/calibrationInformation/F/P/scaleFactor float64 scalar 1 extra (optional)

The dopplerCentroid LUT is the Doppler of the raw data used in focusing, kept for information only (extra["doppler_centroid_lut_max_abs_hz"]): the RSLC grid is zero-Doppler.

Assumptions (stated for the author, see docs/data/formats.md): the image grid is zero-Doppler (doppler = zero polynomial); the time axis is uniform at zeroDopplerTimeSpacing; the SLC phase sign is that of ISCE (-4 pi R / lambda, core/conventions.py), not verified on a real product (extra["phase_sign_verified"] = False); no-data samples are 0 + 0j as stored (non-finite values are zeroed on read). Times: seconds after midnight UTC of the acquisition date; the product's own reference epochs are converted. Units: SI.

docs.title: bosar.data.synthetic_gamma
docs.text:
A tiny synthetic GAMMA / StaMPS-export stack on disk.

Shaped like the author's SNAP export: <root>/rslc/<date>.rslc(.par), diff0/<ref>_<sec>.{diff,diff.par,base}, geo/<ref>.{lat,lon}, geo/elevation_dem.rdc (+ .par) with big-endian data and the key vocabulary of the real 20240821.rslc.par (orbit radii, ranges, frequency, heading, three state vectors). Returns the truths so tests can compare windowed reads. Pure NumPy; no other package module is imported.

Units: metres, seconds, Hz, degrees in the files (as GAMMA writes them); arrays complex64.

docs.title: write_gamma_stack
docs.text:
write_gamma_stack(
    root: Path,
    *,
    dates: Sequence[str] = (
        "20240821",
        "20240902",
        "20240914",
    ),
    reference: str = "20240821",
    shape: tuple[int, int] = (48, 64),
    seed: int = 0,
    snap_signature: bool = True,
    with_geo: bool = True,
    with_diff: bool = True,
    tcn_by_pair: dict[
        tuple[str, str], tuple[float, float, float]
    ]
    | None = None,
    frequency_hz: float | None = None,
    star_phase: bool = False,
) -> dict[str, Any]

Write the stack under root; returns truths (arrays, TCN, lat/lon/height grids).

star_phase=True makes every .diff consistent with the SLCs: diff(ref, k) = R * conj(S_k) * exp(-j phi_k) with a smooth planted phi_k (truths["phi_sim"][date]), the way SNAP writes a flattened, topography-corrected pair.

docs.title: bosar.data.gamma_stamps
docs.text:
GAMMA / StaMPS-export importer (SNAP → StaMPS export layout), the stack that exists on disk.

Layout (author data, the planning notes §2 D)::

<root>/rslc/<date>.rslc  + .rslc.par        FCOMPLEX big-endian, rows = azimuth_lines
<root>/diff0/<ref>_<sec>.diff + .diff.par + .base   topo- and flat-earth-corrected ifgs
<root>/geo/<ref>.lat, <ref>.lon, elevation_dem.rdc (+ .par)   REAL*4 big-endian, radar grid
<root>/dem/projected_dem.rslc + .par         map-projected DEM (informational)

Reads are windowed through numpy.memmap — no full-resolution array is ever loaded. Every failure names the file and the field (E201/E203/E205); implausible values raise E204. The GAMMA .par key vocabulary follows the GAMMA ISP documentation; MintPy's prep_gamma (GPL) was consulted only as a list of key names, no code was copied.

docs.text:
BEAM-DIMAP (ESA SNAP) importer: .dim XML + .data/*.img ENVI bands → Stack.

The import bridge of ARCHITECTURE §6.1: a stack coregistered (Back-Geocoding + ESD + Deburst) in SNAP, optionally with interferograms and coherence, opens as a :class:~bosar.data.model.Stack. Synthetic fixtures only this version (the author's SNAP subset arrives later, docs/data/snap_demo_subset_zh.md).

Conventions handled: * band names i_IW2_VV_mst_21Aug2024 / q_IW2_VV_slv1_02Sep2024 (SLC i/q pairs, int16), i_ifg_IW2_VV_21Aug2024_02Sep2024 / q_ifg_… (complex interferogram), Phase_ifg_…, coh_IW2_VV_21Aug2024_02Sep2024, Intensity_…, elevation, orthorectifiedLat, orthorectifiedLon; * Abstracted_Metadata: radar_frequency is in MHz (converted with a named factor), incidence_near/incidence_far in degrees, slant_range_to_first_pixel in metres, range_spacing/azimuth_spacing in metres, first_line_time 21-AUG-2024 23:40:25; * the Baselines element (Master: 21Aug2024 → Slave: 02Sep2024 → Perp Baseline m). Every band listed in the .dim must exist on disk: a missing .img is E201 naming the band and the expected file. SNAP itself is GPL: nothing of it is used, only its file format.

docs.title: bosar.data.isce_stack
docs.text:
ISCE2 topsStack importer: merged/SLC, merged/geom_reference, baselines → Stack (B4).

Layout (the upstream isce2 source (contrib/stack/topsStack), Apache-2.0, read for the conventions)::

<root>/merged/SLC/<date>/<date>.slc.full (+ .xml, .vrt)
                                                  CFLOAT (complex64), BIP, 1 band
<root>/merged/geom_reference/{lat,lon,hgt}.rdr    FLOAT (+ .xml)
<root>/merged/geom_reference/los.rdr (+ .xml)     2 bands BIL: incidence, azimuth [deg]
<root>/baselines/<ref>_<sec>/<ref>_<sec>.txt      "Bperp (average): x", "Bpar (average): y"
<root>/reference/IW*.xml                          radarWavelength, startingRange,
                                                  rangePixelSize

ISCE image sidecars (.xml) give WIDTH / LENGTH / DATA_TYPE / SCHEME / BYTE_ORDER / NUMBER_BANDS; the rasters are read with numpy.memmap per window (no GDAL, no full load). Synthetic fixtures only this version (no ISCE2 stack exists on the author's drive).

docs.title: bosar.data.gacos
docs.text:
GACOS zenith total delay maps (assisted tier): the request limits of gacos.net and the validation of delivered <date>.ztd / <date>.ztd.rsc binary grids (read-only).

GACOS delivers one grid per date: 4-byte little-endian float32, WIDTH x FILE_LENGTH, north-up from (X_FIRST, Y_FIRST) with steps X_STEP / Y_STEP (degrees, the latter negative), TIME_OF_DAY in decimal hours UTC (e.g. 23.666666666667UTC). The form at http://www.gacos.net/ (checked 2026-09-24) takes N / W / E / S in degrees, the time as hour and minute (UTC), a date list (one YYYYMMDD per line), the output format (GeoTIFF or binary grid) and an e-mail, and accepts at most 10 x 10 degrees and 20 dates per request.

Nothing here downloads anything; :func:check_gacos_dir only reads (np.memmap(mode="r")). Issues carry a code: E201 missing file, E204 implausible (size, time, coverage), E205 unreadable header, W205 marginal (edge margin, NaN/zero fraction, differing grids, extra dates).

docs.title: bosar.data.ionex
docs.text:
IONEX 1.0 global ionosphere maps and the single-layer ionospheric phase of an interferogram.

Format (Schaer, Gurtner & Feltens 1998, "IONEX: The IONosphere Map EXchange Format Version 1"). Fixed columns; every header and map record carries its label in columns 61-80. Header: EPOCH OF FIRST MAP / EPOCH OF LAST MAP (6I6, UTC), INTERVAL (I6, s), # OF MAPS IN FILE, MAPPING FUNCTION (COSZ / QFAC / NONE), BASE RADIUS (F8.1, km), MAP DIMENSION (2 for a single layer), HGT1 / HGT2 / DHGT, LAT1 / LAT2 / DLAT, LON1 / LON2 / DLON (2X,3F6.1: km, degrees; latitudes usually run north to south, DLAT < 0), EXPONENT (I6, default -1), optional START OF AUX DATA ... END OF AUX DATA blocks (differential code biases), END OF HEADER. Data: START OF TEC MAP / EPOCH OF CURRENT MAP / per latitude a LAT/LON1/LON2/DLON/H record (2X,5F6.1) followed by the values of that latitude band, 16 per line (I5), END OF TEC MAP; the same for RMS MAP (and HEIGHT MAP in 3-D files, not supported). Values are in units of 10**EXPONENT TECU (an EXPONENT record inside a map overrides the header's for that map); 9999 = no value. Plain text or gzip (.gz); the Unix compress files (.Z) of the old CODE naming are refused with a hint.

Interpolation (Schaer et al. 1998, eqs. 1-4). Space: bilinear between the four grid nodes around the point. Time: the maps are tied to the Sun rather than to the Earth, so between the maps E_i at T_i and E_i+1 at T_i+1 the value at (lat, lon, t) is

E = (T_i+1 - t) / (T_i+1 - T_i) * E_i(lat, lon + w (t - T_i))
    + (t - T_i) / (T_i+1 - T_i) * E_i+1(lat, lon + w (t - T_i+1))

with w = 360 deg / day (the rotated-map interpolation; a point keeps its local solar time).

Single-layer model. All electrons sit in a thin shell at height H (HGT1 of the header, 450 km for the CODE / IGS maps) above a sphere of radius R (BASE RADIUS). The line of sight from a ground point at zenith angle z pierces the shell at the zenith angle z' with sin z' = R / (R + H) sin z and the earth-central angle psi = z - z' from the ground point, toward the sensor; slant TEC = VTEC(pierce point) / cos z'.

Interferometric phase and its sign. Bosar's SLC phase is -4 pi R_phase / lambda = -4 pi f R_phase / c (ARCHITECTURE §5). The ionosphere advances the carrier phase: the phase path is R_phase = R - K STEC / f^2 (K = 40.31 m^3 s^-2, STEC in electrons m^-2), so phi_slc(f) = -4 pi f R / c + 4 pi K STEC / (c f). The interferogram is ref * conj(sec):

phi(f) = 4 pi f (R_sec - R_ref) / c  +  4 pi K (STEC_ref - STEC_sec) / (c f)
  • the second, dispersive term is :func:iono_phase_rad: 4 pi K 1e16 dSTEC / (c f) with dSTEC = STEC_ref - STEC_sec in TECU (1 TECU at 5.405 GHz: 3.13 rad). More electrons on the reference date read like a longer range on the secondary date: positive phase. The split-spectrum estimate (core.iono.split_spectrum_phases) returns the b / f0 part of phi(f) = a f + b / f of the same interferogram, i.e. exactly this term at the carrier, with the same sign (tested on SLCs simulated from the formula above).

CODE final GIMs (http://ftp.aiub.unibe.ch/CODE/YYYY/): COD0OPSFIN_YYYYDDD0000_01D_01H_ GIM.INX.gz (25 hourly maps, 00:00 to 24:00 UTC) since GPS week 2238 (2022-11-27), CODGDDD0.YYI.Z before. :func:code_gim_candidates names them; nothing here downloads.

Units: degrees for latitude / longitude, radians for angles in computations, metres, seconds, TECU (1e16 electrons m^-2). Re-implemented from the format description; no code copied.

docs.title: bosar.data.doris
docs.text:
Precise orbits for ENVISAT and ERS: DORIS files in the Envisat format and the ERS PRC files of D-PAF.

DORIS (DOR_VOR_AX... precise, DOR_POR_AX... preliminary; ESA now delivers the reprocessed ERS-1/2 orbits in the same form - the ORBIT STATE VECTOR 1 DSD of the ERS IMS products names DOR_VOR_AXVF-P1996...): an MPH (1247 bytes) and SPH with one measurement data set (DS_TYPE=M, DS_NAME="DORIS PRECISE ORBIT" or "DORIS PRELIMINARY ORBIT") of ASCII records, one state vector per record::

07-MAR-2003 16:35:28.000000  <delta UT1 s>  <abs orbit>  X Y Z [m]  VX VY VZ [m/s]  <quality>

Fields are read by whitespace splitting (tokens 0-1 the UTC time, 4-6 the position, 7-9 the velocity, 10 the quality flag), as ISCE2's DOR class does; the Earth-fixed frame of the file is the one the products' state vectors use. Read on real DOR_VOR_AXVF files of the public STEP mirror for the ENVISAT ASAR pair: 3-7 cm from the products' own vectors at mid scene.

PRC (D-PAF / DLR precise orbits for ERS-1/2, "DGM-E04" products): fixed records of 130 ASCII bytes. Reconstructed from ISCE2's Orbit/PRC.py (the format description is not on disk) and confirmed on ESA's PRC_<yymmdd>_<orbit>_rev2 files for the ERS tandem pair (about 10 m from the products' vectors, the +0.5-day convention borne out): STATE record (columns 0-6): bytes 6-12 and 12-18 the first / last epoch in 0.1 days since J2000, bytes 47-52 the TDT - UTC offset in ms; STTERR records (terrestrial frame): bytes 14-20 the day in 0.1 days since J2000 (12:00 TDT of 2000-01-01, so +0.5 day gives days since 2000-01-01 00:00), 20-31 seconds of day in microseconds (TDT), 31-43 / 43-55 / 55-67 x, y, z in mm, 67-78 / 78-89 / 89-100 vx, vy, vz in micrometres per second, byte 127 the quality character. UTC = TDT - offset. STTINE (inertial) records are skipped. Unix-compress .Z files are refused with a hint.

Satellite: OrbitRecords.satellite is "ENVISAT" / "ERS1" / "ERS2" or None when the file does not say. PRC: the lead DSIDP record (DSIDP ERS1.ORB.PRC on ESA's PRC_<yymmdd>_<orbit>_rev2 files), else the COSPAR id of the state-vector records (bytes 6-13: 9105001 ERS-1, 9502101 ERS-2). DORIS: the SPH descriptor (ORBITE POE_REST SAT ENV1 on the STEP mirror's DOR_VOR_AX files). The STEP mirror keeps the ERS-1 and ERS-2 PRC files of a year side by side, and in the tandem months both cover the same times: a folder lookup must filter by satellite (orbit_files_covering).

Units: metres, metres per second, UTC datetime64[us].

docs.title: API — pipeline
docs.text: Every processing operation is a Step (a parameter model, what it requires, what it produces, run(ctx)) registered in bosar.pipeline.registry. The Runner — not the step — does the timing, the logging, the project-file updates and the garbage collection of intermediates.

docs.text:
The Step contract (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §3.3) and what a step receives and returns.

A step declares kind, version (bump when the algorithm changes → cached outputs invalid), a pydantic Params model, the product kinds it requires and the (kind, tier) pairs it produces; run(ctx) does the work. docs.title: bosar.pipeline.runner
docs.text:
The Runner: the only place that times, logs, updates the project and garbage-collects.

Sequence: validate params → run logger + run_start → backend (W401) → offline preflight (blocking → run_end(blocked) + E701, project untouched) → interrupted-step recovery (E802 + W104) → skip rule (W101) → step record running + save → step_start → Step.run inside a warnings capture (W000) → outputs verified (E607) and registered → step_end (seq) → done + log_seq + save → gc → guarded hooks (W803) → run_end + report. On failure the record is written before the project is saved, partial tier-2 outputs are kept and listed, every post-failure action is guarded (W802 never masks the original error) and StepFailedError (E801) is raised with the original exception as __cause__.

docs.title: bosar.pipeline.plan
docs.text:
Declared plans of multi-command chains.

A chain such as bosar sbas prep → bosar pipeline sbas runs over several commands and processes. In storage_mode=minimal the Runner collects a tier-2 product as soon as every known dependent step is done - a dependent that has not been created yet does not count, so the multilooked interferograms of a network were deleted before its unwrap phase, the flattened stack before the PSI step, and so on. A plan declares the ordered steps of a chain up front (step_id, kind, requires) in project.json under aux.plans[<name>]; a declared dependent that is not done yet keeps the products of the steps it requires. The plan is removed when its last step is done (complete_plan), and the normal collection follows.

A time-series step run in a minimal-storage project outside any declared plan is refused with E310 (:class:bosar.errors.ChainUndeclaredError): the one-line remedy is bosar project new --storage-mode full or one of the chain commands, which declare.

docs.text:
StorageManager: registers products with their tier and garbage-collects by the tier rules.

Rules (ARCHITECTURE §3.2, author decisions D-tier): tier 3 of a step is deleted when the step ends — also when it fails; tier 2 is deleted only in storage_mode="minimal" and only when the producing step has at least one dependent and every dependent is done (zero dependents would be vacuously "all done"); tier 1 is never deleted; nothing outside the project directory is ever touched. Files are deleted one by one (safe_unlink), never with a recursive remove.

docs.title: The installed build and its plug-ins
bosar.build
docs.text:
The frozen build and its plug-ins.

A PyInstaller one-folder build carries bosar_build.json next to the collected modules (sys._MEIPASS): the build id, the version, the platform tag, the git commit, the build time, whether the bundled SNAPHU was built without CS2. bosar preflight and bosar version report it; a source checkout reports none.

Plug-ins are wheels unpacked under <user data dir>/bosar/plugins/<name>/site-packages by bosar gpu install (:mod:bosar.plugins); :func:activate_plugin appends such a folder to sys.path before the package that needs it is imported (CuPy in backends). The bundle's own packages stay ahead on the path, so a plug-in never shadows them.

docs.title: module_request
docs.text:
module_request(
    argv: Sequence[str],
) -> tuple[str, list[str]] | None

(module, arguments) when a frozen executable is called as if it were the interpreter - bosar.exe [-X <opt>]... -m <module> [arguments] - which is what cuda-pathfinder's canary probe (sys.executable -m cuda.pathfinder..., CuPy 14) and Bosar's own child processes (sys.executable -X utf8 -m bosar ...) do; None for an ordinary command line. -X options are accepted and dropped here: the bootloader cannot take interpreter options from the command line, the frozen interpreter gets them from the build - bosar.spec passes ('X utf8', None, 'OPTION') to both executables, so a build runs in UTF-8 mode like python -X utf8 (the bootloader's isolated configuration ignores PYTHONUTF8) - and :func:utf8_requested tells :func:run_module_request that the caller asked for UTF-8. Units: none.

docs.title: utf8_requested
docs.text:
utf8_requested(argv: Sequence[str]) -> bool

True when the interpreter-style command line asks for UTF-8 mode: -X utf8 (or -X utf8=1; the last utf8 option wins, as in CPython) among the -X options before -m. Units: none.

docs.title: ensure_utf8_streams
docs.text:
ensure_utf8_streams() -> list[str]

Switch sys.stdout / sys.stderr to UTF-8 when the interpreter is not in UTF-8 mode - the fallback for a bundle whose interpreter did not get the spec's X utf8 option: Bosar's parents read their children's output as UTF-8 (-X utf8 children). Each stream keeps its error handler (reconfigure(encoding=...) alone would reset it to strict); one on strict gets the handler of UTF-8 mode - surrogateescape for stdout, backslashreplace for stderr - so a lone surrogate (an undecodable file name) never raises. Streams without reconfigure (None in a windowed build, a test capture) are left alone. Returns the names of the streams switched. Units: none.

docs.title: run_module_request
docs.text:
run_module_request(
    module: str,
    arguments: Sequence[str],
    *,
    utf8: bool = False,
) -> int

Run module as python -m module arguments would inside this process (the frozen executable standing in for the interpreter), through :func:runpy.run_module with sys.argv set - the package itself too: bosar/__main__.py runs the CLI (the spec bundles it), so this module never imports the CLI (build sits below cli in the layering). utf8 (the caller gave -X utf8, :func:utf8_requested) makes sure the standard streams write UTF-8 even when the interpreter is not in UTF-8 mode (:func:ensure_utf8_streams).

Returns the exit code as the interpreter would make it: the module's SystemExit code (None is 0; a message other than an integer goes to stderr and gives 1), 0 when it returns, 1 with one line on stderr when the module cannot be found or is a package without __main__. An exception raised while the module runs propagates (a traceback, exit code 1). Units: none.

docs.title: bosar.plugins
docs.text:
Plug-ins of a frozen build: wheels fetched from PyPI and unpacked under the user's data folder. The first and only plug-in is the GPU backend: cupy-cuda12x with its [ctk] extra (the NVIDIA runtime wheels), which the installers do not carry.

No pip inside a PyInstaller build - so this module resolves the wheels itself: the PyPI JSON API lists every file of a release; the newest release that has a wheel compatible with this interpreter (packaging.tags.sys_tags) is chosen; the wheel is downloaded, its SHA-256 checked against the index, unpacked; its Requires-Dist lines are followed (markers evaluated with the requested extras) except for the distributions the application already bundles. A manifest records what was unpacked. Network code lives here, never in core.

The functions take their fetch and download callables as parameters so the tests run the whole resolution on a fake index without a socket.

docs.title: Supported input formats and the quirks found on real data
docs.text: One section per reader. "Quirk" means something the files say that is not true or not what the format documentation promises; Bosar reports each one (W-code) and never corrects it silently. Started in v0.1.0.

docs.title: GAMMA / StaMPS export written by SNAP (data/gamma_stamps.py, reader gamma)
docs.text:
Layout: rslc/<date>.rslc(.par), diff0/<ref>_<sec>.diff(.par|.base), geo/<ref>.lat|.lon, geo/elevation_dem.rdc, dem/. Big-endian FCOMPLEX / REAL*4, read through np.memmap windows. Validated on the author's Indianapolis IW2 stack (29 dates, reference 20240821, 25925 × 12239).

# Quirk What the file says What is true Bosar 1 Nominal slant-range axis range_pixel_spacing 2.0 m; near_range_slc / far_range_slc = center_range_slc ∓ (N−1)/2 × 2 m (819528.6 / 871376.6 m) spacing c / (2 · rangeSamplingRate) = 2.329562 m; center_range_slc (845452.572 m) is the first-pixel range of the SAFE annotation to the millimetre W201 on the stack; data import --annotation <SAFE> overwrites spacing, near/mid/far range and stamps geometry.provenance = safe-annotation:<file> (I201) 2 Earth radius under the sensor earth_radius_below_sensor 6358256.3 m 6369807.5 m from the annotation orbit (WGS-84 radius at the sub-satellite latitude); the par value is 11.5 km too small and shifts every incidence angle by ≈ 1.5° and B⊥ by ≈ 8 m same W201 / --annotation (both radii replaced, incidence taken from the geolocation grid) 3 Copied reference header every <date>.rslc.par carries the reference scene's title, date (2024 8 21) and start/center/end_time; only the state vectors differ per scene the scene date is the file name W201 once per stack; acq_utc = file-name date at day precision (2024-09-02); with --annotation the SAFE startTime of every date that has a SAFE 4 Half-seconds times start_time 42612.60 s, center_time 42618.89 s, end_time 42625.18 s (of day) the SAFE says 23:40:25 – 23:40:52 UTC = 85225 – 85252 s of day: the par values are exactly half not used at all (see 3); documented here, not fixed — one stack is not enough to code a rule 5 Geo layer .par is a copy of the SLC par geo/<ref>.lat.par says image_format FCOMPLEX, range_samples/azimuth_lines the layer is REAL*4 the reader accepts width/nlines or range_samples/azimuth_lines and never trusts image_format for a geo layer; the file size check guards the dtype (E203) 6 Malformed .base sidecars initial_baseline(TCN) of 20240821_20240809, _20241231, _20250524 hold 1e11 – 1e15 m garbage (the same three dates MintPy dropped) E205 from parse_base; W202 on the stack, the interferogram is kept, the pair has no baseline row until v0.2.0 recomputes B⊥ from orbits

Baselines: B⊥ = B_C cos θ − B_N sin θ with θ the look angle at the scene-centre range (from the radii and the range axis — hence quirks 1–2 move B⊥: 223.8 m nominal vs 216.1 m in SNAP's own metadata for 20240821_20240704).

MintPy's bperp of this stack is not a perpendicular baseline. The author's ifgramStack.h5 stores, per pair, the raw C (cross-track) component of the .base TCN vector (gamma_utils.read_baseline; 261.21 m for 20240821_20240704 where the projected B⊥ is 213.9 m). Bosar always stores the projected B⊥ above. answer 4: the MintPy exporter writes the projected value; a --mintpy-legacy-bperp flag will reproduce the raw C component when a result has to be compared with the author's existing MintPy runs.

docs.text:
Verified against SNAP's geo/20240821.lat/.lon with Bosar's own rdr2geo (probe p21, median 0.046 px, p95 0.086 px over 198 594 samples):

quantity where it comes from value (IW2, 20240821) first line UTC annotation productFirstLineUtcTime (= SAFE startTime; the par's start_time is half the seconds of day, quirk 4) 23:40:25.206955 line interval annotation azimuthTimeInterval (= par azimuth_line_time, correct) 2.0555563 ms number of lines (productLastLineUtcTime − productFirstLineUtcTime) / interval + 1 12239 = azimuth_lines near range annotation slantRangeTime · c / 2 (the par's center_range_slc; its near_range_slc is centre − (N−1)/2 × a nominal 2 m) 845 452.572 m range spacing c / (2 · rangeSamplingRate) (= annotation rangePixelSpacing) 2.329562 m elevation_dem.rdc ellipsoidal heights (SNAP applies the geoid before writing); a ±33.5 m shift moves the solution by 11 px in range 112–332 m over the scene look side right: nadir × velocity —

docs.title: Bosar crop (data/crop.py, reader crop)
docs.text: crop.json + little-endian tiled GeoTIFFs written by bosar data crop. Carries the source sha256, the window, the shifted geometry and its provenance (so a crop made with --annotation keeps the corrected scalars). No quirks — it is our own format.

docs.title: Sentinel-1 SAFE (data/sentinel1_safe.py, reader safe)
docs.text:
• The author's unzipped SAFEs are VV-only and have no annotation/calibration/ (W203); the VH files listed in the manifest are absent (warning, VV opens).
  • The 20240704 IW1 measurement TIFF is a 1-byte placeholder → E203 naming SAFE, swath, file, actual and expected bytes; --swaths IW2,IW3 opens the rest.
  • Times in the annotation are UTC with microseconds; the geolocation grid holds degrees (converted to radians on read).

docs.title: Burst quirks (the native TOPS chain; data/burst.py)
docs.text:
• A burst's azimuthTime is the zero-Doppler time of its line 0 (sensingTime is the raw acquisition start); the bursts of one date share the azimuth grid, so the start differences are integer multiples of azimuthTimeInterval to ~1e-9 lines.
  • The valid region is per line: firstValidSample / lastValidSample arrays with -1 on the invalid lines at both ends; ISCE2's rectangle (the run of valid lines, the samples common to its first and last line) is what the merge and ESD use. Consecutive bursts overlap by about 100 lines; the merged grid cuts the overlap in the middle.
  • azimuthFmRate and dcEstimate are lists of polynomials in τ − t0 with τ = 2 r / c; each burst takes the entry nearest its mid time (ISCE2). azimuthSteeringRate is in deg/s.
  • The PRF lives in generalAnnotation/downlinkInformationList/downlinkInformation/prf (older annotations may lack it; the model keeps prf_hz=None) — azimuthTimeInterval, not the PRF, is the line spacing of the focused product.
  • The raw pool's zips store the measurement TIFFs deflate-compressed (1.4 GB → 0.9 GB), so random access through the zip is not possible: extract_safe_members inflates manifest, annotation and measurement of one sub-swath into <project>/cache/safe/<name>.SAFE/ once.
  • Orbit state vectors in the annotation are seconds of day; a product near midnight gets vectors of the previous / next day (unwrapped by ±86400 s against the product start).

docs.title: Sentinel-1D next to Sentinel-1A, and newer processor versions
docs.text:
Track 121 (ascending) over Indianapolis, sub-swath IW2, as read from the products on disk:

S1A 2024-08-21 S1A 2026-06-24 S1D 2026-07-13 IPF version 003.80 004.03 004.03 radar frequency [Hz] 5 405 000 454.33 same same range sampling rate [Hz] 64 345 238.13 same same azimuth time interval [s] 2.0555563e-3 same same azimuth steering rate [deg/s] 0.97986 same same processed range bandwidth [Hz] 48.3e6 same same lines x samples per burst 1505 x 25925 1504 x 25389 1504 x 25389 slant range time of sample 0 [s] 5.6402524e-3 5.6406765e-3 5.6406747e-3
  • S1D is handled like S1A / S1C: the same annotation schema, the same relative-orbit track (121), precise orbits named S1D_OPER_AUX_POEORB_... (ASF mirror, CDSE), product names S1D_IW_SLC__.... Nothing in the reader or the burst model is platform specific; the platform is recorded per date (secondaries.<date>.mission in the stack record) so that cross-platform interferograms can be told apart.
  • The burst size is not a constant of the track. The 2026 products (IPF 004.03, S1A and S1D alike) have one line and 536 samples fewer per burst and start 63.5 m farther in slant range than the 2024 ones. The native chain resamples every secondary onto the reference's burst grid from the geometry, so the mix needs no special case; a reader that assumes one burst shape per stack would fail.
  • Azimuth timing of S1D against S1A. ESD on the two S1D dates coregistered to the S1A reference converged to +0.0455 and +0.0468 lines (94 microseconds, about 0.65 m along track), against 0.0001 ... 0.009 lines (absolute) for the 49 converged S1A dates of the same stack: a constant along-track timing offset between the platforms, removed by ESD. Without ESD (geometry only) a cross-platform interferogram would carry a burst-edge phase jump of about 2 pi * 0.046 * dt * 4.5 kHz = 2.7 rad.
  • Range: the cross-correlation check gives -0.063 and -0.048 px for the S1D dates, inside the scatter of the S1A dates (-0.19 ... +0.12 px).
  • S1D phases 7 days after S1A on this track in mid 2026 (S1A 2026-06-24, S1D 2026-07-13 = +19 days = 12 + 7): cross-platform pairs have temporal baselines of 7 + 12 k days.

docs.title: Range shift of a date by IPF version, and what it really is
docs.text:
The amplitude cross-correlation of every date against the reference (20240821) on the downtown crop of track 121, IW2 bursts 6–8, 88 secondaries 2023-07-10 … 2026-09-23 (scripts/range_shift_by_ipf.py):

IPF platform dates first – last median shift [px] min / max [px] max burst spread [px] applied > 0.1 px (W209) 003.61 S1A 9 20230710 – 20231014 +0.013 −0.067 / +0.048 0.014 4 0 003.71 S1A 20 20231026 – 20240610 −0.027 −0.195 / +0.087 0.014 13 5 003.80 S1A 12 20240622 – 20241113 +0.036 −0.064 / +0.122 0.018 10 2 003.90 S1A 8 20241125 – 20250217 −0.100 −0.128 / +0.018 0.020 3 4 003.91 S1A 9 20250301 – 20250605 +0.018 −0.103 / +0.100 0.012 3 2 003.92 S1A 10 20250617 – 20251003 −0.002 −0.102 / +0.076 0.013 4 1 004.00 S1A 5 20251015 – 20251202 −0.078 −0.173 / +0.007 0.022 2 1 004.01 S1A 1 20251214 −0.188 — 0.007 1 1 004.02 S1A 1 20260107 −0.129 — 0.004 1 1 004.03 S1A, S1D 13 20260224 – 20260923 −0.063 −0.155 / +0.030 0.024 7 2

The shifts do not cluster by IPF version — within almost every version they span ±0.1 px. They are propagation delays (scripts/range_shift_vs_era5.py): the change of the tropospheric delay (ERA5 zenith total delay at the crop centre, 1 / cos θ) and of the ionospheric group delay (40.31 TEC / f², 1.38 cm per TECU at 5.405 GHz; slant TEC from the CODE rapid GIM at the pierce point) between the date and the reference:

predictor (87 dates) r R² residual std troposphere only 0.36 0.13 0.064 px ionosphere only 0.70 0.49 0.049 px troposphere + ionosphere 0.87 0.76 0.034 px (7.8 cm) both with free coefficients — 0.77 0.033 px; coefficients 0.94 and 0.83

The ionosphere dominates (±0.18 px: slant TEC differences of up to ±30 TECU between dates near the 2024–2025 solar maximum; the reference date has 46 TECU). The coregistration geometry has no atmosphere, so the envelope of a secondary sits where its group delay puts it; the range correction moves the envelope back and leaves the carrier phase alone (verified with the two versions of one date: 0.005 rad across the crop). The measured shift is thus also an independent, if coarse, estimate of the TEC difference of each date (0.03 px ≈ 5 TECU).

v0.4.0: the implied ΔSTEC per date is a product. bosar aux range-shift <project> --stack <id> [--era5-dir] [--ionex-dir] --write (pipeline/auxdata/rangeshift.py, which supersedes the v0.3.0 script) computes per secondary date the ERA5 zenith delay at the crop centre on the date and on the reference (the two hourly files around the acquisition, no download), tropo_px = Δztd / cos θ / Δr, residual_px = measured − tropo, and implied_dstec_tecu = residual_px × Δr f₀² / (40.31 × 10¹⁶) (168.8 TECU per pixel at 2.33 m and 5.405 GHz); with IONEX maps on disk the GIM slant-TEC difference at the pierce point stands next to it (gim_dstec_tecu), and the summary carries the regressions of v0.3.0 plus implied_vs_gim. --write stores the values in every date's coreg.json (record.range_cc.delay, with the sign convention) and in the coregistration step's summary (range_shift_delay, range_shift_delay_fit); bosar sbas quality then prints the shift[px], dSTEC[TECU] and GIM[TECU] columns in its per-date table. Sign: a positive shift is a later echo (more delay on the date than on the reference); ΔSTEC = STEC(date) − STEC(reference).

docs.title: Thermal-noise annotation and IPF versions (data/noise.py)
docs.text:
annotation/calibration/noise-<mission>-<swath>-<product>-<pol>-<start>-...xml, one per sub-swath and polarisation, named like the calibration XML; read from the zip without extraction. Values are noise power in DN^2 (the unit of |DN|^2), linear. Two layouts:

IPF elements noise power 2.90 and later (from March 2018) noiseRangeVectorList/noiseRangeVector: azimuthTime, line, pixel (list), noiseRangeLut (list); noiseAzimuthVectorList/noiseAzimuthVector: swath, firstAzimuthLine, firstRangeSample, lastAzimuthLine, lastRangeSample (inclusive), line (list), noiseAzimuthLut (list) range(line, sample) x azimuth(line) inside each block before 2.90 noiseVectorList/noiseVector: azimuthTime, line, pixel, noiseLut range only
  • The IPF version is in manifest.safe: <safe:software name="Sentinel-1 IPF" version="003.80"/> under the processing metadata object (the annotation XML does not carry it). The Indianapolis products are 003.80 (2024) and 004.03 (2026).
  • IW SLC (xarray-sentinel's S1B 2021-04-01 test product, IPF 003.31, IW1, 9 bursts of 1501 lines, 21632 samples): one range vector per burst, 542 pixels every 40 samples ending at 21631, plus one vector at the product stop time; one azimuth block over the whole sub-swath (lines 0-13508, samples 0-21631) with a value every 10 lines that follows the TOPS scalloping (about 1.16 at a burst edge).
  • Quirk: the range vectors' line is one burst early in TOPS SLC. The vector whose azimuthTime equals burst k's azimuthTime has line = first line of burst k-1 (-1501 for burst 0; the calibration vectors of the same product map time to line correctly). Bosar picks each burst's range vector by azimuth time, as SNAP does; interpolating by line would give every burst its successor's vector (a few percent of noise power, tenths of a dB near the noise floor).
  • The azimuth line list and the block bounds are image lines of the sub-swath (burst k starts at k x linesPerBurst), the same frame as the calibration LUT.
  • tests/synthetic/safe.py writes <noise/> placeholders with with_calibration=True: an unusable annotation (E205 when read; thermal_noise=auto then skips the subtraction).

docs.title: SNAP BEAM-DIMAP (data/beam_dimap.py, reader dimap) — synthetic fixtures only so far
docs.text: • Abstracted_Metadata/radar_frequency is in MHz; .img bands are big-endian ENVI.

docs.title: ISCE2 topsStack (data/isce_stack.py, reader isce) — synthetic fixtures only so far
docs.text:
• los.rdr band 0 is the incidence angle in degrees, band 1 the azimuth angle; reference/IW*.xml is needed for the wavelength and the slant-range axis.
  • Bosar's native TOPS chain (s1_coregister) writes this layout itself, with the addition DATA_TYPE = CINT16 (int16 I/Q pairs, BIP; half the bytes of CFLOAT) when asked for; the reader returns complex64 either way.
  • The stripmap chain (stripmap_coregister) writes the same layout with reference/<MODE>.xml (FBS.xml, IMS.xml, ...; the reader takes any reference/*.xml, IW* first) carrying dopplerCentroid (the JSON of the slant-range Doppler polynomial, {"r0_m", "coeffs_hz"}; absent = zero-Doppler), azimuthPixelSize, prf, lookSide, mission; orbits/<date>.json (each date's state vectors, so slc_flatten and the baselines need no project orbit file) and a coreg.json next to every SLC with that date's own centroid, offsets and refinement.

docs.title: IONEX 1.0 global ionosphere maps (data/ionex.py) - synthetic fixtures only so far
docs.text:
Read for the order-of-magnitude test of the split-spectrum ionosphere (docs/design/ionosphere.md section 4). Format description: Schaer, Gurtner & Feltens (1998), "IONEX: The IONosphere Map EXchange Format Version 1".

  • Fixed columns. Every header and map record carries its label in columns 61-80. Header records read: EPOCH OF FIRST MAP / EPOCH OF LAST MAP (6I6, UTC), INTERVAL (I6, s), # OF MAPS IN FILE, MAPPING FUNCTION (COSZ / QFAC / NONE), BASE RADIUS (F8.1, km), MAP DIMENSION (only 2 is supported: a single layer), HGT1 / HGT2 / DHGT, LAT1 / LAT2 / DLAT, LON1 / LON2 / DLON (2X,3F6.1; km, degrees), EXPONENT (I6, default -1). START OF AUX DATA ... END OF AUX DATA blocks (differential code biases) are skipped.
  • Maps. START OF TEC MAP (I6 index), EPOCH OF CURRENT MAP, then per latitude band a LAT/LON1/LON2/DLON/H record (2X,5F6.1) followed by the band's values, 16 per line (I5); END OF TEC MAP. RMS maps the same (START OF RMS MAP); height maps (3-D files) are skipped. Values are in 10**EXPONENT TECU - an EXPONENT record inside a map overrides the header's for that map; 9999 = no value (NaN). Latitudes usually run north to south (DLAT < 0); a global grid repeats -180 as +180.
  • End of day. CODE writes the last map of a daily file as hour 24 of that day (2024 12 3 24 0 0); the reader accepts hour 24. An acquisition after the last map is served by merging the next day's file (merge_maps).
  • Interpolation (IonexMaps.vtec_at): bilinear between the four nodes; between two maps linear in time with the maps rotated by 360 deg/day (the "rotated maps" of the format description: a point keeps its local solar time); NaN off the grid or next to a missing node.
  • Single layer. Shell height = HGT1 (450 km for CODE / IGS), radius = BASE RADIUS (6371 km); sin z' = R / (R + H) sin z, slant TEC = VTEC(pierce point) / cos z', the pierce point z - z' of earth-central angle from the ground point toward the sensor.
  • Files. CODE final GIMs at http://ftp.aiub.unibe.ch/CODE/YYYY/: COD0OPSFIN_YYYYDDD0000_01D_01H_GIM.INX.gz (25 hourly maps, 00:00-24:00 UTC) since GPS week 2238 (2022-11-27), CODGDDD0.YYI.Z before (code_gim_candidates). Plain and gzip files are read; Unix-compress .Z files are refused with a hint (decompress them first). The library never downloads; scripts/validate_iono_winter.py does, into its default data/aux/ionex (another folder only with --download).

docs.title: NISAR L1 RSLC (data/nisar.py, reader nisar) - real granules opened, a real pair through the stripmap chain
docs.text: One HDF5 granule -> one StripmapScene per polarisation and frequency sub-band (open_stripmap(path, polarisation="HH", frequency="A", band="L"); frequency defaults to auto - A when the granule holds it, else the frequency it holds; polarisation to the first of the frequency's listOfPolarizations; band to the band the file holds, L before S). Registered as nisar; the sniffer accepts an HDF5 file (signature at offset 0 or after a power-of-two user block of 512 B to 64 KiB) that holds /science/LSAR/RSLC/swaths (or SSAR).

docs.title: The real granules (provisional L1 RSLC, NISAR_L1_RSLC_PROVISIONAL_V1)
docs.text:
granule (cycle, track, frame, date) mode / pol code content size cycle 33, track 40, frame 50, 2026-10-14 0005 / NASV frequency B alone: VV, 5 MHz, 13680 x 6393 0.38 GB cycle 23, track 58, frame 53, 2026-06-18 0505 / SHSV frequency A: HH, 5 MHz; frequency B: VV, 5 MHz; 41040 x 6381 each 2.19 GB cycle 24, track 58, frame 53, 2026-06-30 0505 / SHSV as above (the 12-day repeat of the same frame) 2.19 GB

What the reader found in them:

  • L band, left-looking, descending (lookDirection = Left, orbitPassDirection = Descending). The track 58 / frame 53 granules hold 41040 lines x 6381 samples per frequency, at a slant-range spacing of 24.98 m (25 m range pixels; the derived range sampling rate c / (2 dr) is 6.0 MHz for the 5 MHz processed bandwidth).
  • A zero-Doppler grid with its own line rate: zeroDopplerTimeSpacing is 1/1520 s (0.658 ms) while nominalAcquisitionPRF is 1911.1 Hz - the RSLC lines are not the radar pulses. The reader takes the line interval from zeroDopplerTimeSpacing (azimuth_time_interval_s) and keeps the PRF as prf_hz.
  • The mode and polarisation codes of the file name, read from these two kinds of granule (not from a specification): two digits of processed bandwidth in MHz per frequency, A then B (0005: no frequency A, 5 MHz on B; 0505: 5 MHz on both), and two letters per frequency (NA: not acquired; SH / SV: single polarisation HH / VV).
  • The centre frequency belongs to the frequency group, not to the letter: 1221.5 MHz on frequency A and 1236.5 MHz on frequency B of the 0505 granules, 1221.5 MHz on the frequency B of the 0005 granule (24.98 m slant spacing, the same first slant range - so the stacks of frequency A and B coregistered with the same crop are cell-for-cell comparable, which the two-band ionosphere estimator of iono_split --source bands relies on). The wavelength is each scene's own (processedCenterFrequency of the frequency opened). The stripmap chain does not compare the scenes' wavelengths: pair granules of one mode (with frequency="auto", a granule that holds frequency A and one that holds frequency B alone open different sub-bands).
  • Orbit: orbitType = MOE (medium-precision) in all three.

fetch slc has no NISAR mission: the track 58 / frame 53 pair was found with asf_search and downloaded by Bosar's download loop (bosar.fetch.slc, resumable, the size and MD5 of the ASF record checked) with the Earthdata login. Two things of the ASF records were new: a NISAR record lists bytes per file of the granule (a dictionary - the HDF5's entry is the scene's size), and the scene name keeps its .h5 extension.

docs.title: The first pair through the stripmap chain
docs.text:
Track 58 / frame 53, 2026-06-18 / 2026-06-30 (12 days), frequency A HH, cropped to 69.05-69.30 N, 131.3-130.7 W (tundra, lakes and channels; 8186 lines x 957 samples after the crop), GLO-30 DEM: pipeline stripmap-coregister --reader nisar on the CPU in 308 s. Geometric offsets +556.5 lines / +1.66 samples; the amplitude refinement adds a constant of +0.35 / -0.24 px (azimuth rms 0.96 px over 258 patches - the lakes and channels decorrelate; range rms 0.03 px). B_perp 60 m. The interferogram: coherence median 0.51 (67 % of the pixels >= 0.4) at 12 days of L band in summer.

Left-looking geometry (fixed). The first interferogram showed about 28 fringes of flat-earth phase across 24 km of range (an unwrapped std of 49.8 rad): the imported stack's geometry carried no look side, so the flattening steps (slc_flatten, ifg_flatten), the stack's orbit geometry and the orbit baselines solved the ground point on the right of the track - the reader and the coregistration had the scene's side right. The stack geometry now carries the look side of its reference scene and every ground-point solution of a stack uses it. Re-flattened, the range ramp is gone (unwrapped std 5.2 rad). What remains is a smooth azimuth gradient of about 17 rad over 28 km (2.7 cycles); the ionosphere at 69 N in June or the medium-precision orbit are the candidates - not corrected.

docs.title: Reachability probe (2026-10-16, asf_search 14.0.3, metadata only, no login, nothing downloaded)
docs.text:
• asf.search(platform="NISAR", processingLevel="RSLC", maxResults=25) does return L1 RSLC products: dataset NISAR_L1_RSLC_PROVISIONAL_V1, files at https://nisar.asf.earthdatacloud.nasa.gov/NISAR/NISAR_L1_RSLC_PROVISIONAL_V1/<granule>/<granule>.h5 (the search was marked incomplete at 25, i.e. the archive holds more). platform="NISAR" alone also lists NISAR_L0B_RRSD_PROVISIONAL_V1 (L0B raw, 43 MB samples). A download needs an Earthdata login (bosar auth), as for Sentinel-1; the pair above came through Bosar's download loop that way.
  • The newest 25 RSLC granules were all of 2026-10-14, cycle 033, tracks 032 and 033, ascending and descending, frames 013-155, 0.76-30.4 GB per .h5, each with a _LATLON.png quick-look, _LATLON / _NATIVE / _NATIVE_A_<pol> KMLs, an .iso.xml, a QA report (PDF), QA stats (HDF5), a _QA_SUMMARY.csv and an .rc.yaml run configuration. Example (3.6 GB): NISAR_L1_PR_RSLC_033_033_A_045_0505_SVSH_A_20261014T114317_20261014T114401_P05023_N_F_J_001.h5. Name fields as observed: <cycle>_<track>_<A|D>_<frame>_<mode 0005|0505|2005|4005>_<pol code NASV|NADV|SVSH|DHDH>_<A|M>_<start>_<stop>_P<orbit>_N_<F|P>_J_<version> - the meaning of the mode and polarisation codes is not in a specification on disk; what the granules opened since show is in the section above.
  • A later search listed more than 600 RSLC granules, and one frame repeats every 12 days: the pair above is such a repeat.

docs.title: Layout: what was verified against which source
docs.text:
The product specification (JPL D-102274) is not on disk; the paths in the reader's docstring table were reconstructed from the open ISCE3 sources (Apache-2.0; read, nothing copied):

item source status dataset names, dtypes and units strings under RSLC/swaths/, RSLC/swaths/frequencyA/, RSLC/metadata/orbit/, metadata/processingInformation/parameters/frequencyA/, metadata/calibrationInformation/ ISCE3 writer python/packages/nisar/products/writers/SLC.py verified in source which datasets the ISCE3 swath / metadata loader reads (zeroDopplerTime, zeroDopplerTimeSpacing in the swaths group; slantRange, processedCenterFrequency, nominalAcquisitionPRF, processedRangeBandwidth, processedAzimuthBandwidth, numberOfSubSwaths, validSamplesSubSwathN in the frequency group) cxx/isce3/product/Serialization.h verified in source identification datasets (zeroDopplerStartTime, zeroDopplerEndTime, lookDirection, orbitPassDirection, absoluteOrbitNumber, listOfFrequencies, boundingPolygon, missionId, productType; bytes scalars) python/packages/nisar/products/readers/Base/Identification.py verified in source; trackNumber (uint32) and frameNumber (uint16) from the writer reference epoch of every time axis: attribute units = seconds since YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS (integer seconds) or ...:SS.fffffffff cxx/isce3/io/Serialization.h (setRefEpoch / getRefEpoch) verified in source; the reader accepts both, and a space instead of the T orbit group: time, position (meters), velocity (meters / second), orbitType (FOE / NOE / MOE / POE / Custom, default Undefined), interpMethod (Hermite / Legendre) cxx/isce3/core/Serialization.h verified in source image dtype complex32 = compound ('r', float16), ('i', float16); complex64 also possible python/packages/isce3/core/types.py; probe with h5py 3.16 (.dtype returns the compound, no c4 error; ds.astype(complex32)[window] slices lazily) verified lookDirection / orbitPassDirection spellings writer asserts Ascending / Descending; lookDirection is copied from the L0B seen on the real granules: Left, Descending; the reader compares case-insensitively the image grid is zero-Doppler (doppler = zero polynomial); the dopplerCentroid LUT under processingInformation/parameters/frequencyA/ is the raw-data Doppler used in focusing ISCE3 focusing design assumed; consistent with the real pair (the geometric coregistration from the zero-Doppler grid is within 0.35 lines of the amplitude refinement); the LUT's max SLC phase sign = ISCE's -4 pi R / lambda (Bosar's convention), no conjugation - assumed; consistent with the real pair (its flat-earth phase cancels on flattening, where the opposite sign would double it); the reader still sets extra["phase_sign_verified"] = False range sampling rate: the product has none; range_sampling_rate_hz = c / (2 slantRangeSpacing) - derivation, noted in extra["range_sampling_rate_source"] calibration_db: none - the RSLC carries linear scaleFactor / differentialDelay / differentialPhase per polarisation writer scaleFactor kept in extra["calibration_scale_factor"]

Checks the reader makes (all E205 / E204 with the HDF5 path in dataset): every required path present; zeroDopplerTime and slantRange uniform at their stated spacings (1e-6 of the step plus 16 ulp of the stored values, so a reference epoch months before the scene passes); processedCenterFrequency between 0.1 and 100 GHz; image shape equal to the axes; the orbit usable (>= 4 vectors, increasing times); the polarisation listed and present; the frequency in listOfFrequencies. Times are converted from the product's reference epochs (one per time axis) to seconds after midnight UTC of the zeroDopplerStartTime date; the orbit is rebased to the same epoch. Non-finite samples are read as 0 + 0j.

Fixture: tests/synthetic/nisar.py writes the layout above from a synthetic_scene (complex32 or complex64 images, several polarisations, frequency A or B, distinct reference epochs for the time axis and the orbit, omit= for the missing-path tests). The quirks of the real granules (frequency B alone, the line rate below the PRF, the left look side, the per-file sizes of the ASF records) are in the sections above; the fixture writes one frequency per granule, so a 0505-style granule with two frequencies at different centre frequencies exists only as real data.

docs.title: ENVISAT ASAR IMS and ERS IMS in the Envisat format (data/asar.py, readers asar / ers_envisat)
docs.text: The author's 26 products over Mexico City (track 255, descending, frame 3213; catalogue in mexico_city_esa_products.md): 20 ASA_IMS_1P...N1 (ENVISAT ASAR, IS2, VV, 2003-03-07 ... 2010-06-18) and 6 SAR_IMS_1P...E1/.E2 (ERS-1 1996-05-16, ERS-2 1996-05-17 ... 2000-03-17). All were produced by ESA's on-the-fly service in October 2026 with SOFTWARE_VER="ASAR/7.00": the ERS scenes come from the ASAR processor in the ASAR product format, so one parser serves both flavours, with a sensor table (asar.SENSORS) for the nominal constants that are only checked (W223), never substituted. The ESA specification (PO-RS-MDA-GS-2009 vol. 8) was not on disk: ISCE2's EnviSAT_SLC.py gave the MPH / SPH / DSD scheme and the first offsets of three records, the rest of the layout was reconstructed on the products (the data/asar.py module docstring lists every offset read; big-endian throughout). Opened through bosar.data.stripmap.open_stripmap as a StripmapScene; scripts/validate_asar_products.py prints the report below for a folder.

docs.title: Quirks and decisions
docs.text: # Quirk What the file says What is true / what Bosar does 1 Signed MJD days MJD fields are days, seconds, microseconds since 2000-01-01 the day is a signed i32 (-1325 for 1996-05-16); ISCE2 unpacks >3L and would date the ERS scenes in 2117. Bosar reads >iII 2 Scene height of the geolocation grid the ASAR grids' lat / lon (and the SPH corners) sit at avg_scene_height_ellpsoid = 2527.35 m (MPP offset 1541; ISCE2 reads 1537, four bytes early, as it reads the state vectors at 1761 instead of 1765) with h = 0 the ASAR tie points are 6.0 km off cross-track (6050 m on the ground = 2300 m along the line of sight at 23 deg); ERS grids and ASA 20090911 are at 0 m. tie_point_agreement and the chain's geocoding must use extra["geolocation_grid"]["height_m"] 3 ERS products labelled SWATH="IS2" SPH SWATH="IS2" on ERS too (processor label) mode="IM" from the flavour, the swath string kept in extra["swath"] 4 State vectors span exactly the frame five vectors at the first, last and three intermediate line times no margin for the geometry kernels: the reader extends them by orbit_margin_s (10 s) on both sides with two-body + J2 propagation in the Earth-fixed frame (core.orbit.extend_orbit); the model reproduces vector 4 from vector 0 (18.4 s) to 0.01-0.03 m on ASAR and 0.17-0.24 m on ERS (two-body alone: 1.5-1.8 m), and the MPH vector 20-60 s earlier to 0.01-0.35 m, which also confirms the Earth-fixed frame 5 Doppler polynomial units DOP CENTROID COEFFS ADS: origin slant_range_time in ns, five coefficients the coefficients are Hz, Hz/s, Hz/s^2, ... of tau - tau0 in seconds (c1 = -8.5e5 Hz/s on ASAR, -230 Hz across the swath); the origin is 5 samples past the first-sample time. Converted to slant range into extra["processed_doppler_centroid"]; the scene's own doppler is zero (zero-Doppler product) 6 Line timing line_time_interval float32 6.0517463e-4 s; every MDS line carries its own MJD stamp the stamps follow the interval to < 1 us over the frame; the reader takes (last - first) / (lines - 1) (double precision, consistent with both ends) and reports the ADS value in extra["line_time_interval_ads_s"]; a disagreement above the stamp resolution is W223 7 Zero-filled edges first lines and last samples hold 0 + 0j (quality_flag 0 everywhere) no-data stays 0 + 0j as the contract says; the chain's valid mask comes from the samples 8 Frame sizes vary 30 334-30 377 lines; 20090911 has 29 431 x 5160 and a 0 m grid; ERS 20000317 has 4991 samples, 19960517 29 114 lines every product carries its own geometry; nothing is assumed per track 9 Float32 constants radar frequency 5 299 999 744 Hz on ERS the product value is used as read (5e-8 relative to 5.3 GHz); the nominal table only checks it

docs.title: Geometry convention and the measured agreement
docs.text:
The products are focused to zero Doppler (ALGORITHM="RAN/DOP", lines stamped with zero-Doppler times): line row is at first_zero_doppler_time + row * dt, sample col at the two-way time of the first grid sample plus col / range_samp_rate. Acceptance test (tests/test_integration_asar_real.py, asar.tie_point_agreement): rdr2geo of all 286 tie points (13 records x first and last line x 11 samples; 264 on the two short frames) from the product state vectors, at the grid's scene height, against the tie points' own lat / lon:

products max [m] median [m] along-track mean [m] cross-track mean [m] 20 ASAR 0.35 ... 0.53 0.14 ... 0.28 -0.01 ... +0.09 -0.23 ... -0.07 6 ERS 0.90 ... 1.25 0.18 ... 0.28 0.00 ... +0.07 -0.09 ... -0.06

(2026-10-16, all 26 products; the quantisation of the vectors and of the float32 range times is ~0.1 m.) The zero-Doppler claim, the signed MJD, the 1-based lines and samples, the Earth-fixed frame and the scene height are all settled by this number; before the height was found the ASAR products were 7.4 km off.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text: calibration_db = -10 log10(K) with K = ext_cal_fact (MPP 1381). The ESA convention for single-look complex ASAR products (Rosich & Meadows 2004, ENVI-CLVL-EOPG-TN-03-0010) is sigma0 = |z|^2 / K * (R / range_ref)^3 * sin(incidence); the per-pixel range and incidence terms are the caller's (extra["calibration"] carries K and range_ref). With it the mid-image |z|^2 of 20030307 (mean |z| 66) gives -10.8 dB and that of ERS-1 19960516 (mean |z| 57) gives -15.4 dB for the same lake-bed area; the 4.6 dB gap is close to the 4.1 dB of 1 / sin 23 deg of the ERS convention (reference incidence 23 deg, Laur et al. 2004), so the ERS constant may follow the ERS formula. Not verified on a target: an open point for the data report.

docs.title: ERS caveats
docs.text:
• ERS-2 lost its gyroscopes in January 2001; scenes from 2001-01-01 on get W224 (the Doppler centroid may be ambiguities large; the annotation less reliable). All six ERS scenes on disk predate that date. ERS-2 had already switched to one-gyro piloting in February 2000, and the one scene after that switch, 2000-03-17, carries a mid-swath Doppler of -349 Hz (0.21 PRF) against -91 ... -148 Hz on the 1996-2000-01 scenes (its tie points still agree to 1.25 m): W224 follows the January 2001 rule of the task, so that scene is not flagged - check its Doppler against its pair partner before trusting the azimuth spectra (the common-band filter reads extra["processed_doppler_centroid"]["mid_swath_hz"] of both scenes).
  • The 1996 tandem pair (ERS-1 1996-05-16, ERS-2 1996-05-17, 1 day): B_perp +128 m at the scene centre from the product orbits; the two satellites share the 5.3 GHz carrier but carry different calibration constants (65 026 / 93 325).
  • Doppler centroids of -91 ... -349 Hz (ERS-2) and +133 Hz (ERS-1): the azimuth spectra of a pair are offset by up to 0.3 PRF; the common-band filter of the chain needs the processed Doppler of both scenes (extra["processed_doppler_centroid"]).
  • ESA's reprocessed ERS orbits come as DOR_VOR_AX files (the ERS products' ORBIT STATE VECTOR 1 DSD names DOR_VOR_AXVF-P1996...): the DORIS reader below serves ERS too; PRC is the legacy D-PAF format, and the one the public mirror serves for ERS (fetch orbits --mission ers, below).
